name: Tara Mingledorff
subject: Reminder: Two evenings with Congressman Moore this month
disclaimer_text: paid for by Friends of Tim Moore
body:
Dear Peter,I wanted to follow up on my recent note about Congressman Tim Moore's two events in western North Carolina later this month. Both evenings are coming together beautifully, and we would love to have you with us.This is your opportunity to visit with the Congressman, catch up with friends who have stood with him, and hear directly from him about the work ahead to keep a strong Republican majority in the House. [](https://timmoore.cmail20.com/t/y-l-fdrkylk-hkhielhuy-r/) **Reception hosted by Dr. Gregory and Mariska Berkley**
Tuesday, October 13 | 5:30 - 7:30 p.m.
623 Wilderness Road, Tryon, NC 28782
Attendee: $150 [SAVE MY SPOT IN TRYON](https://timmoore.cmail20.com/t/y-l-fdrkylk-hkhielhuy-y/) [](https://timmoore.cmail20.com/t/y-l-fdrkylk-hkhielhuy-j/) **2026 Campaign Fish Fry hosted by Maynard Bradley**
Thursday, October 15 | 5:00 - 6:30 p.m.
3253 Polkville Road, Shelby, NC 28150
Donations are appreciated but not required to attend. [PITCH IN FOR THE FISH FRY](https://timmoore.cmail20.com/t/y-l-fdrkylk-hkhielhuy-i/) The support raised at these events helps carry the Congressman's message all the way through Election Day, and it means a great deal to him to see familiar faces in the room.To RSVP, email [RSVP@CastlebarStrategies.com](mailto:RSVP@CastlebarStrategies.com) or simply reply to this message. **If you can't make it but would like to contribute, checks payable to Friends of Tim Moore may be mailed to PO Box 97275, Raleigh, NC 27624.** We hope to see you in Tryon, Shelby, or both!With gratitude,Tara Mingledorff

It's Elaine Luria, and Raja said I could reach out.

On November 8th, 2022, after a difficult, expensive, and hard-fought reelection campaign, I called my opponent to offer my concession and congratulations.
It wasn't a pleasant call to make. But I've never second-guessed the decisions that led me there.
If we haven't met: I entered the Naval Academy at 17 and spent 20 years in the Navy as a nuclear engineer, my entire career aboard combatant ships.
In 2018, I ran for Congress and flipped Virginia's 2nd District.
I'm also a mom, which is still the best job I've ever had.
In Congress, I served on the January 6th Committee, knowing full well it could cost me my seat. That cycle, outside far-right groups spent $6,059,677 against me. Add a national environment that was brutal for frontline Democrats, and I came up short.
_**For me, the worst outcome isn’t losing a fight. It’s going down with no fight at all.**_
So I'm back, running to win this seat back from Jen Kiggans, because I can't sit on the sidelines and watch our country descend into chaos.
The Cook Political Report rates VA-02 a Toss-Up. This is one of Democrats’ best pickup opportunities in the country.
Republicans know it too. Jen Kiggans called Elon Musk's DOGE cuts "so necessary," even as they hit Hampton Roads hard. Now Musk's super PAC has started spending to keep her in office and beat me.
That's why September 30th matters. It's my last end-of-quarter FEC deadline before Election Day, and the report that follows is public. Reporters, national groups, and Kiggans' allies will all read it to decide how seriously to take this race.

That quote, from Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson, is from the dissent where she said the Court was wrong to allow President Trump to overhaul the U.S. Department of Homeland Security’s (DHS) Systematic Alien Verification for Entitlement (SAVE) system to initiate voter registration purges. The Supreme Court's "shadow docket" emergency decision in this case came after A district judge found earlier this year that the database “ _trampled on the privacy rights of American citizens in a manner that threatens the sacred right to vote_.”

**You've heard us say it before:** Claims of noncitizen voting and wide-scale fraud are blatant lies. **Every disenfranchised voter is an eligible citizen suppressed**. We have so little time left before ballots are cast to inform voters, get them to check their registrations, verify they can still vote, and make their voice heard in whatever way they can. Central Banks Are Choosing to Move Away From the Dollar. The IMF Just Confirmed It Wasn’t an Accident.
The dollar’s share of world reserves fell to 56.7%, close to its lowest this century. The IMF says currency swings didn’t cause it. Central banks made a choice. Every monetary era has an anchor, and this one is moving.

In 2001, more than 70 cents of every dollar's worth of foreign reserves held by the world’s central banks sat in U.S. dollars. Today it’s under 57 cents. That slide happened slowly enough that most Americans never noticed. But the newest data shows something that should get their attention: central banks aren’t just drifting away from the dollar anymore. They’re actively choosing to.
The evidence board
| | What the Latest Data Shows
---|---
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit A — the share.** IMF data released on September 30 shows the dollar at 56.70% of global allocated reserves at the end of June 2026, down from 57.18% three months earlier. The low this century, 56.32%, came in mid-2025.
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit B — it’s deliberate.** The IMF noted that exchange rates moved within about 2% during the quarter, so “valuation effects were limited.” In other words, the dollar’s share fell because central banks bought other things, not because currency prices moved. The euro’s share rose from 20.04% to 20.60%.
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit C — the long slide.** From about 72% in 2001 to under 57% today: roughly 15 percentage points of the world’s reserves have moved away from the dollar in 25 years, with the decline accelerating since Russia’s reserves were frozen in 2022.

---|---
| | 1944

| | 1971–74

Oil

| | NOW
---
Up for grabs
As oil’s grip loosens and reserves diversify, Washington is pouring money and policy into the strategic assets it thinks will matter most next.

Currency swings didn’t cause the change.

**Our theory:** this sentence matters more than the headline number. In past quarters, the dollar’s share often moved simply because the dollar rose or fell in value. This time it didn’t. Central banks made a choice. When the world’s most cautious investors deliberately rebalance away from your currency, it’s a sign the anchor holding the system together is shifting.

| | LOSING

[ ](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/140911390/651921931/-1473932214?refcode=logo&amount=10&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS83MjY1OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJiNDBjN2RhOC1hY2MyLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E0ZmJlODMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=LumlbFRwXFPGBv9aDHD149jNNwxfEZEEC9xwRqFCzis=) I'll be honest, folks. I never saw myself serving in the U.S. Senate.

This is a longer email about my story and how I came to fight for hardworking Coloradans in the Senate, and I hope you’ll read it until the end. **[But if you don’t have time, please, take a moment and chip in a couple bucks to my campaign. →](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/140911391/651921932/1681514997?refcode=email_100726_bio-RS&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS83MjY1OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJiNDBjN2RhOC1hY2MyLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E0ZmJlODMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=LumlbFRwXFPGBv9aDHD149jNNwxfEZEEC9xwRqFCzis=)** | | [Donate →](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/140911392/651921933/1681514997?refcode=email_100726_bio-RS&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS83MjY1OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJiNDBjN2RhOC1hY2MyLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E0ZmJlODMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=LumlbFRwXFPGBv9aDHD149jNNwxfEZEEC9xwRqFCzis=)

Back in the mid-1980s, I was a geologist — until I wasn’t. Our company got sold, and we all got laid off. I used part of my severance to buy an old Chevy convertible, and drove to visit my brother in Berkeley, CA. He showed me one of the first brewpubs in America, and I loved it. I came back to Denver and took a gamble, risking every scrap of my savings in opening the Wynkoop Brewing Company in downtown Denver.
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/140911393/651921934/1681514997?refcode=email_100726_bio-RS&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS83MjY1OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJiNDBjN2RhOC1hY2MyLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E0ZmJlODMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=LumlbFRwXFPGBv9aDHD149jNNwxfEZEEC9xwRqFCzis=)
I remember working 80-hour weeks. I remember lying awake at night, wondering how we were going to make it. And I remember being so frustrated that our government was focusing more on decisions that’d help politicians get reelected rather than helping solve our problems.

So I ran for Mayor. To everyone’s surprise, especially mine, I won in a landslide. From then on, I focused every day on making decisions based on what was best for Denver.

I then became the first Denver Mayor in 120 years to be elected Governor, on the premise of uniting people and getting things done. We expanded health care to half a million people and created the first methane regulations in any state or country in the world.

And after we flipped Colorado’s Senate seat in 2020, we worked to deliver real change for Coloradans. We invested billions of dollars to confront the climate crisis, lowered prescription drug costs, made investments to rebuild our infrastructure, and brought thousands of good-paying manufacturing jobs back to America.

Now, we’re in the fight of our lives as Trump’s extreme agenda threatens to undo all that work. We refused to let him auction off our public lands or use your tax dollars to give handouts to felons like Tina Peters.
But look, I’ve also seen how broken Washington is – and how Trump has unleashed corruption like a pandemic. I see politicians who only listen to those who cut big campaign checks while ignoring families trying to afford health care. I’ve seen how Trump operates: money comes in, favors go out.

Here's why I'm telling you this: **what drives our work is the people of Colorado.**

The families who are struggling to maintain their health insurance after Trump gutted the Affordable Care Act to give tax cuts to his friends in the Epstein class. The workers who are working full-time and still need a second job to afford their rent. The kids who are studying science and are already worried that the funding for their research will never come back.
As I said, I never thought I’d find myself in the U.S. Senate, but I’m running for reelection because it’s been the honor of a lifetime to fight for you. And too much is at stake to stop now.

That’s why I don't take money from corporate PACs like your typical politician. Instead, I rely on grassroots folks like you. And it’s why I'm depending on your contribution today to help us defend Colorado this November. Even just $5 here or $10 there goes a long way in a campaign like ours.
**[So I have to ask: will you make a donation of whatever is meaningful to you? Together, we can defend this seat we flipped back in 2020 and keep power in the hands of Coloradans:](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/140911394/651921935/1681514997?refcode=email_100726_bio-RS&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS83MjY1OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJiNDBjN2RhOC1hY2MyLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E0ZmJlODMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=LumlbFRwXFPGBv9aDHD149jNNwxfEZEEC9xwRqFCzis=)**

That’s why, if you [**chip in $7, or any amount, to the DNC today,**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-warren-sweepstakes-2026?refcode=em_20261007_9725_fr&amount=7&refcode2=9725_22930333__-fXOg&akid=9725%2E22930333%2E_-fXOg) you’ll be entered to win a trip, travel, and hotel included, to meet me in Boston or DC.

clean_body: My job between now and November is to make sure every one of them hears it. Help me get the word out across this state. | Fellow Conservative, I have been crisscrossing South Dakota, from one end to the other, and I want to tell you what I am hearing. At the gas stations, the diners, and the county fairs, folks keep telling me a version of the same thing. They are worried. Worried about the cost of living, worried about the direction of the country, and worried that the radical left is closer to real power than it has ever been. And here is what almost none of them know yet. A fake independent, a man who ran as a Democrat just two years ago, is quietly working to flip our Senate seat and hand Chuck Schumer his majority. My job between now and November is to make sure every one of them hears it. That takes gas in the tank, ads on the air, and boots on the ground. | I will keep showing up, in every town that will have me. Thank you for having my back. You don't spend six figures against a campaign you're already beating.

body:
Poll after poll shows me tied with Susan Collins, and she’s spending double what we are on TV ads. We need to pick up the pace if we want any shot at flipping this seat and retaking the Senate majority for Democrats.
#
Peter, here’s the deal.
Susan Collins really knows how to put on a show in the Senate.
She votes with Trump 96% of the time. If she knows one of his bad bills is going to tank, she’ll vote against it. If she’s the deciding vote, she’ll always vote for it, just like how she was the deciding vote for Brett Kavanaugh, who then overturned _Roe v. Wade._
The same is also true with Trump’s tariffs. Mainers and folks across the country are hurting badly from rising costs – and too many families are having to pick between picking up their prescriptions or putting food on the table.
So when she said during our debate that she brought down the cost of road salt, **I had to say what shouldn’t need to be said:**
[](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/109729?refcode=em20261007-10995&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1&akid=10995%2E614464%2EZFc9Co)
It goes to show just how out of touch Susan is with families across Maine. Road salt isn’t going to make groceries, heating oil, or everyday necessities affordable again.
Susan Collins is so used to putting the needs of billionaires over her constituents. I’m running to defeat her because folks across Maine have made me into the public servant I am today, and they deserve a Senator who isn’t afraid to take on tough battles.
**But poll after poll shows me tied with Susan Collins, and she’s spending double what we are on TV ads. We need to pick up the pace if we want any shot at flipping this seat and retaking the Senate majority for Democrats.**
**[So Peter, will you please split $15 – or more, if you can spare it – between my campaign and State Democrats Committee right now? Alright, that’s enough campaign talk. Let’s get to know each other, Derek.
My story is Wisconsin’s story. I was born and raised in Milwaukee in a union household. My father was a master electrician and my mother worked in the service industry. Just like so many families in Wisconsin, they worked hard. But also like many families, they struggled with addiction and mental health issues.
Growing up, I watched my family fight every single day just to get by. I learned that when systems fail, families pay the price. **But I also learned that grit, resilience, and hope for a better tomorrow can carry us through even the toughest challenges.**
To me, these challenges aren’t just policy issues. They’re lived experiences. My wife, Ericka, and I are raising three daughters in Milwaukee, which keeps me focused on what policy really means at the kitchen table, not just in Madison.
As Milwaukee County Executive and as a State Assemblyman before that, I’ve also seen first-hand how good government can actually improve people’s lives. I believe that when we commit to putting working families first and bringing the basics back within reach, we create communities where every Wisconsinite can thrive. **Derek, I promise you that’s not just a nice campaign slogan – it’s how I govern.**
But if you’ll forgive a little more campaign talk, the same can’t be said for Tom Tiffany.
Tiffany cares about making Wisconsin better for billionaires like Elon Musk and the Uihlein family, _NOT_ for everyday folks like you and me.
Tiffany’s priority is advancing Trump’s MAGA agenda in our state, _NOT_ creating good government that lifts people up and helps them thrive.

_You're getting this message because you’ve supported good causes and Democratic candidates. We need your support to continue fighting for our democracy. We love having you in our network, but if you only want our most important email updates,[click here.](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/108?t=2&akid=3398%2E259176%2EVC8UhO) If you'd like to unsubscribe, [click here.](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/109?t=3&akid=3398%2E259176%2EVC8UhO)_

Did you watch the Nebraska State Fair debate?

The panel got to campaign finance — how our elections get paid for.

**I told the truth:** unlimited money from billionaires, corporations, and shadowy outside groups are warping this country’s politics, _and it started with a Supreme Court decision called Citizens United._

I want it overturned. I have said that in every county I’ve been to, and I said it again with the cameras rolling.

**Then I looked over at the man standing next to me.** [](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/18018?source=SL_EM_FR_2026.10.07_Osborn-Citizens-United_B4_F1_S2_C1_180AC-360DON_T2&t=4&akid=3398%2E259176%2EVC8UhO) My opponent, Pete Ricketts, raised $6.3 million in one quarter this year. **$5.2 million of it came from his own bank account.**

Think about that for a second.

He is the heir to a fortune. He can write his campaign a check bigger than most Nebraska towns will see in a lifetime, and then go to Washington owing nothing to the people who live here.

_I think that’s totally wrong._

I’m an industrial mechanic. I’ve spent my life in boiler rooms and on picket lines. The only reason I’m on a ballot at all is that tens of thousands of regular people decided to put a few bucks behind a guy like them.

That is exactly the point I was trying to make on that stage. This isn’t left versus right. It’s whether working people still get a say, or whether the folks who can afford to buy the microphone get to do all the talking. **Vote FOR Prop. A in Houston -- the Houston Freedom Act** ** ** TOP is proud to join our allies at Ground Game Texas in engaging voters across Houston to [vote FOR Proposition A (the Houston Freedom Act)](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/140912854/651962589/524068781?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9UU00vVFNNVE8vMS80NTY0MCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJhYjE4MWQxZi1iYWMyLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E0ZmJlODMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=a2cSjtZpXyVjZrIj9x5Wg5ZNQxa4R_zL-w2Ce9p7baw=&emci=32705632-b1c2-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbe83&emdi=ab181d1f-bac2-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbe83&ceid=227997) in this year’s midterm election. The Houston Freedom Act would make enforcement of Class A and B misdemeanor cannabis possession Houston’s lowest law-enforcement priority, expand diversion, require greater transparency around enforcement, and prohibit Houston police participation in no-knock raids. The measure reached the ballot after Ground Game Texas organizers collected and submitted approximately 40,000 signatures from Houston residents. [Houstonians: Learn more about Prop. A and how it will appear on your ballot!](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/140912855/651962590/524068781?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9UU00vVFNNVE8vMS80NTY0MCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJhYjE4MWQxZi1iYWMyLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E0ZmJlODMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=a2cSjtZpXyVjZrIj9x5Wg5ZNQxa4R_zL-w2Ce9p7baw=&emci=32705632-b1c2-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbe83&emdi=ab181d1f-bac2-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbe83&ceid=227997)

**Hosting a Fort Worth conversation on the intersection of Black women's health and voting** We thank the Fort Worth Association of Federated Women's Clubs and all in the community who joined us at last night's #RootedInCare conversation. Put on by [BlackTOP,](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/140912856/651962591/-54181795?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9UU00vVFNNVE8vMS80NTY0MCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJhYjE4MWQxZi1iYWMyLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E0ZmJlODMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=a2cSjtZpXyVjZrIj9x5Wg5ZNQxa4R_zL-w2Ce9p7baw=&emci=32705632-b1c2-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbe83&emdi=ab181d1f-bac2-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbe83&ceid=227997) the discussion covered how electoral politics intersects with Black women’s health in Texas. Healthcare is a key issue for Black Texans heading into this year's midterm election, especially Black women, as federal budget cuts under the Trump administration have reduced access to low-cost healthcare for families, as well as essential food programs for working-class households.

**End Non-Safety Traffic Stops + Mass Surveillance in Texas** Every day, thousands of Texans are pulled over for minor, non-safety issues. **These stops draw working people into unnecessary police contact with zero public safety benefit.** At the same time, Automated License Plate Readers (ALPRs), like Flock Safety, are expanding across our state. They create massive tracking databases that monitor where you drive, work, worship, and seek medical care. 👉🏾 **Sign the petition:[Tell Texas officials to end non-safety traffic stops and Flock surveillance.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/140912857/651962592/-731476291?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9UU00vVFNNVE8vMS80NTY0MCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJhYjE4MWQxZi1iYWMyLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E0ZmJlODMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=a2cSjtZpXyVjZrIj9x5Wg5ZNQxa4R_zL-w2Ce9p7baw=&emci=32705632-b1c2-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbe83&emdi=ab181d1f-bac2-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbe83&ceid=227997)** **TOP Tip: Check if you're eligible to vote by mail this midterm**
The voter registration deadline in Texas has passed, but if you know you will be away from the state at the time of early vote and on Election Day, you _**might**_ be eligible to vote by mail this midterm. [_**Learn more here to see if you qualify.**_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/140912858/651962593/-1482168202?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9UU00vVFNNVE8vMS80NTY0MCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJhYjE4MWQxZi1iYWMyLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E0ZmJlODMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=a2cSjtZpXyVjZrIj9x5Wg5ZNQxa4R_zL-w2Ce9p7baw=&emci=32705632-b1c2-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbe83&emdi=ab181d1f-bac2-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbe83&ceid=227997)

**Español** **Vote A FAVOR de la Propuesta A en Houston: la Ley de Libertad de Houston** TOP se enorgullece de unirse a sus aliados de Ground Game Texas para movilizar a los votantes de todo Houston a [favor de la Propuesta A (la Ley de Libertad de Houston o *Houston Freedom Act*)](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/140912859/651962594/524068781?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9UU00vVFNNVE8vMS80NTY0MCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJhYjE4MWQxZi1iYWMyLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E0ZmJlODMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=a2cSjtZpXyVjZrIj9x5Wg5ZNQxa4R_zL-w2Ce9p7baw=&emci=32705632-b1c2-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbe83&emdi=ab181d1f-bac2-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbe83&ceid=227997) en las elecciones de mitad de mandato de este año. La Ley de Libertad de Houston convertiría la aplicación de la ley respecto a la posesión de marihuana —clasificada como delito menor de clase A o B— en la prioridad más baja para las fuerzas del orden de la ciudad; asimismo, ampliaría los programas de desvío penal, exigiría mayor transparencia en las actuaciones policiales y prohibiría la participación de la policía de Houston en redadas sin previo aviso (*no-knock raids*). La medida llegó a la boleta electoral después de que los organizadores de Ground Game Texas recopilaran y presentaran aproximadamente 40.000 firmas de residentes de Houston. [Habitantes de Houston: ¡Infórmense más sobre la Propuesta A y cómo aparecerá en su boleta electoral!](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/140912860/651962595/524068781?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9UU00vVFNNVE8vMS80NTY0MCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJhYjE4MWQxZi1iYWMyLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E0ZmJlODMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=a2cSjtZpXyVjZrIj9x5Wg5ZNQxa4R_zL-w2Ce9p7baw=&emci=32705632-b1c2-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbe83&emdi=ab181d1f-bac2-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbe83&ceid=227997) **Organizar una convención en Fort Worth sobre la intersección entre la salud de las mujeres negras y el voto** Women's Clubs y a todos los miembros de la comunidad que nos acompañaron anoche en la conversación #RootedInCare. Organizado por [BlackTOP](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/140912861/651962596/-54181795?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9UU00vVFNNVE8vMS80NTY0MCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJhYjE4MWQxZi1iYWMyLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E0ZmJlODMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=a2cSjtZpXyVjZrIj9x5Wg5ZNQxa4R_zL-w2Ce9p7baw=&emci=32705632-b1c2-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbe83&emdi=ab181d1f-bac2-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbe83&ceid=227997), el coloquio abordó cómo la política electoral se cruza con la salud de las mujeres negras en Texas. La atención médica es un tema clave para los texanos negros de cara a las elecciones de mitad de mandato de este año —especialmente para las mujeres negras—, ya que los recortes presupuestarios federales de la administración Trump han reducido el acceso a servicios de salud de bajo costo para las familias, así como a programas alimentarios esenciales para los hogares de clase trabajadora. **Poner fin a las paradas de tráfico no relacionadas con la seguridad y a la vigilancia masiva en Texas** Cada día, miles de tejanos son detenidos por infracciones menores que no comprometen la seguridad. **Estas intervenciones obligan a personas trabajadoras a tener contactos innecesarios con la policía, sin aportar ningún beneficio a la seguridad pública.** Al mismo tiempo, los sistemas automatizados de lectura de matrículas (ALPR), como Flock Safety, se están extendiendo por todo el estado. Estos sistemas crean enormes bases de datos que rastrean dónde conduces, trabajas, acudes a servicios religiosos y recibes atención médica. 👉🏾 **Firma la petición:[Exige a las autoridades de Texas que pongan fin a las paradas de tráfico no relacionadas con la seguridad y a la vigilancia mediante sistemas como Flock.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/140912862/651962597/-731476291?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9UU00vVFNNVE8vMS80NTY0MCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJhYjE4MWQxZi1iYWMyLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E0ZmJlODMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=a2cSjtZpXyVjZrIj9x5Wg5ZNQxa4R_zL-w2Ce9p7baw=&emci=32705632-b1c2-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbe83&emdi=ab181d1f-bac2-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbe83&ceid=227997)** **Consejos de TOP: Verifique si reúne los requisitos para votar por correo en estas elecciones ** El plazo para registrarse como votante en Texas ya ha vencido; sin embargo, si sabe que estará fuera del estado durante el periodo de votación anticipada y el día de las elecciones, _**es posible**_ que reúna los requisitos para votar por correo en estas elecciones de mitad de mandato. [_**Obtenga más información aquí para saber si cumple con los requisitos.**_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/140912863/651962598/-1482168202?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9UU00vVFNNVE8vMS80NTY0MCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJhYjE4MWQxZi1iYWMyLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E0ZmJlODMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=a2cSjtZpXyVjZrIj9x5Wg5ZNQxa4R_zL-w2Ce9p7baw=&emci=32705632-b1c2-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbe83&emdi=ab181d1f-bac2-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbe83&ceid=227997)

| **A NOTE FROM KELLY**
---
| Hello friends,It’s Kelly here this week. With early voting now underway, there’s something I want you to know about the man on your ballot.Eric and I have built our lives in Wyoming, raised our family here, worked here, and served here. Through those years, I’ve watched him show up for our schools and communities, listen to people, and follow through on his word.He believes every Wyoming kid, whether they’re in one of our bigger towns or in an unincorporated sweet spot in the road, deserves a great teacher, a safe classroom, and an education built on Wyoming values. He believes parents and local communities should be the ones making those decisions.Spending time with students, teachers, and parents this past week brought those commitments home. Our young people have questions and ideas of their own, and they deserve to be heard. We want them to have a good education and opportunities to build their lives here.That connects to so much of what we saw throughout the week. People in energy and manufacturing are finding new ways to put Wyoming’s resources and experience to work. State and local government agencies working to keep our communities safe and running efficiently. Small business owners creating jobs and places where neighbors gather. Over coffee and in town halls, we heard from folks who care about where Wyoming is headed and want to help.Eric is a man of his word. I know that from our life together and from watching him serve Wyoming. He takes people’s concerns seriously and understands that the work continues long after the visit is over.Thank you for welcoming us, sharing your questions and giving us so much to take home from these conversations.Early voting is now open, October 6 - November 2. Check with your county clerk’s office to find your voting location. If you can, go this week and take a neighbor with you.Kelly

| **On The Trail**
---
| | | | |
---
| | |
---
| | | | |
---
| **CHEYENNE** Kelly and I had a great evening in Cheyenne at Vintages Handcrafted Wine. Lots of folks showed up with questions about property taxes, the work of the Healthcare Task Force, and the challenges facing rural health care in Wyoming.Kelly introduced her plans as First Lady for a platform on service called SITE - Service In The Everyday.Thank you to Vintages and Tammy Kennedy for hosting us, and to everyone who joined the discussion and shared their thoughts.
---
| |
---
|
---
| |
---
| | | **CHEYENNE** Kelly and I spent an afternoon visiting with members of the Wyoming Young Republicans. It’s encouraging to see young people getting involved in the political process, asking thoughtful questions and making their voices heard. The decisions we make today will have a lasting impact on their generation, and their involvement matters
---
| | |
---
|
---
| | | | |
---
| **ROCK SPRINGS** Kelly and I had a great day in Rock Springs, starting with a meet and greet at Pin Up Coffee and catching up with folks over good conversation. We also attended a fun Cowboys watch party. The game didn’t go our way, but we still cut a rug and enjoyed seeing so many friends and fans!We finished the evening with supporters who are excited and ready to help bring this campaign to a successful finish in November. Thank you to everyone who spent part of the day with us!
---
| | | | |
---
| | |
---
| |
---
|
---
| | | **MOUNTAIN VIEW** We stopped for a visit at the Mountain View Town Hall, where folks took time on homecoming evening to talk about the issues affecting their communities. Our youngest attendee helped open and close a thoughtful discussion covering property taxes, climate change, mental health, carbon capture, education, firefighting needs, and plenty more.Thank you to Senator Wendy Schuler, Jon Conrad, and everyone who joined us for another great day in Uinta County!
---
| | |
---
| | | | |
---
| | |
---
|
---
| | | | |
---
| **LYMAN** Kelly and I enjoyed stopping at the Lyman Soda Station for drinks, cookies, and good conversation. We sampled the lime raspberry cookie and the cream-filled pumpkin snickerdoodle fall special - both were quite a treat! It was also great to catch up with my former colleague Allen Jaggi before heading down the road.
---
|
---
| | | **EVANSTON** The team at Black Mesa Advanced Fission is working to bring new manufacturing opportunities to Wyoming by putting our state’s talent and resources to work. It was great to hear their vision for strengthening our nation’s security with Wyoming uranium and expertise.
---
| | |
---
| | | | |
---
| | |
---
|
---
| | | | |
---
| **EVANSTON** We made a quick stop at GiGi’s Coffee House in Evanston for a pick-me-up after an early morning in Gillette. It was great to say hello to owners Gina Jones and Gina Black, along with a few supporters and interested voters!
---
|
---
| | | **DOUGLAS** Kelly and I joined local and county leaders, landowners and neighbors in Douglas for a dinner hosted by Occidental Petroleum (Oxy) to thank the community for its work and partnership.It was great chance to visit and hear about local developments.Thank you to Nate Reardon, Bobby Rolston and the Oxy team for hosting, and to everyone who took time to be there.
---
| | |
---
|
---
| | | **DOUGLAS** Kelly and I appreciated the chance to meet up with Douglas teachers, students, and parents during an after-school gathering at the LaBonte Hotel.We answered questions, shared a few funny moments from our time on the road, and Kelly talked about her initiative, SITE - Service In The Everyday - and how small acts of service can make a difference in communities across Wyoming.We’re grateful to Rhonda Dilts and her crew for organizing the event and putting together some great door prizes. A special thank you to Macey and Keith Moore for welcoming us into such a nice space and providing popcorn for everyone to enjoy.Thank you to all the students, families, and educators who stopped by!
---
| | |
---
| | | | |
---
| | |
---
|
---
| | | MILLSThank you to the DISA team for welcoming me to Mills. I joined a tour with global investors interested in technology being developed here in Wyoming to advance our uranium and rare earth markets.In August, DISA became two Wyoming companies, DISA Technologies and DISA Uranium, to better serve the energy industry. Together, they have raised more than $183 million.Wyoming has generations of experience in mining and energy, and people finding new ways to put that knowledge to work.
---
| | |
---
|
---
| | | | |
---
| **RAWLINS** Kelly and I had a wonderful evening visiting with community members at the Rawlins City Old Depot.We’re grateful to Tara and Copper France and Scott and Pam Thayer for organizing the gathering and giving us the chance to hear from so many folks. A special thank you to Aspen House, Totally Toasty Toad and Gem Cookie for providing the food and goodies for this event!Thank you to everyone who stopped by and shared part of their evening with us.
---
|
---
| | | | |
---
| **RAWLINS** Kelly and I appreciated the opportunity to tour the Wyoming State Penitentiary and learn more about the work of the Department of Corrections.We saw new cameras and technology upgrades that are helping improve inmate safety and employee satisfaction. We also learned about strategies to reduce recidivism and the treatment services available to offenders while they are incarcerated. Public safety and rehabilitation are both important to building stronger communities across Wyoming.The programs also give inmates opportunities to develop practical and creative skills.Thank you to the staff who took time to show us around and share their work. We appreciate their commitment to safety, rehabilitation and service to Wyoming.

We sampled the lime raspberry cookie and the cream-filled pumpkin snickerdoodle fall special - both were quite a treat! It was also great to catch up with my former colleague Allen Jaggi before heading down the road. | | | | EVANSTON The team at Black Mesa Advanced Fission is working to bring new manufacturing opportunities to Wyoming by putting our state’s talent and resources to work. It was great to hear their vision for strengthening our nation’s security with Wyoming uranium and expertise. | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | EVANSTON We made a quick stop at GiGi’s Coffee House in Evanston for a pick-me-up after an early morning in Gillette. It was great to say hello to owners Gina Jones and Gina Black, along with a few supporters and interested voters! | | | | DOUGLAS Kelly and I joined local and county leaders, landowners and neighbors in Douglas for a dinner hosted by Occidental Petroleum (Oxy) to thank the community for its work and partnership.It was great chance to visit and hear about local developments.Thank you to Nate Reardon, Bobby Rolston and the Oxy team for hosting, and to everyone who took time to be there. | | | | | | | DOUGLAS Kelly and I appreciated the chance to meet up with Douglas teachers, students, and parents during an after-school gathering at the LaBonte Hotel.We answered questions, shared a few funny moments from our time on the road, and Kelly talked about her initiative, SITE - Service In The Everyday - and how small acts of service can make a difference in communities across Wyoming.We’re grateful to Rhonda Dilts and her crew for organizing the event and putting together some great door prizes. A special thank you to Macey and Keith Moore for welcoming us into such a nice space and providing popcorn for everyone to enjoy.Thank you to all the students, families, and educators who stopped by! | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | MILLSThank you to the DISA team for welcoming me to Mills. I joined a tour with global investors interested in technology being developed here in Wyoming to advance our uranium and rare earth markets.In August, DISA became two Wyoming companies, DISA Technologies and DISA Uranium, to better serve the energy industry. Together, they have raised more than $183 million.Wyoming has generations of experience in mining and energy, and people finding new ways to put that knowledge to work. | | | | | | | | | | RAWLINS Kelly and I had a wonderful evening visiting with community members at the Rawlins City Old Depot.We’re grateful to Tara and Copper France and Scott and Pam Thayer for organizing the gathering and giving us the chance to hear from so many folks. A special thank you to Aspen House, Totally Toasty Toad and Gem Cookie for providing the food and goodies for this event!Thank you to everyone who stopped by and shared part of their evening with us. | | | | | | | RAWLINS Kelly and I appreciated the opportunity to tour the Wyoming State Penitentiary and learn more about the work of the Department of Corrections.We saw new cameras and technology upgrades that are helping improve inmate safety and employee satisfaction. We also learned about strategies to reduce recidivism and the treatment services available to offenders while they are incarcerated. Public safety and rehabilitation are both important to building stronger communities across Wyoming.The programs also give inmates opportunities to develop practical and creative skills.Thank you to the staff who took time to show us around and share their work. We appreciate their commitment to safety, rehabilitation and service to Wyoming. | | | Wyoming’s strength has always come from neighbors pitching in. Peter,

Last night, David Valadao finally had to answer for his vote to gut Medicaid, after promising us he wouldn't. I want to walk you through his response and a few more, because every voter in this district deserves to hear them.

**Medicaid Vote**
Valadao didn't back away from his vote to gut Medicaid. He doubled down and said he was "excited" about the bill that rips healthcare away from over 70,000 CA-22 residents -- all so his corporate donors can get another tax break.

**The Iran War**
When asked about the war with Iran, which he voted to continue six times, the best Valadao could offer was that it's "only temporary" until Iran's nuclear threat is eliminated and the Strait of Hormuz is reopened. He left out that the Strait was open before Trump launched this war in the first place. Not to mention Trump and Hegseth have zero plan to end it while gas prices continue to skyrocket.

**ICE Raids in the Central Valley**
The answer I can't stop thinking about came when he was asked about the chaotic, warrantless ICE raids terrorizing local farmers and families across the Central Valley, all he could muster was: "it is what it is."

subject: We won tonight's debate. Here's why.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Eric Jones for Congress
body:
| [](https://us.list-manage.com/w4ZIzMqeMqe?e=2ce0ad0449&c2id=45350b27067c85fdcb9eb8e5b2087927)
---
**We won tonight’s debate, and I’m fired up.** Tonight, voters finally got the chance to see the two candidates seeking to represent this district — side by side.You can see the difference for yourself.It’s clear we need new leadership in Congress — fresh energy and new ideas. Someone who fights for you, not the corporate PACs and special interests that built the careers of today’s lifetime politicians.**My commitment to you: I’ll never take a dollar from any corporate PAC, lobbyist, or special interest. I will always answer to you and you alone.** Voters deserve answers to hard questions. Lifetime politicians survive by avoiding accountability. In July, I asked Congressman Thompson for 9 live debates across the district. Tonight, we only got 25 minutes, and it’s obvious why he wouldn’t give us more.25 minutes may have been enough to see the difference between us, but it wasn’t nearly enough time for a real discussion about the issues that matter. name: Chris Pappas
subject: You have to listen first
body:
[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/126?t=1001&akid=9399%2E582294%2EH5Bp3D ]Chris Pappas for Senate[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/126?t=1002&akid=9399%2E582294%2EH5Bp3D ]Chris Pappas for Senate

Hi, it’s
Chris.

Before I ever knocked on a door for a campaign, I spent my time bussing
tables for my family’s restaurant in Manchester.

I didn’t know it then, but it’s where I learned the most important thing
about public service: You have to show up and listen.

People from all walks of life came through those doors. Neighbors who had
lived in town for decades or folks who just moved to New Hampshire. It
didn’t matter which side of the political aisle they were on. What
mattered was whether you showed up, said hello, and treated people right.

That’s the same way I run this campaign — showing up, listening, and
making sure that I hear directly from Granite Staters about what’s on
their minds.

We need a
Senator who’s fighting for New Hampshire, not special interests.

But time is running out. Outside groups are pouring millions of dollars
into this race, and I need people like you to step up right now. Election
Day is just around the corner, and there’s no time left to waste.

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20261008_1.N5KPMX&refcode=em20261008-1&t=1003&akid=9399%2E582294%2EH5Bp3D ]That’s why I’m asking: Will you make a donation to our campaign today?
Pitching in $5 or $10 right now will help
make sure we have the resources to win on November 3rd.

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20261008_1.N5KPMX&amount=5&refcode=em20261008-1&t=1022&akid=9399%2E582294%2EH5Bp3D ]Donate $5 »

Thank you,

Chris Pappas

GOD'S CHILDREN ARE NOT FOR SALE

Friend,

I want to start with two simple words.

Thank you.

Thank you for caring about children you may never meet.

Thank you for believing that every child has value and for refusing to accept a world where innocent children can be bought and sold.

Because that is exactly what is happening.

Every day.

https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABl7ImQiOjUwMjMsInQiOjc2NywicyI6MTJ9AAwAAAAAA2Vk0nrOjt6uMAsYu8ZxWfzlQo6uZMBcc8OA-4BLqBRy0nBYxV7Uh2H7TUxkcNJnxnIfQlAUr4yW7R2cfUwruw9WRhf_NCOEc3Hyrhy0wA

God's children are not for sale.

And today, I'd like to send you a shirt that boldly declares that truth.

When you make your first gift to the Sound of Freedom Foundation today, we'll send you a FREE white "God's Children Are Not For Sale" t-shirt as our thank-you.

https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABl7ImQiOjUwMjMsInQiOjc2NywicyI6MTJ9AAwAAAAAA2Vk0nrQPSb6luGprxGvC0PYVgylcJXuPb1tz-fSXp7xYkwDY81PRr_yLVruhODTzYUbbh8HEMY2cjCHsVKQCsuLQBwbVTOPlEt-YSISsQ

https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABl7ImQiOjUwMjMsInQiOjc2NywicyI6MTJ9AAwAAAAAA2Vk0nrSW1MD-5j6GK79S1aO46VU4H7GQKT-QOaiE2e1Dtnd9mLhWjVPdwcC9_KSiIPWv2XwxUmd2J6l1m_xlBDORBJYZV1BJ3BfjHBD-w

This isn't a shirt you'll find in a store.

You can't buy it online.

It was created exclusively for supporters of the Sound of Freedom Foundation.

People who believe children deserve safety, refuse to look away and are willing to stand up and say:

"No more."

Every time you wear it, you'll be sharing a message that matters.

A message that reminds the world that every child has God-given dignity.

And importantly, a message that sparks conversations and helps raise awareness about a crisis many people still do not see.

Most of all Friend, I hope this shirt reminds you that you are part of something bigger than yourself.

A growing movement of people determined to protect vulnerable children.

Please accept this shirt as our way of saying thank you for joining this mission.

Give any amount today and choose your shirt size and select a color.

https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABl7ImQiOjUwMjMsInQiOjc2NywicyI6MTJ9AAwAAAAAA2Vk0nrTOWNGnKvisRlbKCOfDGrHagqpA4AA9mzq-ldEi6vKCUDN018AQ8qHFbXKQg4ETv-vZJZ8ysIO2nZeIkNvJRSAgDQwRGgBFblHJw
Protect God's Children Today

Now let me tell you why this mission means so much to me.

My name is Eduardo Verástegui.

Several years ago, I learned firsthand about the horrific reality of child trafficking. What I heard broke my heart.

Children were being bought and sold.
Families were being torn apart.
Lives were being destroyed.

I couldn't forget it.

I couldn't stay silent.

I kept asking myself one question:

"What if it were my child?"

That question changed my life.

What started as a film project became a mission and a calling.

That calling eventually led me to help produce the film Sound of Freedom.

Not for fame.
Not for awards.
But because I believed people needed to see the truth.

For years, many people said the film would never succeed.

Doors closed.
Studios walked away.
People told us to give up.

But when innocent children are suffering, silence is not an option.

And while the film helped awaken millions of people to this crisis, awareness alone is not enough.

That is why we created the Sound of Freedom Foundation.

Our mission is simple:

To stop the sale of God's children.

https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABl7ImQiOjUwMjMsInQiOjc2NywicyI6MTJ9AAwAAAAAA2Vk0nrV9P5WFyWiR4XlKfPPgzQ11QNjzMShWlsav4Yayv4Yk0uYc4Ot6dSgZBTuVp9vg6Y91g_xejxHpUhFClZeCYvbQcGR5zsM7kyIcQ
Protect God's Children Today

Every day, vulnerable children are targeted by traffickers who prey on poverty, instability, loneliness, and fear.

And every day, we work to fight back.

Jesus said,

"Let the little children come to me, for the kingdom of heaven belongs to such as these." (Matthew 19:14)

Every child is precious in God's eyes.

Every child is created with dignity, purpose, and worth.

And every child deserves someone willing to stand up and fight for them

https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABl7ImQiOjUwMjMsInQiOjc2NywicyI6MTJ9AAwAAAAAA2Vk0nrW0SJwbzoLjXviM6PvSSfKjSxN862yIuOqiXpahkrumBjh4dqNON20v_sBM3nrxPXDlA0JyRl7ZWnjgAAtdpNGHiRQFTXJ8hPM7g

https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABl7ImQiOjUwMjMsInQiOjc2NywicyI6MTJ9AAwAAAAAA2Vk0nrYWWgV9QUdJECrli369BGVQdh7ihOv8XacoNIRDou_HBIK_PqgE7GZU3M6NQi4fmTrLsiEiE6Q24JxG_ll9m5HsgI0lgbZrXView
Protect God's Children Today

When you make your first gift today, you help:

- Prevent exploitation by helping strengthen vulnerable families before traffickers can prey on children.

- Support intervention efforts by equipping trusted partners working to help rescue children trapped in exploitation.

- Educate parents and communities about the warning signs traffickers use to target children.

- Raise awareness so more people understand the reality of this crisis.

- Advocate for stronger protections for vulnerable children and greater accountability for traffickers.

This is how change happens.

One person refuses to ignore the suffering, refuses to stay silent, and chooses to fight for a child they may never meet.

Today, that person can be you.

https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABl7ImQiOjUwMjMsInQiOjc2NywicyI6MTJ9AAwAAAAAA2Vk0nraRGYZwIkAG1_-uXXvL0zlSCA7cEzvoX-VFkh48G_ZwkxOyTevo00gHHy9kqR7F92Y8Aoig0i-WsfAISnx1Nw4wPiQx2LUYn_ZUw

body:
They’re still too little to understand politics. But I wasn’t going to lie to them.

| [](https://trk.email.vivekforohio.)
---
Peter,
Before I announced this campaign, I sat down with my two sons.
They’re not old enough to grasp what a campaign or politics really is. But they know when something serious is happening.
So I told them the truth. We’ll be on the road. _A lot._
They might see strangers shouting at dad... I might be out of town some days... They might read nasty headlines about our family — things that aren’t true.
I promised to always keep them safe, but I also told them the truth:
**This won’t be easy. But when your country is at a crossroads, you don’t hide. You lead.****
****[That’s why I’m running for Governor of Ohio.](https://trk.email.vivekforohio.)****
**Not because it’s easy. Not because it’s safe. But because I refuse to let my sons grow up in a country that no longer believes in itself.
Ohio should be the state that leads this nation again — in education, in industry, in values that matter.
I’m fighting for that future. For my family. For yours. For every child who deserves a country worth inheriting.**
****[If you believe that too, I need you with me today.](https://trk.email.vivekforohio.)**

Winning in Ohio would bring us one step closer to the four seats we need to flip for a Democratic Senate majority. **In Iowa,** recent polling has the race _within reach_. Winning this race would mean flipping a seat that’s been in Republican hands for _years_. **In Kansas,** Republicans are scrambling to pour millions of dollars into attack ads. That’s because new polling shows the Senate race is _tied in Kansas._ If we won that seat, it would be held by a Democrat for the first time in **_nearly 100 years._** We can win in all of these races, Derek, [**but not without your help.**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-dnc-october-2026-gfr?amount=7&refcode=em_20261008_9752_fr&refcode2=9752_22930333_VxvcMA&akid=9752%2E22930333%2EVxvcMA) **Your gift to the DNC will not directly fund any specific candidate, but it WILL fuel our national midterm operation — helping us expand our digital operations, reach more voters, and support 10,000+ campaigns that rely on our tech and data infrastructure. name: =?UTF-8?q?Mar=C3=ADa_Teresa_Kumar=2C_Voto_Latino?=
subject: A conversation I had with my Uber driver
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Voto Latino
body:
We’re going all in this year.
#
Hi Peter, it’s María Teresa.
I want to talk to you about a recent conversation I had with my Uber driver in Texas.
His name was Tim, and he wasn’t registered to vote in Texas. In fact, he didn’t even know an election was coming up. So I did what I do best — I talked with him, listened, and convinced him on the spot.
There are thousands of Texans just like Tim, Peter. Eligible voters who are totally out of the loop in this election. Not because they don’t care, but because they don’t know how powerful their vote is.
**That conversation is Voto Latino's entire mission in a nutshell — finding the voters traditional campaigns ignore and getting them into the game.**
Traditional political campaigns spend tens of millions of dollars fighting over the same voters who are likely to turn out, and they routinely ignore voters who care deeply about their communities but simply aren’t being reached or informed by standard campaign outreach.
Look at Texas’s 15th Congressional District, for instance: 315,000 registered voters sat out the last election. That’s more than 300,000 already-registered voters who stayed home because _no one_ engaged them or gave them a reason to turn out.
**We’re not letting that happen this year, Peter.**
That’s why Voto Latino is heading to the Rio Grande Valley not once, but _three_ times before Election Day. This week, we’re hosting community town halls, connecting directly with folks who don’t vote often, and powering aggressive get out the vote operations across South Texas.
**But reaching voters who’ve been left behind takes real, on-the-ground resources and direct community organizing.**
**[Will you pitch in $3 right now to help fund our Rio Grande Valley town halls and get out the vote operations before November 3rd?](https://act.votolatino.org/go/57?c0=em-ms-voto-20261008-1._C1N2f&amount=3&refcode=em20261008-658&t=1&akid=658%2E1366028%2EbTlaX3)**
**[Donate $3 ››](https://act.votolatino.org/go/57?c0=em-ms-voto-20261008-1._C1N2f&amount=3&refcode=20261008-658&t=20&akid=658%2E1366028%2EbTlaX3)**
When we meet people where they’re at, answer their questions, and show them how much their vote matters, we don’t just increase turnout, but we build lasting political power.
Thank you for supporting our work,
María Teresa Kumar
Voto Latino

Sarah’s commitment to public service and her focus on improving the lives of working families across Delaware are exactly what we need more of in government. And all of Sarah’s work is made possible by grassroots donors like you. She doesn’t have right-wing billionaires writing huge checks to fund her campaign. She’s counting on our neighbors here in Delaware, and regular people across the country, pitching in $20 or whatever they can at a time. Thank you for your support! Tess

**Smucker: All Jelly, No Substance**
I recently received a promotional mailer from Congressman Lloyd Smucker, with messaging on how he’s “focused on affordability” which literally made me both laugh out loud and shake my head in disbelief. He talked about how he’s cutting taxes for working families, cutting wasteful spending, lowering health care costs, as well as standing up for small businesses and family farms. He’s clearly feeling the pressure to hitch his campaign wagon to “affordability” as voters continue to experience the increasing economic pressures of everyday life.
I do agree with the statement on his mailer that “...reckless spending and government waste are driving up prices...” I’ve heard Nancy say this more than once: we don’t have a spending problem, we have a spending priority problem. So, yes, Congressman Smucker, if we wouldn’t have spent...

* $9.5 billion by the Department of Government Efficiency to pay federal employees not to work;1

* $43.6 billion so far this year on the war in Iran (and p.s. it’s likely to cost us $2-$3 billion more a month as it continues)2; or

* $45 billion for ICE detention centers, allocated through the One Big Beautiful Bill (in which the Government Accountability Office has recently reported a slew of wasted / wasteful resources)3

...you wouldn’t need to spend time trying to convince voters that you’re focused on our affordability and responsible spending, because you would have already done something about it as a senior member of the House Committee on Ways and Means as well as a member of the Joint Economic Committee and the House Committee on the Budget.
While this mailer makes me angry, it also motivates me. I support Nancy’s campaign because we need someone who will actually represent our everyday needs and concerns in Washington – not someone who will just make desperate, last-minute plays to try to earn our votes with empty commitments while spending most of his time enabling a reckless administration.
So, I hope you get angry and motivated too. Put a sign in your yard, talk to your friends, family and neighbors and make sure they have a plan to vote. Choose one item off the list at the bottom of this email to support Nancy.
Because Nancy’s been doing the work – talking to voters, researching the issues – understanding what we need from our Congress. Now it’s our responsibility to help her get there.
_\- Contributed by Amy Criswell, York County PA-11 resident_

## **Week in Review**
---

**The Zekely Podcast****** Nancy was recently interviewed by Dr. Zeke Taylor, a PA doctor and podcaster who interviews Democratic leaders, candidates and individuals who are creating change in their communities. During the interview, they talked some medical shop, how Congress should hold the President accountable, Americans’ medical debt and the expected 2027 Medicaid cuts from the One Big Beautiful Bill, and the importance of soft diplomacy, among a slew of other topics. If you know anyone who is on the fence or says, “I don’t know Nancy and what she stands for,” share this video to see her in action!
You can watch the full episode [here](https://matj3.r.a.d.sendibm1.com/mk/cl/f/sh/7nVU1aA2nfuSp5GZj1ll2PMecZY1d1V/S9llildI-5TS).

---
**Meeting with Future Constituents Across the District** Nancy continues to meet with voters across the district and here are just a few highlights from this past week:
She met with the Willow Valley Democratic Club on September 29 to provide an update on the campaign, shared results of a [recent poll against Lloyd Smucker](https://matj3.r.a.d.sendibm1.com/mk/cl/f/sh/7nVU1aA2nfyEo8HBgAEf780GxIXb6uX/ANSaGdPgct01), and engaged in a wide-ranging discussion on healthcare costs, immigration, and foreign policy.
On October 1, she also visited Moravian Manor in Lititz, with Democrat, Independent and Republican voters in attendance, where they held a lively discussion on affordability, especially the rising cost of medications, what legislation she would champion in Congress, and how she would work to address the skyrocketing national debt.

**Good Morning!** On this day in 1918, U.S. Cpl. Alvin York was credited with killing 20 German soldiers and [leading the capture of 132 more](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2OpDAQhJ_GZKC2MT8TOLiEbC69EBnTxn1r8MhugXj71ewmm29Yn0pV0vfvOT8tRTq2v3ZHwz7NB14lIjPmOdq8YeE3CfS6bV5XKgfeZVag-lpCDeNsHdOJs7bVajyiwrZCI4eH1F07DmMVzOKtdRKcBq1ka-WiYPFetd04yG7sXUXmvScBRgmg267Ry8PrvnMo9bA6BUIDrsQpN_8THRzQxzudmBuX9iqawPwqov0j1CTUdF1Xc6HNyAF32gLf75pQ03eoAxVO-RZqsvGko75T_vgBq2zW10UxUukHoWHbLcWvI_6ln9OozwAAAP__Zvh8pA) during the Meuse-Argonne offensive in WWI. He was promoted to sergeant and awarded the Medal of Honor. If you live along the Gulf Coast, start with our _Take Off_ section. The Atlantic's [first hurricane of the year](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykUL2OtDAQexrogiY_LFCk-Bq6_dorUTaZwJyyBCWzi_btT9wrXGfZlm35677cHSXa1__uiZZjXnY8a0JmLEtyZcXKF7PR8XElBKo7fuqiQN2EBAHj4jzTGxfj2mAjokLdopXDJE2vx2FsN-shgkbv-ylK2TuQAOhB6j7oSY6Db8leeRJglABG9515TNHceo_SDMEraAxgIM6l-86084YxffIbS-fzs012Yz5qo_81am7UfJ5n5x_1Wn3pjZov2Kh5e5VC3u0oKrqad8ElH-RdErwVdCzWV4ridVnbYsNxUkpUb0NjYH06Sr9t_MeT3lb9BAAA__9qc33P) is expected to form today and come ashore tomorrow night. Stay safe. Is a blood sugar spike after a meal actually a bad thing? The glucose monitors that changed life for millions of diabetics are now showing up on everyone else, from marathon runners to your coworker counting carbs. But there's a catch. New research found the sensors overestimated blood sugar by about 30% in people without diabetes, and the spike scaring you might not even be real. Christopher has the full story on today's episode of _The Flyover Podcast_. [Tune in here](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykz71uwyAYheGrgS0W_-CBoUu2dO2ICHy2qTBYgBz57qtUvYOuR0eP9H493MOnnMr66XewY6muwKtnGAOay76t0Md72dJx-RZj6gWu7hhh6kbJjRjnw0gnOOFxtAsAA47BUj1TIbnRBm9WBuGFXrhW0qg4SzVHbzSVgTMPMVCc7NujhBhKiOByEs95EUoGoELHwAgSBGIatU3fNZWxwZKvekKbQt1xttsYR0f8A7E7YvcGz-ZLnPKF2P3veNTYIEAZuNl4vFLOqSuNBFl3n_IvM_5Zf1r2EwAA__97n3Ai)! Later today, watch for a message from our partner, [Doroni Aerospace](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkT-v2zAMxD-NvMWQKPnf4KFAkO117WgwFm2zsCRDYvKQb1_4NS3QuevvCPKO9-Nj-kDeOa7fMdAoS5oifZadRChPO-aVipxk4-OF2XsukV5lAg3txeiL7iechZ80Oaz8uBAB2YpG0w3GNbbv-mobB2itJQOwuDuYO3rE1mvsScNgoGsqHs99RuveaO1sU7v7sLi2mcm4zs-gldPkWVKufyaOstGyv9KTcj2nUO3jJnIUZb8puCm4cXxSkdqnnCLXnE5qbw8JU0mPPJOyVwrIu4L2hIE8P4Ky1wPZXw7MEimfed_6jOFAXuPXxF_R9Ppih376_QNnoXXGOt1oBa1EDFSUvWZaKGf8c2lOUSiKsteYIr2hUA7_kgPX0-OWAlV59Mcn7zuXtlNOr6fvr9Dyn109R_gVAAD__3BWqgw), about its two-seat personal electric aircraft and an opportunity to invest as the company moves toward flight testing and FAA certification. Today’s sponsor, [The Oxford Club](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykz71u6yAYxvGrwVusl288MJzFW87aEWF4iamwiYAmzd1X6S10ffToJ_0_ru7qc8nn7b8_0I5U3YnPXnAMbK74dsM-3sue7y_fYsz9xFd3DJi6ULiAcT6M_EAn_BRtQmTIJ7RUL1RIbrSZdivMhpAUJi2D2biMQcjEqfKG0sWoNGX79iiAoQCCy1lsSxJKBqRCx8CACMCYR23zZ83n2DGVV31gm0M9pmL3Me6d8H-ErYStJz7n-p1qi6F8be8LYevBCFvVAqCnZuP9mUvJXWki4Hb4XH6h8cf-h2U_AQAA___GJ272), is sharing Dr. Mark Skousen’s research into three publicly traded companies he believes could become potential acquisition targets for Elon Musk.

## US Plans Largest Shipyard Since WWII
President Trump announced a [$6.6 billion plan](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOpDAQRL8GMka2MeAJHFxCNpdeiBrcQJ9sg9o9M-LvV7PSfsGmpVKV3vv3mB5AkfL2FxJ6WY8p47tEFEGeIvCGRT7JTucFHAKVjFeZjDJ9o1Wj3ASL0AsnC3XwK6LBtkavh7u2XesGV---DW7WzqnFalDaLCG4rrtjP7ctOOiXmvxnTyvltFK27W52vq-27xbUdgiLUZVVGEgOvv0_KMuOa7yOF_JtOVId_S5ylqr9U5mxMiNlQcYilDfMG2VEprx9qpUZE0US4Ksyo_AznQ3kwE-m2CTgK0IOTXnOCZgyNj_UNftwvilGKv1QWbUloPj9Lb9U9vLmKwAA__-ZcYT5) to build what he called the largest new U.S. shipyard since World War II at Sparrows Point, near Baltimore, to produce parts for Virginia-class nuclear attack submarines. Anduril Industries, the defense tech company co-founded by Palmer Luckey, is putting up [$3.7 billion](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2unTAQhJ8GukW2MT-ncJGG7qRNiRZ7OWxkDLINhLeP0L1vcNtvNDOa-fMe38iew-c3rmTyvI2BruQpZ4qjx_ihlB-y8H5jdI5ToDuNSqgWpADRj2gznzRqLJ2ZiRTVJRnZvaRu6r7ry8V0tbDU6pej2Srq5smik20jm0bNpKapZPPkSSF6KYSum0pPr1m3jSWpO2eVKLQgx3mL1d-NQ15o9vd2UqzstpbeLDnvqah_FWoo1HBdV4XBHZH9oxdqeAYUaviGcECCgOcNHE5KGY7kWmhhYu95C5A3oH87Bge4UmSLkCAd04qRAwEHd6QcGT1MmKiMxu3X40xtV2jxWfGrtsw_fPM06n8AAAD__wKujhk), and the Navy will pay up to $2.9 billion for what the 2-million-square-foot plant produces. Trump also said American taxpayers will get a [40% stake](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0L1uhDAQBOCngc7INuavcJGG7tKmRAtejk0MWPYeHG8fkVdIOyONPs3XY3gAedqen7Ci5XkfNjyTR2aMg4f4xMR3slC4IDpHacMrDVrqWigpZDvAxHTgYCB3dkbUWOZoVdMpU5Vt0-aLrUzZ4AydUV3VdGquunFSbqxNpbtydHVO9t5TUrZKSlNWhRm72dTVhMo0btIyMxId8R6L7502XnD2135gLKZ9zb1dmEPKyo9M95nuz_Ms5v19q-8-033YPTFNKdM9x9caRMQDwSeRXjFESihgxUgTbILhHeDCKBLDD4oNT1GLehTpNa4QaUPhEHwerQsneU-pbjIjnyuQ_8PwPz88rP4NAAD__9HCieo) in the subsidiary running the yard. What the government pays for that stake hasn't been released. The plant, on the site of a former Bethlehem Steel mill, will start with torpedo tubes and later build [larger submarine sections](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkMHOpCAQhJ8Gb0xaZJQ5cNiLt9nrHg1KM_YGwUDrxLffuK_w3ypVyZeq-vOe3o4ipc9vt6HlkKeE3xqRGcsUXflg5dtZab9c8Z5qwqtOClQvW5BgJrcwnThp13gbEBV2Ddp2eLX62ZnBNKt1asHQwQBeK4M4dzME8zQ9vAbXqsE0ZG9eC2BaAN09H3p-Bd0_F2z14BcFQgN64lwefzMlXjHEK59YHkvemmhX5r2K7pdQo1BjuvZc-Y6EGm-wUGMLQo1wq6PKe49QI5dj2yVn6VLKR1pQ9rKf5VElpRMrb5hYfolX6ZI_CkUZcpGzi0xbLijrMcvgForEl1BjU6zfvxQj1X4QGj6bo_i_IP_w19OqfwEAAP__ZnWNxQ). The U.S. has 26 Virginia-class subs and builds about 1.3 annually against a Navy goal of two, as officials point to China's dominance in shipbuilding. Operations will begin around 2030 with 3,100 permanent jobs.
## Isaias Set to Hit Gulf Coast as Hurricane
Tropical Storm Isaias is expected to [rapidly strengthen](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykUL2OtDAQexrogiY_LFCk-Bq6_dorUTaZwJyyBCWzi_btT9wrXGfZlm35677cHSXa1__uiZZjXnY8a0JmLEtyZcXKF7PR8XElBKo7fuqiQN2EBAHj4jzTGxfj2mAjokLdopXDJE2vx2FsN-shgkbv-ylK2TuQAOhB6j7oSY6Db8leeRJglABG9515TNHceo_SDMEraAxgIM6l-86084YxffIbS-fzs012Yz5qo_81am7UfJ5n5x_1Wn3pjZov2Kh5e5VC3u0oKrqad8ElH-RdErwVdCzWV4ridVnbYsNxUkpUb0NjYH06Sr9t_MeT3lb9BAAA__9qc33P) into a hurricane today and make landfall Friday evening on the north-central Gulf Coast, forecasters said. It would be the Atlantic's first hurricane of 2026. Hurricane watches cover coastal Mississippi, Alabama, and the western Florida Panhandle, where winds could gust [70 to 100 mph](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkMuK3DAURL9G3qnR04-FFoHgXWcTQpbmtnTVvolsGUnTjf9-8PzCbKuo4nD-3pc7UKL9-Qs2dC3mZcd3TdgaliVBeWJtV7LScUIJgeqOZ12UUD2XgotxAd_ohYuBLriIqFB36OQwSWP1OIzd6mJEiGZQBoIxEEcpeovoQxR2sHKyHbnrTwoxSiGMtjfzmKLprUdphuCVYEZgoJbL7V-mva0Y05lfWG4-b11ya2tHZfoHUzNTMzz8RXx1TM1_fjM1t5IP8pB4bblsnCoQVB5zQQ-18Q3-I0-whwgp8fWjFPKwI4-FApxMzdfsZHqmwPRPqQdhJzPqrrhwvCklqv3AjHhuQOkLqX3T5MupzwAAAP__kXuJ-Q). A first hurricane this late in the season has never been recorded. Storm surges could reach 7 feet along the Mississippi and Alabama coasts, with 3 to 6 inches of rain and up to 10 inches in spots from southeastern Louisiana to the Panhandle. Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis has declared a state of emergency in 25 counties. Track the latest advisories [here](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLFuwyAURb8Gb7EeGAwZGNJKljqk6hCpo4XNw1BhEwGym7-vkl_oeO9wjnS-r-PVhBi25dOsqKtL44ZHiVgr5jGavGCpz8eH-8Nka0PZ8FFGBqw_UTiBGs1cw44jN43VDpFh16Cm8ky56JRUjddGukmAlJRaxV0nlEU-9ZPhcw9c9NgE_eRRAEUBeCdaPp0d78WMlEs7MyAc0IaacvuTwlY9uvhIO-Z2TmsTta_1Xkh3IWwgbDiOo9383G7JmHZJO2FDxd9K2JDRZSyesOH6cbm9f11unLC34usaCRtAghKsfc0ma3s_Qoyh9JJwWFYT4stW_xlp1-wvAAD__zmdevo). Landfall is forecast between 5 p.m. and midnight Friday as a Category 1 or 2 storm. Rain could spread across the Southeast this weekend and reach the Ohio Valley and Northeast by midweek.
## List: Israel, Poland Top Defense Spending Rates
A survey of defense spending by advanced nations showed that Israel now devotes a [larger share of its economy to defense](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0DFurjAQBODTQAeyjQFTuHgN3f_alGiDF9jE2MjeH8TtI3KFtJ9GM9J8vKYXkKew_ocdLS9xCnhlj8yYJg9pxcyPbHTckJyjHPDOkxKqq6SohJlgZjpx0lA6uyAqbEq0sh-kbhvTm3KzIJq-c8pIY2RnFmwFuh6HHlrTKT1gSfbpk0IYKYRu2lp_Dovu2hml7t2sRKEFOuKY6q9IgTdc_B1PTPUc99LbjfnIRfOvUGOhxuu66pPyG_wMBzF4yvwECzUmCN_oqp08MaS7ygcGR2GtKFQRZ1fN8R04EeZHlFBtocYyWXdc5D3lri-0WHcg_7vMfzzstOonAAD__1GagdA) than any other country, spending 7.8% of GDP in 2025 amid intensifying multi-front conflicts in the Middle East. That's up from its 5% average between 2015 and 2022. Poland is second at 4.5% of GDP, the highest among NATO members and above the alliance's new 3.5% core-defense target for 2035. The U.S. came in at 3.1%, despite spending $954 billion in absolute terms. Overall, 28 of 33 nations in the ranking boosted defense spending relative to their 2015-2022 averages. Only five saw their GDP share decline, including the U.S. [See the full ranking.](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0DFurjAQBODTQAeyjQFTuHgN3f_alGiDF9jE2MjeH8TtI3KFtJ9GM9J8vKYXkKew_ocdLS9xCnhlj8yYJg9pxcyPbHTckJyjHPDOkxKqq6SohJlgZjpx0lA6uyAqbEq0sh-kbhvTm3KzIJq-c8pIY2RnFmwFuh6HHlrTKT1gSfbpk0IYKYRu2lp_Dovu2hml7t2sRKEFOuKY6q9IgTdc_B1PTPUc99LbjfnIRfOvUGOhxuu66pPyG_wMBzF4yvwECzUmCN_oqp08MaS7ygcGR2GtKFQRZ1fN8R04EeZHlFBtocYyWXdc5D3lri-0WHcg_7vMfzzstOonAAD__1GagdA)

clean_body: The dubbed "Stop Nick Shirley Act" was made to stop me. | | | | | | | Peter, There's now a law in California with my name associated with it. Everyone in Sacramento knows exactly what the "Stop Nick Shirley Act" means. On August 22nd, Governor Newsom signed AB 2624. Three days later, I was standing at the State Capitol with a crowd of people who showed up because they understood what this law actually does. Supporters say it protects immigration workers from harassment. Here's what it really does, Peter: it makes it harder for anyone -- me included -- to investigate where your tax dollars are being sent. I said it plainly at the rally: this is not the end; this is just the beginning. Because here's the part that should bother you more than anything else. The assemblymember who wrote this bill is married to California's Attorney General -- the one person in this state whose entire job is supposed to be going after fraud. Instead, his wife wrote the bill that makes it harder to expose it. That's not a coincidence, Peter. That's the system protecting itself. I've spent the last year showing up where legacy media won't -- daycare centers, tax-funded nonprofits, the offices of people who'd rather I disappear than answer a question. That work is exactly why a state legislature decided to write a law with my name on it instead of going after the fraud I keep finding. A state senator at the rally called it unconstitutional. A city attorney called it a direct threat to the First Amendment. They're right -- and they're not going to be the ones who stop it. That's going to take people willing to fund the reporters still asking the questions. Here's something most people don't see, Peter: doing this work independently means there's no network paying for the flight to Sacramento, no legal department covering me if a state files a complaint over a story, no corporate budget for the cameras and editors it takes to get this footage in front of you. When I showed up at that rally, Lincoln Media Foundation was on site with their own journalists to cover it, because they understood what was actually at stake before most of the country did. That 's why I'm partnering with Lincoln Media Foundation. They understand how important it is to support independent journalists and help us keep doing the work without compromising what makes it independent in the first place. I'm grateful for their partnership and commitment, and - helping cover travel, equipment, and the costs that come with confronting people on camera instead of reading a press release about them. They can try to prevent people like me from exposing their corruption, that's why it crucial to support independent journalists like myself. They are creating laws to silence free speech -- and that's why we need to continue the fight and I need your support. People like you decide this work is worth funding, and it helps me continue! Peter Willis,

Before this year, it would have sounded like a pipe dream if we told you

We just finished a three-day swing through the district's northern counties.
It started on Thursday with our Veterans Beer Call in Anniston. It was exactly what we hoped for. We spent time with more than 30 people, not all of whom were veterans, shared some good laughs, and had very emotional conversations about veterans' suicide, the state of the Veterans Health Care System, and how we can care for our veterans.
Friday night was First Friday in Gadsden. The team from the Etowah County Democratic Women's Club turned out, along with a few other supporters, and we handed out nearly 1,000 push cards.
Then, on Saturday, it was Oxfest in Oxford. Okay, I won't lie. It was a long, hot, exhausting day, but here are the good parts. First, we shared a table with the great Pam Howard, who is running in State House District 40; her campaign staff, Carol and Joe, were with us the entire way; and we were right across the street from the Calhoun County Democrats. What kept me going in the 90+ degree heat was the constant stream of people who came over and said, "We've never met, but I'm following you, I'm voting for you, and I want to thank you for campaigning with such a positive message." ....

| |

# One Last Thought Until Next Week
---
| | |
---
Hey everybody,
We've started the sprint to the finish line. That means two things:
* First, we're doing more events every week now. In the last two weeks, we spent 11 days on the road meeting people. We've got 5 events this week. We expect it to pick up. If you have public events happening in your area, let us know about them. We'll do our best to get there.
* Second, we're spending money on advertising. We've been waiting for the past few weeks, and they're here. We've got time on over 20 billboards across the district, and in Lee and Chambers County, you can hear our ads on multiple local radio stations.

But what you've been doing is as important as ever. We're still a grassroots campaign. We need you out there talking to your friends, sharing our posts on social media, and putting up those yard signs for people to see.
And that strategy is working. Everywhere we go, people tell us they've seen our signs and want to meet us. They tell us they came across us on social media and liked what they saw. Many of them also say that a friend or family member told them about the campaign, and they looked us up.
It's working, but we have to keep building the momentum. Make sure your friends are registered to vote and make a plan to go with them to the polls. Talk to everyone and ask them to ignore party labels. We don't want their votes just because we're Democrats. We want their votes because we care about the people who live in this district.
There are four weeks... 28 days... to the general election.
Be well.

We'll talk soon,

Lee

## Fort Hood Shooter Execution Set
The Army is [scheduled to execute](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL2uozAUhJ8GOiP_BULhYhu6bLslOphjsGQwa59g8vZX5BVuN8Vo9M337zW-wAe_L39hQ0OXi-OOJQckwjQSXpALLLikWGi1sUzxk888jZLLlgnO-HMES_7EUUM9m4nPvajRiK4X-tEpJerVoHSTe1iwfT9ZpZyc5ENrq5XSQnW2rb255wTnTyG45F3Tcq0USIdgn9BLqDTH2VNMDa34hXLhE09MjY1bHcxKdORK_ankUMmhlNK4eOn7yF2o5HDHSg6U3tvB4DhSPDGzzQdPkD7M-eT3heX_b5gZXmjf5OPOXEzE1hhnltcYCRPb_QyBrZBhr5OZj-JD8LntKs2XDXz48tBvPZ5G_gQAAP__d8SNGQ) Nidal Hasan by firing squad at Fort Hood on Dec. 3, acting Army Secretary Adam Telle announced Tuesday, days after President Trump approved the method. Hasan, a former Army psychiatrist, killed 13 people and wounded more than 30 at the post's Soldier Readiness Processing Center on Nov. 5, 2009. Julia Wilson, who was [nine months pregnant](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL2OpDAQhJ_GZB75b4wnILiEbC-9EDWmAes8NLJ7zezbn2Z1b7BxqUr1fX8-pg9IOR3bb3jiwK-VpgOvmpEZy8T4gnrBhluhi_dI10xftdV5Msp4qZVUYYLIqeHkoFuGWS0P3eGg-4d2995a3e1DtIgWEa3Rzvn1jsb5JdgIGLz3QXdpeM9ppYLWyqj-5pWzFsyKEAM8DAincElM5cY7fp9a8xc1LLdIzy4PO_NZhf0lzCjMeF3X7W_Eg9s7FmaEwilmFGZ8swkzZoqQhRlXKix3okXWnYjTscn6WVpqVGRBiFwlnGehhovEF8ZPTnTISEdLkfF_C4sw410pOQdv1365y9ArLd0KswxBWanA9jCvRsdZd2VYzivlnKrvhVPbE1L-puCf2m-D-RcAAP__q9WbuQ) and in a vehicle parked outside that day, said of the execution: "_An eye for an eye. Too bad he doesn't have 13 of them_." Then-Staff Sgt. Alonzo Lunsford took a round to the head, hit the floor, and played dead while Hasan shot him twice more. He [calls the firing squad](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL2OhCAURp8GOwyg409BsY3dbLulucBVyTIygTvivP3GeYXtvuRLTk7Oz32-gw9-X7_hgZrOJc47lhyQCNNMeEIusOKaYqHNxmLiOx_ZzEqojkvBxTCDJX_g3ELltBFulBVq2Y-yvfVNI6tNGxg6oW4OLd5Gt_RD39jWDH1rOjMYgZXXF04KMUgplOjrTrRNA2pBsAOMClgr0HmKqaYNP1JLeMcDU23jowp6I3pm1nwxNTE1lVLqX0PndTI1XWymJimYmsS1lpiIbzE6nrcYye8rz690-CMmnhAsZY4n2hf5uPOYHCa-eweBb5BhZ2qqknbP4kPwuetZK9YH-PBRof8mPLT6CwAA___VhYgN) a fitting end. Whether it happens Dec. 3 is another question. Hasan has exhausted his military appeals, but his lawyers can still take the case to [federal civilian courts](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0L1upTAQxfGnMZ2vxmMuH4WLbeiy7ZZogAGsDDjCDoa3X5FXSH2kn_46_z76D_Li9-UvbezSNYd-5xyFU-KjT3xRzLTwcoSc1jHkIdzxjEOPgJU2oKHpaUz-5L6kYnIDTK0p2Jm6NeW7ttYUq5t5mpFMDWjbeWAsS8sDVG-o27e13BTePZwBaIwBhPpVQWkt4cw0NtQiqRJ48ikcr7TyT9Qsdzj5eI1hK8StKX1FZf8o7BR2OefXZ07XMyrsHlthZ0BhB7XC7uTj1uI_WW6dWWcvoiOzHsOe_P7Nk55Y6NbCC4keVxLhfeGoN7p1TCSiV4q0R80Xj9_Jh11hVxxu-nosH6talbBs5OWnL_3219Ph_wAAAP__lxqPIg), and no U.S. service member has been shot by firing squad since 1945.
## Texas Executes Man in Silsbee Killing
Texas [executed Jamaal Howard](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGyozAMRb_GdGRkmcW4oNjG3dt2S0YYEfzWiTNYiZO_34FfeJUK3Tk6un-_pi-KKd6vf-jGo7zXPN25lsQivE_CbyqVrnzdc5Ut5DrnT3mVeULAvtXQwjBRkPjiqaNmGWdYnG541Nbp7pc1Rjfb6GC1JnRAfe8saTustIZ5CORms-hgmzgeOA0waA0I9tJDZwzhyhQGckiqA16i5P0iG59Sa_rkF--XkG9NGjeRR1Hmt0Kv0NdaL89Ckhf6HAGFvkjePwr98dsxSGK-K_THXYVeg0IPVqE_4S2_OTyPSPtNN6LUbrnSvrSJZaPUxvs3h3Mdtj0WofYR_7FC7xDQOGfgZDX7uDxqTCmW3qoOrjeK6TSWnzb9GvF_AAAA__-yk5OW), 46, by lethal injection Wednesday evening at the Huntsville Unit for fatally shooting convenience store clerk Vickie Swartout during a 2000 robbery in Silsbee. Howard [apologized to Swartout's relatives](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL2SozAMgJ_GdM7I4sdJQXEN3V57JSOMAM86eMdWcHj7G_IKW0vzfZ_072v8Ih_8vv6lJ_fyXuK4c8mBRTiNwm_KhVZeUyyyuVimeOYjTyMCdtqAhvtITvzBY0PV3E8wP0zFvbEP07S2rk219W1tl3nh1tk7O5ixRWA7tbOz0D2azla-v3AG4G4MINhbB01dEy5M7k4PJNUAz15iusnGn6glnPHgdHPxWYV-E_nJqv6jcFA4lFJu35nkGiocrnsUDpdC4WBA4QBW4fDh6MyiJWp-s3sJ6yfteolJLyQUwqnzFqP4fdWkXdwP3j3vjnWWmFi7wOlbz690LaQ4TZxO7XeNAJelSv38U3wIPndWNbA-yYdPsfz200eP_wMAAP__rGmUvw), who watched through a window feet from the death chamber. "_I wish that you accept my apology and I wish for your forgiveness_ ," he said. He was pronounced dead at 8:03 p.m. Howard was 20 when he shot Swartout, 42, in the chest at the store, about 100 miles northeast of Houston. [Surveillance video shown at trial](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGO4yAQhp8Gd0QD9sZOQXEN3V57pTWGIbCHjQWzcfL2J0f3BtuNNL8-ff__53P-xJTTdv-NKxl-hjJvdLRMzFRnpie2A-90r-Xg6MqxlFd7tGXWoK9SgYRpRsfpQfOAnTcL-JvqyKjxpoaPse9VF80IC5ALvp-GwfseAsB4gyGEfsHpw1-7ZE6cApiUAg3j5QpD36MOhG7Cm0YxAPnEpV440lsq5Fd5UL24snbZROa9if6X0FZou7320vh8CW1PstBWgdAWRqHtd5NnQ6HtGyQbseQi6Unum0l-4YqYZSwHVi9Dqo1lJo6YZdq-yHEq2__webW0OZIu1tQY5Z7-klwKuyiRmdadhbZdNX4_Us6pXUcxwH3FlN_i_NPBH0b_CwAA__-IY5jn) captured the shooting, and court records say he took $114 and a carton of cigarettes.
