A steady gaze is more than looking; it is the discipline of seeing what is before us and wondering what brought it here.
The sag of a weathered gate, weakening boards, a fence line straining against itself.
A sentinel begins not with conclusions, but with inquiry:
What happened here?
What has changed?
What if we leave it?
The gaze follows the evidence--from what shaped it to what our choices will set in motion.
**Observation is the first act of stewardship.**
**We cannot protect what we refuse to observe.**
**Stewardship is the courage to look closely and act.**
Pause.
Breathe.
Look Deeper.
Refuel.
**Welcome to Sweet Ground.**

| |
---
| | **Spartz to J.D. Ford: Hoosiers Deserve a Real Policy Debate, Not a Circus**
---
| | FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE
__Two Indianapolis TV Stations Offer to Host Debates__ **October 8, 2026** **WESTFIELD, IN** - Congresswoman Victoria Spartz (IN-05) is challenging her Democratic opponent, State Senator J.D. Ford, to participate in a real policy debate, not a staged rally with his activists. The Spartz campaign has been working with the debate commission and local television stations to arrange a substantive debate. Two stations have offered to host:
* WTHR: October 19 or 20
* FOX59/CBS4: October 23 or 30

Spartz is ready to participate under either station’s proposed format and welcomes constituents from both sides in the audience if the stations can accommodate them. “Hoosiers deserve a serious policy debate, not another circus of nonstop screaming, shouting, jumping on tables, and spitting at my staff, as we have experienced at some town halls,” said Spartz. “A debate should be about answering tough questions, not who can shout the loudest.” “Since J.D. Ford just recently moved to Indiana’s 5th District from Marion County, he might not realize that you don’t usually run to get elected here on defunding the police, violent criminals on the streets, men in girls’ sports, transgender surgery for children, higher taxes, taxpayer benefits for illegals, and loopholes for special interests to fund his campaign. Or maybe he does realize that, and that’s why he is avoiding a real debate while radical San Francisco billionaires spend millions attacking me with fabricated lies.” “I am ready to defend every vote I have taken and answer tough questions about my record. J.D. Ford should be prepared to do the same and substantiate his accusations against me. Two television stations have offered to host. I am ready for either—or both. Why is J.D. hiding?”

# Palestine
* **Killed and wounded in Gaza:** Over the past 24 hours, four Palestinians were killed and 28 injured across Gaza, according to the Palestinian Ministry of Health.
* The total recorded death toll since October 7, 2023 is now 74,254 killed, with 175,306 injured. Since October 11, 2025, the first full day of the so-called ceasefire, Israel has killed at least 1,471 Palestinians in Gaza and wounded 5,189, while 836 bodies have been recovered.
* **Israeli artillery fire kills woman, wounds several in Gaza City:** A Palestinian woman was [killed](https://substack.com/redirect/30f7a1e3-c72c-4b89-80b2-a28ba6cfb607?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and several others wounded on Thursday by Israeli artillery fire northwest of Gaza City, WAFA reported.
* **Israeli forces detain dozens of Palestinians as settler attacks continue across the occupied West Bank:**
* **Detentions:** Israeli forces [detained](https://substack.com/redirect/a6ced0b0-4fa4-4f8b-94e3-183a23d23ab4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) or subjected at least 95 Palestinians to field interrogations across the occupied West Bank overnight and Thursday morning. Nine former prisoners were arrested in Qalqilya and five in Jenin, while the mayor of Tuqu, Saqr Suleiman, was arrested after Israeli forces raided his home southeast of Bethlehem.
* **Jericho:** Israeli forces [demolished](https://substack.com/redirect/2a910a40-f84e-4291-87b0-52d7994d450e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a two-storey home in Al-Duyuk Al-Tahta, west of Jericho. The demolition came two days after settlers established an outpost in the same area, where 15 Palestinian families were displaced in February following demolitions and settler attacks.
* **Ramallah:** Israeli settlers, protected by Israeli soldiers, attacked Palestinian olive harvesters in Abwein and forced them from their land in the eastern and northern areas of the town. The attacks came a day after settler violence in Burqa and the Ramin plain killed 44-year-old Ali Al-Bazari and wounded 16 others.
* **Salfit:** Four Palestinians were injured, including with fractures, when settlers [attacked](https://substack.com/redirect/139423db-662b-4da4-a124-655bc7338a00?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) farmers with sharp objects in Wadi Al-Shaer.
* **Hebron:** Israeli forces accompanied by settlers [raided and closed](https://substack.com/redirect/1aabe99e-c46c-490b-a9bc-b2bd509ad83b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the Freedom Center for Culture and Folk Arts in Ramadin, confiscating a Palestinian flag and searching books in its library.
* **Tulkarm:** Israeli forces [raided](https://substack.com/redirect/54972330-869e-47b2-a996-ee6da08ae2fd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the home of Muayyad Shaaban, head of the Palestinian Colonization and Wall Resistance Commission, for the second time in two months, holding him, his wife and daughter in one room while searching the property. His two sons remain in Israeli detention, including one held for about a year and a half without trial.
* **East Jerusalem:** Israeli forces [raided](https://substack.com/redirect/611f56e5-e1c3-4cc1-af8b-f6036eb37c0a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the home of Al-Eizariya municipal director Atta Jabr, beating him and leaving him requiring medical treatment, according to the Jerusalem governorate. Forces also extensively damaged four homes belonging to Jabr, his mother and his two brothers.
* **Israeli authorities demolish Palestinian-owned shop in northern Israel:** Israeli authorities [demolished](https://substack.com/redirect/16eea59d-949e-4791-8030-65cd77068c3f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a Palestinian-owned commercial building in the Arab town of Daburiyya in northern Israel on Thursday.
* The demolition comes amid increasing demolition orders targeting buildings in Palestinian communities inside Israel, often on the grounds of lacking construction permits.
* Restrictive planning policies make obtaining permits extremely difficult in many Palestinian towns, while some families have been forced to demolish their own homes to avoid heavy fines and demolition costs imposed by Israeli authorities.
* **Israel returns body of Palestinian prisoner, continues to withhold 99 others:** Israeli authorities returned the body of Palestinian prisoner Marwan Harzallah, from Al-Ain refugee camp in Nablus, the occupied West Bank, on Thursday, more than six months after he died in Israel's Megiddo Prison on March 28, 2026.
* Harzallah was arrested in January 2026 on allegations of "incitement." Palestinian prisoners' organizations [said](https://substack.com/redirect/75aa6f73-3207-4244-b0a8-2535f1f9383a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) his death was a direct result of being denied necessary medical treatment and healthcare, holding Israeli authorities responsible.
* Following the return of Harzallah's body, Israel continues to withhold the bodies of at least 99 Palestinians who died in its prisons, including 88 who have died since October 7, 2023.

* **Israel forces out most UK diplomats from occupied East Jerusalem:** Most British diplomats are [leaving](https://substack.com/redirect/e9748b87-43b9-4e45-85a5-85169ffaa6fd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the UK consulate in occupied East Jerusalem following an Israeli move to shut down its operations in retaliation for British sanctions last month on illegal Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank.

* As dozens of Palestinians were being killed near aid distribution sites run by the Gaza Humanitarian Foundation (GHF) in the summer of 2025, American diplomats in Israel drafted a cable warning against the GHF distribution system and said it risked more "mass casualty events." # Yemen
* **Three killed, 36 injured in attacks on Saudi airports:** Three people were killed and 36 others injured in Ansarallah [attacks](https://substack.com/redirect/554b0670-4a73-42e7-bdb0-f3e37bdbaffa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) targeting Abha International Airport and King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh on Tuesday and Wednesday, according to Saudi Arabia's General Authority of Civil Aviation. Both airports sustained material damage.
* The Saudi-led coalition claimed it destroyed the ballistic missile launch platform in Sana'a used in the Riyadh attack while it was being prepared for another imminent attack on Saudi Arabia.
* Loud explosions were reported in Riyadh on Thursday, according to AFP.
* **Ansarallah warns workers to stay away from Saudi oil facilities it considers targets:** Ansarallah [warned](https://substack.com/redirect/7a949f31-0a10-4d64-b3c3-8014cbae8163?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) workers on Thursday against remaining at Saudi oil facilities that the group considers potential military targets.
* "Our armed forces warn all employees, experts, engineers and workers at all Saudi oil facilities against being present in locations that represent targets for our forces, so as not to put their lives at risk, whether they have been targeted before or not," military spokesperson Yahya Saree said in a statement.
* Saree also renewed previous warnings to airlines, passengers and employees concerning airspace and airports that Ansarallah has threatened to target.
* **Saudi-backed Yemeni forces and Ansarallah continue battle for territory around Bab al-Mandab:** Fighting is continuing between Saudi-backed Yemeni forces and Ansarallah across southern and western Taiz as both sides make competing claims over control of strategic territory around the Bab al-Mandab Strait.
* Fighting was reported in Al-Shamayatayn, Al-Ma'afer and the southern and western Taiz countryside.
* Yemen's Saudi-backed army separately claimed it has carried out at least 2,103 operations against Ansarallah across multiple fronts, killing 1,860 fighters and destroying hundreds of pieces of military equipment and positions. The casualty figures could not be independently verified.
* Ansarallah military spokesperson Yahya Saree said the group targeted Saudi-backed forces and reinforcements near Bab al-Mandab with ballistic missiles, including at Al-Qawah camp in the Ras Al-Ara area, as well as positions south of Bab al-Mandab. He claimed the attacks killed and wounded dozens and caused fires at weapons storage sites. Ansarallah also claimed it shot down a Turkish-made Bayraktar Akinci armed reconnaissance drone belonging to Saudi Arabia over Taiz.
* The fighting displaced residents from rural areas of Taiz, while government authorities suspended classes and granted leave to public employees in districts they say have fallen under Ansarallah control, citing deteriorating security conditions.

* **Turkey rules out troop deployment under Mecca defense pact:** Turkey [will not deploy](https://substack.com/redirect/8611df31-ca22-40d2-ac00-2459a40a23b5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) troops to carry out offensive operations under its mutual defense agreement with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan, Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan said Thursday.
* "The Mecca agreement requires parties to defend any member under attack. It is not an offensive pact," Fidan said, stressing that Turkish forces would not be sent into another country to conduct attacks.
* Fidan said military officials were assessing possible contributions to Saudi Arabia's defense, particularly air defence, electronic warfare and technical support.
* The three countries agreed Monday to activate their collective defense commitments and facilitate the rapid deployment of military capabilities to Saudi Arabia following Ansarallah attacks.

* **Syria says it stands with Saudi Arabia but does not seek to "open new fronts": **Syria [said](https://substack.com/redirect/cf96f427-2a69-4d14-9eba-ac4437968fdc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) it "stands firmly alongside Saudi Arabia against threats to its security and stability," while stressing that its policy is based on "stability, peace and cooperation, not opening new fronts," according to the Syrian Information Ministry.
* The statement came after reports that Damascus was considering providing military assistance to Saudi Arabia as fighting between Saudi-backed Yemeni forces and Ansarallah escalated.

# Iran
* **U.S.-Iran negotiations continue as Tehran weighs latest proposal:** Iran said it would respond to U.S. proposals on the war after the two sides reportedly discussed Tehran's nuclear program through indirect negotiations in New York this month, according to NBC News.
* Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi [said](https://substack.com/redirect/08e72c2d-285d-4900-9202-f352b3a5f94e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) "messages are being exchanged through mediators" and that Tehran was reviewing U.S. positions after presenting its seven-day plan. "We are currently reviewing the American perspectives, and I believe we will provide our response within the next few days," he said.
* Iran's proposal calls for the U.S. to begin lifting sanctions and unfreezing Iranian funds in exchange for reopening the Strait of Hormuz, with nuclear negotiations taking place separately later. The Trump administration, however, wants any agreement to address Iran's nuclear program and is not interested in an interim arrangement focused solely on Hormuz.
* Trump said his special envoy Steve Witkoff was working on an agreement but suggested a deal was not his preferred outcome. "I think the deal isn't really something that I want to do, but they're willing to offer us anything to stop," Trump said, while reiterating that Iran would "never have a nuclear weapon."
* **Pentagon ordered CENTCOM to prepare for possible resumption of major U.S. attacks on Iran, Axios reports:** The Pentagon [instructed](https://substack.com/redirect/f42f3d4a-257a-4d31-952d-574367b84b56?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) U.S. Central Command several days ago to complete preparations for a possible resumption of major combat operations against Iran, Axios reported. The directive did not set a date for strikes, and President Donald Trump has not made a final decision.
* If operations resume, U.S. and Israeli sources said they are expected to involve large-scale strikes on Iranian energy infrastructure and nuclear sites.
* A Pentagon official said the department's role was to "develop and present military options to the President," while a White House official said Trump continued to have "all options available at any time."
* Trump spoke with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Wednesday, their second call in a matter of days, following an Israeli national security meeting focused on Iran.
* **Multiple projectiles hit tanker off Qatar, casualties reported:** A tanker was struck by multiple projectiles off Qatar's northern coast on Wednesday, causing an unspecified number of casualties, according to the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations agency.
* The vessel was hit about 94km (58 miles) north of Madinat Al-Shamal.
* **International flights resume at Tehran airport after 40-day suspension:** International flights [resumed](https://substack.com/redirect/3d066733-8cdc-418b-a4b8-b619fbb83685?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) at Tehran's Imam Khomeini International Airport on Thursday following a 40-day suspension during the war, Iranian state broadcaster IRIB reported.
* The first international flight, operated by Iraqi Airways, arrived from Iraq's Najaf airport, with the service set to operate in both directions.
* **U.S. prepares release of last batch of Strategic Petroleum Reserve:** The U.S. is [preparing to release](https://substack.com/redirect/2d623e51-5c86-4218-837b-588be89a34d5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the last of the 172 million barrels it has pledged from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve to offset oil lost to the war on Iran. The Energy Department said the final batch, up to 40 million barrels from storage sites on the Texas and Louisiana Gulf Coast, will ship in November and December.
* The reserve held about 283 million barrels as of October 5, the lowest level since 1982, according to the Energy Information Administration. The barrels are loaned to oil companies, which must later return them with extra barrels as a premium.
* Meanwhile, G7 countries agreed Friday to release up to 100 million barrels of diesel and crude. At a meeting on Wednesday, EU countries broadly agreed that the release will "just enact previous commitments rather than requiring additional volumes," Bloomberg reported.

* **Emails show ICE cut training, dropped real-world scenarios** : The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) [shortened](https://substack.com/redirect/f87ed75d-7232-4295-ac0a-7843cee15054?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) training for local police making immigration arrests from four weeks in person to 40 hours of virtual instruction last year, according to emails obtained by watchdog group American Oversight through a FOIA request and reported by The Washington Post. The data was described as part of a "strategic line of effort" for fraud investigations.
* It separately got 50.6 million records from the Justice Department and more than 26,000 derived from U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services, prioritizing states including Texas, Pennsylvania, California, New Jersey, Minnesota, Michigan, Arizona, Florida, Georgia and Ohio.
* **GAO finds Trump administration illegally withheld over $1 billion at EPA and HHS** : The Government Accountability Office (GAO) [sent](https://substack.com/redirect/741ac68b-b8b7-4a21-9cb8-6fd12aafadd8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Congress two decisions Wednesday finding that the Trump administration illegally impounded funds in 2025 at the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) and the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS).
* At the EPA, the agency impounded funds when it terminated more than $1 billion in Community Change Grants, created in the Inflation Reduction Act for climate resilience and pollution reduction in disadvantaged communities. Congress later voted to rescind the money, but the GAO found the initial termination was still an impoundment.
* At HHS, the Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality disbursed less than 60% of its fiscal 2025 funds, leaving more than $78 million unawarded. Over the summer, it terminated more than 150 grants across 32 states, citing new priorities such as nutrition, autism, and "overmedicalization of children," likely following the lead and interests of HHS secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr.
* **WSJ: Ambassador Guilfoyle begged Trump donor to pay $100,000 credit card debt before confirmation** : **Kimberly Guilfoyle** , the U.S. ambassador to Greece, [asked](https://substack.com/redirect/c019f9fa-10ca-4d89-95f0-417ed335da88?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Republican donor and lawyer **Eric Deters** to wire $100,000 to her American Express account days before her July 9, 2025 confirmation hearing, according to the Wall Street Journal, citing Signal messages between the two. Deters declined the request, saying he would lose his wife if he paid.
* The Journal said the two communicated for months as Deters sought help with tax and legal problems and promised her up to $1 million if she used her Trump connections to help. She reportedly relayed messages she had sent to the IRS on his behalf and said she was lobbying the Justice Department. Deters said Guilfoyle told him that if he came up with the money, "I will be your Trump ride or die, forever and ever," but "she never came through on anything."
* In one message, he wrote, "I have paid you $300,000 over the years... I have not received one favor." Guilfoyle also told him to stop "papering all these things," saying "you'll literally cost me my ambassadorship."
* **Arizona Democratic congressional candidate reports sexual assault while repairing campaign signs** : **Bernadette Greene-Placentia** , the Democratic candidate challenging Republican Rep. **Abe Hamadeh** in Arizona's 8th District, told the Phoenix New Times she was struck on the head and [sexually assaulted](https://substack.com/redirect/685cc702-3e18-4130-9136-6e9dd764a4c6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) by two men in a parking lot around 2 a.m. on a Friday while fixing a damaged campaign sign.
* She reported the assault to the Maricopa County Sheriff's Office a little over two weeks later, telling deputies it happened near 99th Avenue and Bell Road in Sun City. The sheriff's office said the investigation is ongoing.

* **U.S. intercepts biodiesel shipments headed to Cuba:** The U.S. intercepted 90 shipments of biodiesel, worth nearly $3 million, headed to ENETEC S.A., a Havana-based fuel wholesaler the Treasury sanctioned in July, [according](https://substack.com/redirect/ca011ced-0a68-4670-ae73-f5c678454aa5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to officials from**** Homeland Security Investigations, Customs and Border Protection (CPB) and the Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security.

Tehran has denied any role in the alleged plot.
* The U.S. used RAF Fairford to deploy B-1 and B-52 bombers to the Middle East, with the UK authorizing the base's use for U.S. strikes against Iran. President Donald Trump said Sunday that U.S. bombers had been moved out of Fairford because of "some threats" to the base.
* **UK charges Royal Navy member with National Security Act offenses over alleged foreign-power link** : British police have [charged](https://substack.com/redirect/c66d48c0-c4c1-4107-ae93-a90c44c83b08?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Teddy Young, 24, a member of the Royal Navy, with two offenses under the National Security Act on accusations of working with a foreign power. Authorities allege that between November 2024 and May 2025 Young "obtained, copied, recorded or retained protected information, intending the conduct to benefit a foreign power," contrary to section 1 of the National Security Act 2023, and prepared to transfer it for that power's benefit. The foreign power has not been named, and UK police said the case is not related to the investigation into an incident near the RAF Fairford airbase last month.
* **U.S. bars Fiji-based Chinese service center director over corruption tied to China** : The State Department publicly [sanctioned](https://substack.com/redirect/bd55acd3-de70-4082-a42a-ce75fa4b4850?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Zhao Fugang, director of the Overseas Chinese Service Center in Fiji, saying he "abused his public position by paying bribes to Fijian citizens to advance China-based government, business, and criminal interests." The designation, announced Wednesday, makes Zhao and his immediate family "generally ineligible for entry into the United States," and the department said his actions "adversely affected U.S. interests in Fiji."

Government Accountability Office finds President Donald Trump's administration illegally withheld over $1 billion at the Environmental Protection Agency and the Department of Health and Human Services. Wall Street Journal: U.S. Ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle begged Trump donor to pay $100,000 credit card debt before confirmation. Arizona Democratic congressional candidate reports sexual assault while repairing campaign signs. International: Russian bomb attack kills at least 33 in Kramatorsk, one of the year's deadliest single strikes. Witnesses report Eritrean troops in Ethiopian town of Adigrat, Eritrea denies. Nigerian troops kill more than 25 militants in Borno; gunmen kill over 25 soldiers, 100 miners in Zamfara. Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro, wife expected to face new U.S. charges over alleged torture of detained Americans. Trump administration opens direct talks with Myanmar's military-installed government. Seventh man arrested over suspected RAF Fairford plot released on bail. UK charges Royal Navy member with National Security Act offenses over alleged foreign-power link. U.S. bars Fiji-based Chinese service center director over corruption tied to China. This is Drop Site Daily, our free news recap We send it Monday - Friday Palestine Killed and wounded in Gaza: Over the past 24 hours, four Palestinians were killed and 28 injured across Gaza, according to the Palestinian Ministry of Health. The total recorded death toll since October 7, 2023 is now 74,254 killed, with 175,306 injured. Since October 11, 2025, the first full day of the so-called ceasefire, Israel has killed at least 1,471 Palestinians in Gaza and wounded 5,189, while 836 bodies have been recovered. Israeli artillery fire kills woman, wounds several in Gaza City: A Palestinian woman was and several others wounded on Thursday by Israeli artillery fire northwest of Gaza City, WAFA reported. Israeli forces detain dozens of Palestinians as settler attacks continue across the occupied West Bank: Detentions: Israeli forces or subjected at least 95 Palestinians to field interrogations across the occupied West Bank overnight and Thursday morning. Nine former prisoners were arrested in Qalqilya and five in Jenin, while the mayor of Tuqu, Saqr Suleiman, was arrested after Israeli forces raided his home southeast of Bethlehem. Jericho: Israeli forces a two-storey home in Al-Duyuk Al-Tahta, west of Jericho. The demolition came two days after settlers established an outpost in the same area, where 15 Palestinian families were displaced in February following demolitions and settler attacks. Ramallah: Israeli settlers, protected by Israeli soldiers, attacked Palestinian olive harvesters in Abwein and forced them from their land in the eastern and northern areas of the town. The attacks came a day after settler violence in Burqa and the Ramin plain killed 44-year-old Ali Al-Bazari and wounded 16 others. Salfit: Four Palestinians were injured, including with fractures, when settlers farmers with sharp objects in Wadi Al-Shaer. Hebron: Israeli forces accompanied by settlers the Freedom Center for Culture and Folk Arts in Ramadin, confiscating a Palestinian flag and searching books in its library. Tulkarm: Israeli forces the home of Muayyad Shaaban, head of the Palestinian Colonization and Wall Resistance Commission, for the second time in two months, holding him, his wife and daughter in one room while searching the property. His two sons remain in Israeli detention, including one held for about a year and a half without trial. East Jerusalem: Israeli forces the home of Al-Eizariya municipal director Atta Jabr, beating him and leaving him requiring medical treatment, according to the Jerusalem governorate. Forces also extensively damaged four homes belonging to Jabr, his mother and his two brothers. Israeli authorities demolish Palestinian-owned shop in northern Israel: Israeli authorities a Palestinian-owned commercial building in the Arab town of Daburiyya in northern Israel on Thursday. The demolition comes amid increasing demolition orders targeting buildings in Palestinian communities inside Israel, often on the grounds of lacking construction permits. Restrictive planning policies make obtaining permits extremely difficult in many Palestinian towns, while some families have been forced to demolish their own homes to avoid heavy fines and demolition costs imposed by Israeli authorities. Israel returns body of Palestinian prisoner, continues to withhold 99 others: Israeli authorities returned the body of Palestinian prisoner Marwan Harzallah, from Al-Ain refugee camp in Nablus, the occupied West Bank, on Thursday, more than six months after he died in Israel's Megiddo Prison on March 28, 2026. Harzallah was arrested in January 2026 on allegations of "incitement." Palestinian prisoners' organizations his death was a direct result of being denied necessary medical treatment and healthcare, holding Israeli authorities responsible. Following the return of Harzallah's body, Israel continues to withhold the bodies of at least 99 Palestinians who died in its prisons, including 88 who have died since October 7, 2023. Israel blocks Gaza crossings three years into the genocide: Israel the anniversary of October 7 by halting aid and medical evacuations for more than 2 million Palestinians in Gaza, Eyad Amawi of the Gaza Relief Committee told Drop Site. Israel closed Gaza's only crossing, Kerem Shalom, for "many days," Amawi said. Israel's COGAT acknowledged closing the crossings on October 5 and 7. The closures "leave us die by the tightening siege" as winter nears, Amawi said. "No one intervened to stop this." Even when open, just 150 trucks enter daily, he said, far below the 600 trucks agreed upon in the ceasefire deal signed by Israel last year. More than 175,000 people have been injured, most needing long-term rehabilitation, Amawi said. Some 22,000 patients, including 5,600 children, are awaiting urgent medical evacuation, a Nasser Medical Complex doctor told Anadolu last week. Israel forces out most UK diplomats from occupied East Jerusalem: Most British diplomats are the UK consulate in occupied East Jerusalem following an Israeli move to shut down its operations in retaliation for British sanctions last month on illegal Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank. Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Saar said in a statement the consulate had "ceased to function as a consulate" and that the consul general and 19 other diplomats would leave Israel, while seven diplomats would be permitted to remain with what he called a "very limited scope of activity." UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband denied the building was closed and said it will now be known as the U.K. Mission, Jerusalem instead. He said the staff had been "temporarily withdrawn" because Israel had not provided necessary security assurances. Miliband reiterated Britain's position that East Jerusalem is occupied territory and said the remaining mission would continue to "work with the Palestinian people." NYT: Huckabee aide David Milstein suppressed and rewrote U.S. Embassy reports critical of Israel : David Milstein , 36, a top aide to Ambassador Mike Huckabee, has blocked or rewritten embassy actions critical of Israel since arriving in April 2025, according to a dozen people who work with him in Jerusalem and Washington, and 15 U.S. officials interviewed by the New York Times, which also reviewed dozens of cables and memos. The Times report highlights a late-March memo criticizing Israel's approval of a record number of settlements in the occupied West Bank, which Milstein reportedly nixed. Milstein also reportedly stymied reporting that Israel was failing to curb settler violence, and authored a cable praising Israel's "unprecedented new initiatives" under the title "Government Cracks Down on Escalating West Bank Violence." Milstein also helped quash a report on the deaths of Palestinian Americans, following a push by lawmakers led by Maryland Sen. Chris Van Hollen. The report initially found little progress and no charges filed related to the deaths, yet Milstein instead pushed for a letter saying Israel was handling the cases properly, sources said. As dozens of Palestinians were being killed near aid distribution sites run by the Gaza Humanitarian Foundation (GHF) in the summer of 2025, American diplomats in Israel drafted a cable warning against the GHF distribution system and said it risked more "mass casualty events." According to the Times, Milstein rewrote the cable to declare GHF's operation a success while overlooking the mass casualties. Yemen Three killed, 36 injured in attacks on Saudi airports: Three people were killed and 36 others injured in Ansarallah targeting Abha International Airport and King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh on Tuesday and Wednesday, according to Saudi Arabia's General Authority of Civil Aviation. Both airports sustained material damage. The Saudi-led coalition claimed it destroyed the ballistic missile launch platform in Sana'a used in the Riyadh attack while it was being prepared for another imminent attack on Saudi Arabia. Loud explosions were reported in Riyadh on Thursday, according to AFP. Ansarallah warns workers to stay away from Saudi oil facilities it considers targets: Ansarallah workers on Thursday against remaining at Saudi oil facilities that the group considers potential military targets. "Our armed forces warn all employees, experts, engineers and workers at all Saudi oil facilities against being present in locations that represent targets for our forces, so as not to put their lives at risk, whether they have been targeted before or not," military spokesperson Yahya Saree said in a statement. Saree also renewed previous warnings to airlines, passengers and employees concerning airspace and airports that Ansarallah has threatened to target. Saudi-backed Yemeni forces and Ansarallah continue battle for territory around Bab al-Mandab: Fighting is continuing between Saudi-backed Yemeni forces and Ansarallah across southern and western Taiz as both sides make competing claims over control of strategic territory around the Bab al-Mandab Strait. Fighting was reported in Al-Shamayatayn, Al-Ma'afer and the southern and western Taiz countryside. Yemen's Saudi-backed army separately claimed it has carried out at least 2,103 operations against Ansarallah across multiple fronts, killing 1,860 fighters and destroying hundreds of pieces of military equipment and positions. The casualty figures could not be independently verified. Ansarallah military spokesperson Yahya Saree said the group targeted Saudi-backed forces and reinforcements near Bab al-Mandab with ballistic missiles, including at Al-Qawah camp in the Ras Al-Ara area, as well as positions south of Bab al-Mandab. He claimed the attacks killed and wounded dozens and caused fires at weapons storage sites. Ansarallah also claimed it shot down a Turkish-made Bayraktar Akinci armed reconnaissance drone belonging to Saudi Arabia over Taiz. The fighting displaced residents from rural areas of Taiz, while government authorities suspended classes and granted leave to public employees in districts they say have fallen under Ansarallah control, citing deteriorating security conditions. Turkey rules out troop deployment under Mecca defense pact: Turkey troops to carry out offensive operations under its mutual defense agreement with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan, Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan said Thursday. "The Mecca agreement requires parties to defend any member under attack. It is not an offensive pact," Fidan said, stressing that Turkish forces would not be sent into another country to conduct attacks. Fidan said military officials were assessing possible contributions to Saudi Arabia's defense, particularly air defence, electronic warfare and technical support. The three countries agreed Monday to activate their collective defense commitments and facilitate the rapid deployment of military capabilities to Saudi Arabia following Ansarallah attacks. Syria says it stands with Saudi Arabia but does not seek to "open new fronts": Syria it "stands firmly alongside Saudi Arabia against threats to its security and stability," while stressing that its policy is based on "stability, peace and cooperation, not opening new fronts," according to the Syrian Information Ministry. The statement came after reports that Damascus was considering providing military assistance to Saudi Arabia as fighting between Saudi-backed Yemeni forces and Ansarallah escalated. Iran U.S.-Iran negotiations continue as Tehran weighs latest proposal: Iran said it would respond to U.S. proposals on the war after the two sides reportedly discussed Tehran's nuclear program through indirect negotiations in New York this month, according to NBC News. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi "messages are being exchanged through mediators" and that Tehran was reviewing U.S. positions after presenting its seven-day plan. "We are currently reviewing the American perspectives, and I believe we will provide our response within the next few days," he said. Iran's proposal calls for the U.S. to begin lifting sanctions and unfreezing Iranian funds in exchange for reopening the Strait of Hormuz, with nuclear negotiations taking place separately later. The Trump administration, however, wants any agreement to address Iran's nuclear program and is not interested in an interim arrangement focused solely on Hormuz. Trump said his special envoy Steve Witkoff was working on an agreement but suggested a deal was not his preferred outcome. "I think the deal isn't really something that I want to do, but they're willing to offer us anything to stop," Trump said, while reiterating that Iran would "never have a nuclear weapon." Pentagon ordered CENTCOM to prepare for possible resumption of major U.S. attacks on Iran, Axios reports: The Pentagon U.S. Central Command several days ago to complete preparations for a possible resumption of major combat operations against Iran, Axios reported. The directive did not set a date for strikes, and President Donald Trump has not made a final decision. If operations resume, U.S. and Israeli sources said they are expected to involve large-scale strikes on Iranian energy infrastructure and nuclear sites. A Pentagon official said the department's role was to "develop and present military options to the President," while a White House official said Trump continued to have "all options available at any time." Trump spoke with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Wednesday, their second call in a matter of days, following an Israeli national security meeting focused on Iran. Multiple projectiles hit tanker off Qatar, casualties reported: A tanker was struck by multiple projectiles off Qatar's northern coast on Wednesday, causing an unspecified number of casualties, according to the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations agency. The vessel was hit about 94km (58 miles) north of Madinat Al-Shamal. International flights resume at Tehran airport after 40-day suspension: International flights at Tehran's Imam Khomeini International Airport on Thursday following a 40-day suspension during the war, Iranian state broadcaster IRIB reported. The first international flight, operated by Iraqi Airways, arrived from Iraq's Najaf airport, with the service set to operate in both directions. U.S. prepares release of last batch of Strategic Petroleum Reserve: The U.S. is the last of the 172 million barrels it has pledged from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve to offset oil lost to the war on Iran. The Energy Department said the final batch, up to 40 million barrels from storage sites on the Texas and Louisiana Gulf Coast, will ship in November and December. The reserve held about 283 million barrels as of October 5, the lowest level since 1982, according to the Energy Information Administration. The barrels are loaned to oil companies, which must later return them with extra barrels as a premium. Meanwhile, G7 countries agreed Friday to release up to 100 million barrels of diesel and crude. At a meeting on Wednesday, EU countries broadly agreed that the release will "just enact previous commitments rather than requiring additional volumes," Bloomberg reported. Lebanon Israeli attacks towns across three southern Lebanon districts in continued violation of "ceasefire": Tyre (Sour): Israeli artillery Wadi Zibqin on Thursday and shelled Mansouri earlier in the morning. Wadi Zibqin was also shelled overnight, according to Lebanon's National News Agency. On Wednesday evening, Israeli warplanes struck Mansouri. Bint Jbeil: Israeli forces the outskirts of Hadatha and Bra'shit overnight. On Wednesday, artillery and heavy machine-gun fire targeted Hadatha, while Israeli warplanes struck Bra'shit and the area between Bra'shit and Kounine. Nabatieh: Israeli warplanes Kfar Tibnit twice within less than 15 minutes on Wednesday evening. Hezbollah receives $200 million from Iran for displaced Lebanese, Reuters reports: Hezbollah $200 million from Iran last month to provide assistance to Lebanese families displaced by Israel's war on Lebanon, two people with direct knowledge of the transfer told Reuters, though the U.S. disputed that the transfer took place. A Hezbollah official confirmed that funds had been secured and said a distribution plan would be announced in the coming days, but did not identify the source. Hezbollah leader Naim Qassem said last month that the group would contribute to housing thousands of displaced people using "available resources and donations." The U.S. rejected the account. State Department spokesperson Tommy Pigott said the money "is not there" and accused Hezbollah of "trying to save face with fake stories about cash influxes from Iran," while the Treasury Department said Tehran was "running out of money and ways to move money." U.S. News NY Fed survey: Americans worse off than last year, expect higher inflation: The New York Fed's monthly Survey of Consumer Expectations, released Wednesday, found consumers inflation to be higher a year from now, and more households reported being worse off than a year ago. The survey polls a rotating panel of about 1,300 household heads. Senate nominee Ken Paxton privately blames Iran war, gas prices for campaign troubles : In audio from a closed-door Washington fundraiser last month, obtained by Axios, Texas Republican Senate nominee Ken Paxton donors and lobbyists his campaign is being dragged down not by tariffs but by "the war, it's gas prices, it's diesel." He complained that "when it's over $6 per gallon for diesel... people are feeling the pinch," that fuel costs drive up food prices, and that affordability is "by far our biggest problem" and why "we're having a hard time with numbers." Separate audio obtained by The New York Times and Politico had Paxton saying the Republican Midterm Convention in Dallas last month headlined by Trump "dropped our numbers," and that campaign control is "all coming... from D.C." Recent polls show Democratic nominee James Talarico narrowly leading in the race. Emails show ICE cut training, dropped real-world scenarios : The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) training for local police making immigration arrests from four weeks in person to 40 hours of virtual instruction last year, according to emails obtained by watchdog group American Oversight through a FOIA request and reported by The Washington Post. A February email from an ICE official to current acting ICE head David Venturella and former acting ICE head Todd Lyons said instruction on immigrant classifications and removal charges would be "truncated" at the request of unnamed individuals, and that real-world scenario training was eliminated altogether. ICE amassed tens of millions of voter records in sweeping fraud hunt, documents show : Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) tens of millions of voter records, explored undercover investigations of voter registration groups, and considered feeding state election data into a deportation-targeting system, Democracy Docket reported, citing documents obtained through a FOIA request by Democracy Forward. Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) reportedly obtained 48.4 million voter records from "independent sources of information" connected to Heather Honey , an ICE adviser who first came to public attention for denying the results of the 2020 election. The data was described as part of a "strategic line of effort" for fraud investigations. It separately got 50.6 million records from the Justice Department and more than 26,000 derived from U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services, prioritizing states including Texas, Pennsylvania, California, New Jersey, Minnesota, Michigan, Arizona, Florida, Georgia and Ohio. GAO finds Trump administration illegally withheld over $1 billion at EPA and HHS : The Government Accountability Office (GAO) Congress two decisions Wednesday finding that the Trump administration illegally impounded funds in 2025 at the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) and the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS). At the EPA, the agency impounded funds when it terminated more than $1 billion in Community Change Grants, created in the Inflation Reduction Act for climate resilience and pollution reduction in disadvantaged communities. Congress later voted to rescind the money, but the GAO found the initial termination was still an impoundment. At HHS, the Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality disbursed less than 60% of its fiscal 2025 funds, leaving more than $78 million unawarded. Over the summer, it terminated more than 150 grants across 32 states, citing new priorities such as nutrition, autism, and "overmedicalization of children," likely following the lead and interests of HHS secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. WSJ: Ambassador Guilfoyle begged Trump donor to pay $100,000 credit card debt before confirmation : Kimberly Guilfoyle , the U.S. ambassador to Greece, Republican donor and lawyer Eric Deters to wire $100,000 to her American Express account days before her July 9, 2025 confirmation hearing, according to the Wall Street Journal, citing Signal messages between the two. Guilfoyle reportedly wrote, "It won't show up anywhere if you wire money to American Express. Please," and on July 3 texted, "Honey please I need you to get this done for me today." Deters declined the request, saying he would lose his wife if he paid. The Journal said the two communicated for months as Deters sought help with tax and legal problems and promised her up to $1 million if she used her Trump connections to help. She reportedly relayed messages she had sent to the IRS on his behalf and said she was lobbying the Justice Department. Deters said Guilfoyle told him that if he came up with the money, "I will be your Trump ride or die, forever and ever," but "she never came through on anything." In one message, he wrote, "I have paid you $300,000 over the years... I have not received one favor." Guilfoyle also told him to stop "papering all these things," saying "you'll literally cost me my ambassadorship." Arizona Democratic congressional candidate reports sexual assault while repairing campaign signs : Bernadette Greene-Placentia , the Democratic candidate challenging Republican Rep. Abe Hamadeh in Arizona's 8th District, told the Phoenix New Times she was struck on the head and by two men in a parking lot around 2 a.m. on a Friday while fixing a damaged campaign sign. She reported the assault to the Maricopa County Sheriff's Office a little over two weeks later, telling deputies it happened near 99th Avenue and Bell Road in Sun City. The sheriff's office said the investigation is ongoing. 📥 Have a tip on Capitol Hill? Email DC Correspondent Julian Andreone at Julian@dropsitenews.com Other International News Russian bomb attack kills at least 33 in Kramatorsk, one of the year 's deadliest single strikes: A Russian bomb attack on the eastern Ukrainian city of Kramatorsk at least 33 people and wounded 18 on Thursday, authorities said, in one of the deadliest strikes this year. Police said two city buses were operating on the street at the time. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said the attack targeted a bus stop. The region's governor ordered the cities of Kramatorsk and Sloviansk to halt public transport following the attack. Separately, on Thursday morning, drone strikes on Kyiv killed three people and wounded 14, according to the city's mayor. Witnesses report Eritrean troops in Ethiopian town of Adigrat, Eritrea denies: Two residents of the northern Ethiopian town of Adigrat Reuters they saw two trucks carrying dozens of Eritrean soldiers on Wednesday morning, identifying them by off-white camouflage uniforms; a third resident said relatives also saw them. If confirmed, it would be the first sign of Eritrean troops on Ethiopian soil during the conflict between the federal government and a rebel alliance that began on September 23. Eritrea's Information Minister denied any military presence in Ethiopia, calling the accounts part of a plan to justify a "war of aggression" against Eritrea. Eritrean soldiers fought alongside Ethiopia in the 2020-2022 Tigray war. Last week, the two countries terminated diplomatic relations after Ethiopia accused Eritrea of backing the rebel alliance headed by the Tigray People's Liberation Front. Nigerian troops kill more than 25 militants in Borno; gunmen kill over 25 soldiers, 100 miners in Zamfara: Nigerian special forces killed more than 25 Islamic State-aligned militants as they an assault from four directions on Tuesday night at Kukawa, Borno State, near Lake Chad, a military official cited by Reuters said. 14 bodies of those militants were recovered, and six AK-47s seized. Military sources said some soldiers died without giving details, and a Civilian Joint Task Force member said more than three of its members were killed. Separately, heavily armed bandits on motorcycles overran a military camp in the Maru area of Zamfara State on Oct. 5, killing at least 25 soldiers, three eyewitnesses and a military source told Reuters, who each counted 25 bodies. The gunmen then attacked a gold mining pit on Tuesday where about 1,000 people were digging, killing at least 100, according to a village head and victims' relatives. Trump administration opens direct talks with Myanmar 's military-installed government: The Trump administration has direct talks with Myanmar's military-installed government, reversing Washington's post-2021 coup policy of isolating the generals, Reuters reported. The Naypyidaw meeting reportedly aimed to secure the release of American businessman Adam Castillo, detained at Yangon airport on June 11 and later freed. The U.S. is seeking to shut down Myanmar-based "scam hubs" that have defrauded Americans of billions, and may also seek control over Myanmar's rare-earth deposits, though those mostly lie in territory held by rebel ethnic militias fighting the military. House Democrats, including Rep. Gregory Meeks, who sits on the Foreign Affairs committee, condemned the rapprochement, calling it "contrary to both our values and our interests U.S. intercepts biodiesel shipments headed to Cuba: The U.S. intercepted 90 shipments of biodiesel, worth nearly $3 million, headed to ENETEC S.A., a Havana-based fuel wholesaler the Treasury sanctioned in July, to officials from** Homeland Security Investigations, Customs and Border Protection (CPB) and the Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security. CBP said that it spotted the shipments in early September leaving Port Everglades in Florida and from the Port of Houston. Authorities seized 71 storage tanks holding about 500,000 gallons at Port Everglades and 19 shipments of about 120,000 gallons in Houston, citing suspected violations of U.S. sanctions. The agencies did not name the exporters or say whether anyone has been charged. Cuba faces chronic fuel shortages and blackouts that have disrupted water pumping for roughly 3.5 million people, along with hospitals, transport and food storage. Maduro, wife expected to face new U.S. charges over alleged torture of detained Americans: Detained Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro and his wife, Cilia Flores, are to face new criminal charges in the U.S. over allegations that Americans detained in Venezuela were tortured, a U.S. official briefed on the investigation told Reuters, with the charges possibly coming as soon as Thursday. The couple was abducted by U.S. forces in Caracas on January 3 and brought to New York on drug trafficking charges, to which they have pleaded not guilty. The trial is set for June 1, 2027. Washington accused Maduro's government of holding Americans as leverage for concessions such as sanctions relief, including five oil executives freed in 2022 and two former Special Forces members freed in 2023, both in prisoner swaps. Seventh man arrested over suspected RAF Fairford plot released on bail: A 22-year-old British man arrested on suspicion of preparing "terrorist acts" in connection with a suspected plot targeting RAF Fairford was r, UK police said. Seven men have now been arrested and bailed in connection with the investigation, with no charges brought. U.S. officials alleged that Iran was behind a possible plot targeting the base, while British Prime Minister Andy Burnham said there were "strong indications" of Iranian involvement. Tehran has denied any role in the alleged plot. The U.S. used RAF Fairford to deploy B-1 and B-52 bombers to the Middle East, with the UK authorizing the base's use for U.S. strikes against Iran. President Donald Trump said Sunday that U.S. bombers had been moved out of Fairford because of "some threats" to the base. UK charges Royal Navy member with National Security Act offenses over alleged foreign-power link : British police have Teddy Young, 24, a member of the Royal Navy, with two offenses under the National Security Act on accusations of working with a foreign power. Authorities allege that between November 2024 and May 2025 Young "obtained, copied, recorded or retained protected information, intending the conduct to benefit a foreign power," contrary to section 1 of the National Security Act 2023, and prepared to transfer it for that power's benefit. The foreign power has not been named, and UK police said the case is not related to the investigation into an incident near the RAF Fairford airbase last month. U.S. bars Fiji-based Chinese service center director over corruption tied to China : The State Department publicly Zhao Fugang, director of the Overseas Chinese Service Center in Fiji, saying he "abused his public position by paying bribes to Fijian citizens to advance China-based government, business, and criminal interests." Friends,

The momentum we are feeling on the ground keeps building. This past weekend, we had one of our strongest weekends yet, knocking more than 18,500 doors across every corner of this district. We also had the honor of having NYS Comptroller Tom DiNapoli and Congressman Jim Himes out on the trail with us.

We also had the privilege of welcoming former Congresswoman Gabby Giffords to Nyack this week to talk about community safety and gun violence prevention. Community safety means ensuring we have commonsense gun safety laws in place, that our law enforcement has the resources to keep our communities safe, and ensuring that we have proper mental health resources for our communities.

Community safety also means ensuring families have the basics, like food. I was honored to join Gabby Giffords and Mayor Joe Rand in visiting Soup Angels, bringing over donations from our campaign event.

The stakes of this race could not be higher. We are fighting for an America that once again works for working people.

Our path to victory is clear, but in a race this close it is going to take everything we’ve got over these next 26 days. That means knocking doors, making calls, and talking directly to voters about what is at stake in this election: affordable groceries, lower utility costs, and quality healthcare accessible to everyone. Let’s go finish what we started. With gratitude and fire,
Cait Conley

# **BREAKING: DNC Sues Trump for Illegally Using Millions of Taxpayer Dollars on Partisan Political Propaganda**
---
| _Trump administration continues to misuse public funds for a purely partisan, political propaganda TV ad campaign as Trump and GOP approval plummets_
Today, the DNC [sued](https://us.list-manage.com/19_HS0LLbGd?e=d6c5c7d7ec&c2id=d01ae369e8fbc8d507a43d27c2d1769e) Donald Trump and his administration over their illegal use of taxpayer dollars to fund political propaganda ads in a desperate attempt to boost Republicans’ plummeting approval ratings ahead of the midterms. The DNC’s lawsuit accuses President Trump of personally directing this illegal, blatant violation of the statutory ban on the use of taxpayer dollars for political propaganda, and directing U.S. Customs and Border Protection to carry out this partisan advertising campaign. The illegal use of government funds for campaign-style ads is a clear violation of the [Congressional ban](https://us.list-manage.com/70LPIfZeISw?e=d6c5c7d7ec&c2id=d01ae369e8fbc8d507a43d27c2d1769e) on the use of appropriated funds for “publicity or propaganda purposes,” and allows Republican campaigns and committees to spend on other political activities.

Trump is illegally using funds that were transferred to an [account](https://us.list-manage.com/18r8mvln1DS?e=d6c5c7d7ec&c2id=d01ae369e8fbc8d507a43d27c2d1769e) for commemorative events — including memorials for Americans killed in the line of duty and commendation ceremonies — to attempt to boost his dismal approval numbers. Even [Republicans](https://us.list-manage.com/sKAoYPP02ra?e=d6c5c7d7ec&c2id=d01ae369e8fbc8d507a43d27c2d1769e) are [admitting](https://us.list-manage.com/ti26TnF7dOd?e=d6c5c7d7ec&c2id=d01ae369e8fbc8d507a43d27c2d1769e) that the more Trump centers himself in the midterms, the [worse](https://us.list-manage.com/FZYkxktmSFx?e=d6c5c7d7ec&c2id=d01ae369e8fbc8d507a43d27c2d1769e) Republican polling gets.

Not only is this a misuse of public funds for illegal political propaganda, but it is also [overwhelmingly unpopular](https://us.list-manage.com/ho6hMmBDuDr?e=d6c5c7d7ec&c2id=d01ae369e8fbc8d507a43d27c2d1769e) with the American people, including four out of five Republicans, and [prominent](https://us.list-manage.com/74uIOYx1fc0?e=d6c5c7d7ec&c2id=d01ae369e8fbc8d507a43d27c2d1769e) [members](https://us.list-manage.com/WzODJqRmSjg?e=d6c5c7d7ec&c2id=d01ae369e8fbc8d507a43d27c2d1769e) of Trump’s own party.
_As the[DNC](https://us.list-manage.com/19AtbHGuWkA?e=d6c5c7d7ec&c2id=d01ae369e8fbc8d507a43d27c2d1769e) [once again](https://us.list-manage.com/14__peQsEZ6?e=d6c5c7d7ec&c2id=d01ae369e8fbc8d507a43d27c2d1769e) [takes](https://us.list-manage.com/4IKHeCczbhy?e=d6c5c7d7ec&c2id=d01ae369e8fbc8d507a43d27c2d1769e) Trump to court over his illegal actions, **DNC Chair Ken Martin released the following statement: **_ | |
> “Donald Trump is misusing millions of taxpayer dollars to fund pure propaganda ads in a last-ditch attempt to save Republicans in November — so we’re suing him. As gas and grocery costs rise and his approval numbers continue to crater, this president has stooped to taking money from a fund intended for memorials for Americans killed in the line of duty to promote his failed policies. Americans deserve better than to have their hard-earned tax dollars used for Trump’s illegal schemes.”
> ###

name: Defenders of Wildlife
subject: Heroes in American Conservation: Capture this Photographer’s Story! Meet Ansel Adams
body:
Meet American Conservation Hero Ansel Adams
Meet American Conservation Hero Ansel Adams
| [](https://support.defenders.org/s/6126947/38SyG9Xl)
---
| | |
---
#
|
---
#
_The Tetons and the Snake River (1942) Grand Teton National Park, Wyoming © Ansel Adams. National Archives and Records Administration, Records of the National Park Service_
---
#
Meet American Conservation Hero Ansel Adams
---
| | |
---
#
#### **_Who is he?_**
When it comes to photography of our National Parks and wilderness areas, Ansel Adams (1902-1984) paved the way. He is best known for his high-contrast black-and-white photos of the American West. He captured iconic scenes of Yosemite, Glacier, Grand Teton and Yellowstone for the National Park Service in the 1940s.
#
Adams was also an advocate for the preservation of wilderness. While he didn’t (intentionally) create photographs specifically for environmental advocacy, his art nonetheless inspired others to become advocates themselves.
#
|
---
| | |
---
#
#### **_How did Adams help wildlife?_**
Adams’ photographs of National Parks like Yosemite and Kings Canyon often inspired others to want to protect these places, which also serve as important habitat for wildlife.
#
Adams also advocated for the protection of large, intact wilderness. He even collaborated on a photo-book which was distributed to politicians to help [**pass the Wilderness Act.**](https://support.defenders.org/s/6126948/38SyG9Xl) The wilderness areas created under this act protect millions of acres of habitat for hundreds of species.
#
The current administration is attempting to weaken longstanding policies that keep these swaths of protected habitat from roadbuilding, off-road vehicle use, mountain biking and development activities. Defenders of Wildlife is advocating to continue the protection of wilderness areas and uphold the integrity of the Wilderness Act.
#
|
---
| | |
---
#
#### **_How can you become a conservation hero?_**
Adams used his photography to inspire others to care about the beautiful places he saw. You too can [**capture a few wildlife photography tips**](https://support.defenders.org/s/6126949/38SyG9Xl) or hone your talents to promote the protection of wildlife and wild places that inspire you. You can even [**become a Wildlife Defender**](https://support.defenders.org/s/6126950/38SyG9Xl) to advocate for wildlife protection policies in your state and federally.
#
|
---
###
_A note on our Heroes in American Conservation series: Our country has a long and complex history, populated with high-profile figures whose views may have been complicated or divisive in their time as well as ours. We present these conservationists in the interest of creating a greater understanding of the roots of the American conservation movement, and to inspire you to make your own contribution to ongoing conversations about how we preserve our wild world._
#

House Minority Leader Jim Durkin wears a mask during the legislative session. (Credit: Justin L. Fowler of The State Journal-Register)
By Jacqueline Garretson, Opinion Contributor

It has been more than five years since COVID-19 changed our lives, but for many Illinois families, the consequences never really went away. Businesses were lost, jobs disappeared, families drained their savings, and children lost something that can never be replaced: their childhood.

Under Gov. JB Pritzker, Illinois families spent 1,155 days under some form of COVID-era emergency declarations, restrictions, and executive orders. For more than three years, Illinoisans lived with a government response that repeatedly changed how we worked, learned, worshiped, and interacted with one another. What was initially presented as a temporary emergency became a prolonged period of government intervention that affected every aspect of daily life.

But the people who paid the greatest price were often those with the least ability to understand what was happening: our children.

In a matter of weeks, their entire world changed. Schools closed. Sports disappeared. Friends became faces on computer screens. Birthday parties, school activities, graduations, and family gatherings were canceled.

Children were isolated during some of the most important developmental years of their lives, and many are still dealing with the consequences. Parents watched their children struggle with anxiety, fear, isolation, and academic setbacks. Years later, many students remain behind where they should be.

Yet instead of confronting those failures honestly, Illinois continues to lower the bar and declare victory.

Changing standards doesn’t change reality. If students are struggling academically, lowering expectations doesn’t make them more successful. It simply makes the numbers look better. Parents in Illinois deserve an education system that tells the truth about where our children are; not one that manipulates the measurements to make politicians look more successful.

And here’s the part voters should not forget: Democrats weren’t the only politicians who supported the COVID response. Some Republicans did too.

Former Illinois House Republican Leader Jim Durkin, along with others in the party, supported restrictions, defended the status quo, and failed to challenge the system, while families and businesses were suffering. Politicians shouldn’t be more concerned with maintaining political relationships than standing up for the people who elected them.

Today, former Illinois House Republican Leader Jim Durkin has endorsed JB Pritzker for Governor. Durkin’s endorsement is a political nod of approval to the very Governor whose COVID policies left such a lasting mark on Illinois families.

To me, that endorsement says a lot. It is a reminder that the old political establishment has never been as divided as the party labels would have us believe.

There was, however, a Republican who was willing to challenge the governor when it mattered: Darren Bailey.

I watched Darren stand on the House floor and tell the political establishment that the path Illinois was taking was wrong. He challenged Pritzker’s restrictions. And while others were willing to go along to get along, Darren was willing to stand up and fight.

You don’t have to agree with Darren Bailey on every issue to recognize the importance of political courage.

Leadership isn’t simply agreeing with the majority when it is politically convenient. Sometimes leadership means standing alone and telling the people in power that they have gone too far.

The next crisis will eventually come. When it does, Illinois families need leaders who understand that government power must have limits and that emergency authority cannot become a blank check.

We need leaders who will listen to parents, protect children, support small businesses, and question the establishment when its power becomes unchecked.

Because those 1,155 days weren’t just numbers on a calendar. They represented birthdays that couldn’t be celebrated, seasons that couldn’t be played, businesses that never reopened, jobs that disappeared, and children who lost years they will never get back.

Five years later, Illinois families are still picking up the pieces. They don’t need politicians to tell them everything worked. They know it didn’t.

They deserve the truth. They deserve accountability. And they deserve leaders who will put people before politics.

That leader is Darren Bailey.

Hi Peter, We talk a lot about the impacts of abortion bans and the fight over mifepristone, and those battles are real and ongoing. But I want to make sure you know about some of the other ways this administration is attacking reproductive healthcare right now, because the hits are coming from every direction at once.
1. **RFK Jr. is blocking teen pregnancy prevention funding.** Congress passed $100 million for these programs, but less than 1% of that money has been spent this past fiscal year. HHS is obligated to spend that money, as directed by Congress – it’s not optional.

As an OB-GYN, I’m extremely concerned about what this means for young people, their safety, their health, and their well-being. I’m leading more than 90 House and Senate Democrats in demanding that RFK Jr. release this funding immediately. We will not let this administration put teenagers’ lives at risk to advance their dangerous agenda.

2. **There’s an estrogen patch shortage here in the U.S. and no plan to fix it.** Estrogen patches help millions of women manage menopause symptoms, and for many of them, these patches are life-changing. It is unacceptable that the FDA has no plan to address this shortage, so the House Democratic Women’s Caucus is demanding answers from RFK Jr. immediately.

3. **Trump’s FDA pick won’t say that birth control _isn’t_ abortion.** His nominee to lead the FDA, Heidi Overton, holds extreme anti-science views on vaccines and reproductive health. During her confirmation hearing, Senator Patty Murray asked her directly whether she agrees with the Trump administration falsely calling an IUD an abortifacient, and she wouldn’t answer.

Trump wants to hand control over Americans’ access to birth control, vaccine regulations, food safety, and prescription drug supply to someone who refuses to acknowledge that birth control is not abortion. She is completely unfit for the role, and the Senate must reject her nomination.

Every one of these attacks is part of a coordinated effort to restrict access to reproductive healthcare for every American, and they will continue unless we flip the House and put real guardrails on this administration.

I've been warning you about New Hampshire for months. I told you this race was being ignored. I told you the map didn't work without it. I told you Sununu was a uniquely dangerous opponent.
Now I need you to look at this.
The University of New Hampshire released a new poll. _And for the first time this entire campaign,**John Sununu is ahead. 45 to 43.**_

subject: A heartfelt request.
disclaimer_text: Paid For By Alex Vindman for Florida
body:
Eugene Vindman deserves your support.

[](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/evfc-em-oct26?refcode=em261008-av-ken-burns&refcode2=1147_3892029_wWzud1&akid=1147%2E3892029%2EwWzud1)
---
Hi, it’s Ken Burns. I am coming to you with a heartfelt request:
[**If you, like me, are deeply concerned about the future of our democracy and the rising tide of extremism, I urge you to join me in supporting Eugene Vindman’s reelection campaign for Congress today.**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/evfc-em-oct26?refcode=em261008-av-ken-burns&refcode2=1147_3892029_wWzud1&akid=1147%2E3892029%2EwWzud1)
As a filmmaker, my life’s work has been dedicated to capturing pivotal moments in American history — moments that have shaped our nation’s identity and spirit. I’ve documented our country navigating through its darkest hours and emerging stronger and understanding the profound consequences of these moments.
Throughout my career, I’ve seen our nation evolve in countless ways, but one constant remains: our democracy, the cornerstone of our republic, and the essence of what it means to be American.
Yet, at this very moment, our democracy faces an unprecedented challenge — a critical inflection point. We are at a juncture where our very rights and freedoms are threatened.
The stakes have never been higher. Our democracy stands at a crossroads — and this moment requires leaders who will unify our country in defense of the very fabric of our nation — no matter political party or affiliation. Eugene Vindman is one of those leaders.
I first met Eugene and Alex nearly 40 years ago, when I interviewed the Vindman twins and their grandmother for a documentary about the meaning of the Statue of Liberty. It was shortly after they fled Soviet Ukraine and sought refuge in the United States as children.
[](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/evfc-em-oct26?refcode=em261008-av-ken-burns&refcode2=1147_3892029_wWzud1&akid=1147%2E3892029%2EwWzud1)
Their father came to the U.S. with $759 in his pocket, three children, and a dream of giving them a better life. And through hard work and perseverance, they achieved just that.
Eugene’s story is the embodiment of the American dream. He is a Ukrainian immigrant, an Army Veteran, and a lifelong defender of our democracy. He’s a good man — one who has devoted himself to defending our country with courage, selflessness, and resilience, even at his own expense.
Eugene has never failed to hold our leaders accountable — no matter their party. But right now, not only is our government baselessly retaliating against him through an investigation aimed at removing him from Congress, but he is being attacked relentlessly by the far right, all because he has never failed to hold our leaders accountable.
We need to keep people like Eugene in Congress — leaders who continue to stand up for our democracy and represent the true spirit of America.
So it would mean a lot to me if you could support his reelection campaign today to help keep him fighting for us in the People’s House.
[**Can you please contribute $25 or whatever you can afford to Eugene Vindman’s campaign for Congress today? I am asking because it is critical.**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/evfc-em-oct26?refcode=em261008-av-ken-burns&refcode2=1147_3892029_wWzud1&akid=1147%2E3892029%2EwWzud1)

name: Ahlers for Governor
subject: Brighter Days are Ahead for South Dakota
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY DAN AHLERS FOR GOVERNOR
body:
|
---
| |
---
| | | |
---
| | | |
---
| |
---
DWU Town Hall

Thank you to everyone who attended the town hall at the McGovern Library at DWU in Mitchell. It was an honor speaking at the library named after the incredible Sen. George McGovern whose decades of work is still helping millions of people around the world.

I especially appreciated the students who took the time to share their concerns, ask thoughtful questions, and talk about the issues that matter to them. I’m grateful to everyone who joined us for the conversation.

| | |
---
| |
---
NSU Town Hall

Thank you to the NSU College Democrats for hosting this town hall in Aberdeen. We had great conversations about the importance of monitoring water usage and supporting conservation efforts in South Dakota. Having a healthy and protected environment is crucial to our farmers, national parks, and our overall quality of life.

It’s truly inspiring to see young people stepping up to the issues we face in South Dakota. Young folks who ask important questions and make their voices heard are vital to a thriving South Dakota.

| | | |
---
| |
---
Dakota Days & Gypsy Days

It’s homecoming season! This is one of my favorite times of the year because it gives me an opportunity to meet many different people from various communities across the state. I always find myself falling behind the float as I stop to visit with South Dakotans. These events demonstrate the vibrancy of our state and the unique identities of our towns and cities.

I am excited to walk in the DWU and SDSU parades later this month and meet more of South Dakota!

| | |
---
| |
---
Pumpkin Festival

After D-Days in Vermillion, my Lt. Governor pick Steve McCleerey and I headed to Webster for the Pumpkin Festival and parade!

I love these small-town celebrations. It’s wonderful seeing an entire community come together to celebrate their roots and the future ahead. There was a great crowd, lots of energy, and a very warm welcome. Events like this are a great reminder of what makes our South Dakota communities so special.

| | | | SDPB Governor’s Debate

---
[| |
---](https://us.list-manage.com/19izT2Eyh0D?e=cee7b49c04&c2id=3adc23449cf80dcda430cceaf3c4b05d)
Thank you to South Dakota Public Broadcasting for hosting a debate between me and my opponent Larry Rhoden. We had a robust conversation about affordability, investing in local businesses, properly funding education and making healthcare more accessible.

I spoke about the missed opportunities to bring good paying jobs to South Dakota and my plans to strengthen small businesses right here in our state. I laid out my proposal to bring down the cost of childcare by creating a childcare tax rebate program. I offered solutions to protect our farmers and ranchers.

What did my opponent offer? Sticking with the status quo.

Ask yourself, are you better off than you were a year ago, five years ago, ten years ago? South Dakotans deserve a leader who will listen to your concerns and find solutions. [If you missed the debate, click here to watch it on SDPB.](https://us.list-manage.com/17SvGG9JjgL?e=cee7b49c04&c2id=3adc23449cf80dcda430cceaf3c4b05d)

| | | | Early Voting Has Begun!

---
Five votes. That’s all it took to change the outcome of a Sioux Falls mayoral election. After the 2026 runoff, the final margin between Christine Erickson and Jamie Smith was just four votes after the recount. Think about that for a moment. Five more people voting for Jamie Smith could have changed who became mayor of South Dakota’s largest city.

It is easy to believe that one vote doesn’t matter, especially when we look at the thousands of people who vote in an election. But elections aren’t decided by thousands of people voting as one person. They are decided one vote at a time.

Your vote matters, and sometimes it matters more than you could ever imagine. Your vote also matters because it is one of the most important ways, we can hold our elected leaders accountable. South Dakota has a long history of giving citizens the power to make laws and change our Constitution directly through ballot measures. But for years, our elected leaders have tried to make that process more difficult when they don’t like the results. We are seeing that fight again this year with Amendment L, which would change the requirement for constitutional amendments from a simple majority to 60% of the vote. I believe South Dakotans should have the right to make decisions about our state, not have that voice made harder to exercise by the people we elect. Democracy works best when more people participate, not when we put more obstacles between citizens and their government.

We can change all of this in November. We can elect leaders who listen to the people, respect the will of voters, and understand that government is supposed to work for all South Dakotans. But it starts with showing up. Our polling numbers are really good. If Democrats show up, we can win this race. We can change our priorities, change the direction of our state, and make sure every South Dakotan has a voice in their government. Be the difference. Make your voice heard. Vote.

On the Campaign Trail

| |
---
Here’s the latest from across the campaign trail—key updates, major milestones, and where we’re headed next.

| | | | | |
---
What’s Next
