clean_body: A Method for Investigating the Promise and the Practice of Public Authority | | ---|---|--- | | | Forwarded this email? ? for more A Method for Investigating the Promise and the Practice of Public Authority | | | Oct 8 | | | | | | | | | | | | | | ---|---|--- You are being fed a diet of finished conclusions. Every day, a thousand voices--pundits, campaign advertisements, political organizations, and curated news feeds--offer you a version of reality that feels complete. They tell you what happened, who is responsible, what a candidate believes, and what you should think about it. The work of citizenship begins when you decide to look for yourself. We the People did not surrender political judgment when we elected representatives. A vote authorizes someone to exercise public authority; it does not transfer our responsibility to understand what that authority is being used to do. That does not mean you must know everything. It means that when something matters, you know how to proceed. It Starts With a Lead Consider a candidate running for governor. In 2025, Byron Donalds spoke favorably about the growth of data centers in Florida, describing the power demands as critical and arguing that Florida should embrace the opportunity rather than run away from it. Then the landscape changed. In May 2026, a Change Research survey of 1,593 likely Florida voters found that 79 percent opposed AI data centers. In July, H.R. 9777--the Protecting Ratepayers Act--was introduced in Congress. The proposal would require large data centers to provide their own off-grid power and water rather than shifting those infrastructure costs to the public. Florida had also enacted SB 484, establishing requirements for large-load customers and addressing ratepayer costs and water permitting. Now there was something worth investigating. Not because a poll proves a candidate wrong. Not because a new bill proves a candidate changed. And not because a campaign statement tells us what the government can actually do. The question is: What does the record actually show? Follow the Question The first step is to separate the pieces. What did the candidate actually say? When did he say it? What happened afterward? What did the government actually do? What authority belongs to the office being sought? Those questions matter because political language and government action are not the same thing. A candidate can support a policy without having the authority to enact it. A law can exist without proving that a particular candidate caused it. A federal proposal can be politically relevant to a gubernatorial campaign without being an action available to a governor. So the record must be followed before the judgment is made. This is where the work changes. You are no longer asking, " What am I being told about this candidate?" You are asking, " What have I established about this candidate?" Do Not Fill the Gap The temptation comes when the record leaves a space. Donalds's earlier position on data centers was clear. The later record showed a more restrictive policy direction. But the record did not establish why the change occurred. Perhaps the candidate's position changed. Perhaps the policy became more specific. Perhaps the political circumstances changed. Perhaps the candidate always intended something different from what the earlier statement suggested. The evidence does not answer that question. So we do not fill the gap. That is one of the most important disciplines in citizen investigation: An unanswered question is not permission to invent an answer. The same discipline applies when the subject is law, regulation, authority, or political motive. The Second Lead The same candidate offered another opportunity to test the method. In July 2026, Donalds called for a "full and immediate pause" on Flock and similar automated license plate reader systems, raising constitutional and privacy concerns and warning against a surveillance state. After the Florida Sheriffs Association responded, his position moved toward working with sheriffs and police chiefs to establish parameters and limitations rather than maintaining an outright pause. Again, the sequence can be established. Again, the explanation cannot simply be assumed. And again, the question of authority matters. Who controls the use of these systems? What authority belongs to the governor? What belongs to sheriffs? What belongs to police chiefs, counties, municipalities, or state agencies? In August, the Florida Department of Transportation revoked general-use permits for automated license plate readers in state highway rights-of-way. That is a government action. It is evidence. But it is not automatically evidence of gubernatorial control. The work is to follow the authority to its source. When the Record Does Not Give You a Label You may reach the end of an investigation without a satisfying political label. You may not be able to prove that a candidate is a "flip-flopper." You may not be able to prove that a candidate was acting from political calculation. You may not be able to prove that a campaign promise will become government action. That is not failure. It is an honest finding. A disciplined citizen can say: This is established. This is supported by the record. This is contradicted. This remains unresolved. And then make a judgment. The point of investigation is not to manufacture certainty. It is to make your judgment answerable to what you can actually establish. The Vote Is Still Yours Eventually, investigation reaches a point where evidence gives way to judgment. That is the purpose of the work. You decide what matters to you. You decide how much uncertainty you are willing to accept. You decide what a candidate's record means in relation to the American Kitchen Table--your family's freedom, security, prosperity, and future. Before you make that decision, ask one more question: What remaining fact or contradiction could actually change my judgment? If there is one, investigate it. If there is not, you may be ready to decide. The judgment is yours. The Election Is Not the End A vote does not end citizenship. If the candidate you supported wins, the promise still has to become practice. If the candidate you opposed wins, the government still belongs to you. Watch what happens next. Watch the laws, the budgets, the votes, the appointments, the administrative actions, public statements, reports, and the decisions that follow. Compare what was promised with what is being done. When something changes, begin again. A new matter becomes a new question. A new question begins the work again. DECODE. AUDIT. STRIKE. SECURE. That is how accountability becomes a continuing practice rather than an election-season event. Political Sovereignty Political sovereignty is not freedom from influence. It is not distrusting everyone. It is not investigating everything. It is accepting responsibility for your own political judgment. You can listen to experts. You can read journalism. You can use voter guides. You can listen to candidates and people you trust. But you should know what you are trusting, why you are trusting it, and when something matters enough to look further. That is the difference between receiving a conclusion and possessing the means to examine one. The citizen comes first. Bring It Back to the Kitchen Table The work eventually returns to the place where politics becomes real: the American Kitchen Table. Not the campaign stage. Not the television panel. Not the social-media argument. The table where people think about their families, their work, their homes, their communities, their freedom, their security, and the future they are leaving behind. The question is simple: Does this make the family at the American Kitchen Table more free, secure, and prosperous? That is not a slogan. It is a measure. And the citizen is the one who must apply it. The Work Continues The full Citizen 's Candidate Investigation Manual takes this work further, providing the complete method, procedures, evidence practices, worksheets, and working examples. It will be available free to American Kitchen Table Founding Members. The link to the Manual will be posted here shortly. You do not need to know everything before you begin. You only need to notice when something matters, ask the next question, and do the next thing the matter requires. The citizen comes first. The responsibility remains. The work continues. DECODE. AUDIT. STRIKE. SECURE. Strike the Root. Secure the Table. Join the Working Table What are you investigating? Have you encountered a candidate, claim, law, or public decision that made you want to look closer? Tell us what caught your attention-- and what you found when you followed the record. | | ---|---|--- Receipts Narratives built from evidence. We follow the record, examine the exercise of public authority, and bring what we find back to the American Kitchen Table. Evidence. Accountability. Sovereignty. Uncompromised. Distribute the Intel The method works when citizens use it. Share this Field Guide with someone who wants to look beyond the finished conclusion and investigate for themselves. Stop accepting the finished conclusion. Start asking the next question. Join the community of citizens putting evidence, judgment, and civic responsibility back in their own hands. The Citizen 's Candidate Investigation Manual takes the work beyond this Field Guide-- with the complete DECODE -> AUDIT -> STRIKE -> SECURE method, evidence practices, working examples, and reusable investigation tools. Available free to American Kitchen Table Founding Members. American Kitchen Table This is journalism from the ground up, built on the Sunshine Mandate. We open the records. We follow the evidence. We publish the Receipts. The work belongs to the citizen. Strike the root. Secure the table. Because a man is worth his hire. Become a Table Member. body:
[1]Justice Democrats

Hi Peter,

Today, I have a big announcement: after nearly ten years, I’m stepping
away as Justice Democrats’ Executive Director to become President of JD’s
Board and a senior advisor to the organization.

Leading Justice Democrats has been the honor of a lifetime,
Peter. Looking back, it all
started in 2016 after Bernie Sanders shocked the establishment and mounted
a historic challenge for the Democratic presidential nomination. And then
— the Democratic establishment lost against Donald Trump.

It was clear that the party insiders and political machine could not be
trusted to protect our democracy or fight for our people. We needed a new
path forward — so we built it ourselves. I cofounded and helped build
Justice Democrats alongside others who gave our all to the progressive
movement Bernie brought together.

Starting in 2017, we set out to change Congress by recruiting and electing
a diverse slate of working people who share real-life experiences with the
communities they represent. And we have, thanks to support from thousands
of people like you who share our vision and have pitched in your time,
effort, and grassroots donations along the way.

Over the course of the last four election cycles, we’ve made JD the
leading progressive electoral organization recruiting working-class
candidates to Congress.

From electing the Squad in 2018 and later expanding it, to taking on the
rise of coordinated Super PAC spending from groups like AIPAC, Crypto, and
AI, to weathering some tough re-election losses, to ushering in the
organization’s most successful cycle to date this year — it was an honor
to go through it all with you,
Peter.

The success of the progressive primary movement over the last decade would
not have been possible without the work we’ve done and led at Justice
Democrats. Now, as we look ahead to 2027 and 2028, our successes demand we
continue growing in new directions.

While I proudly step into my new role, I’m thrilled to share that Reverend
Hodari Williams will take up the mantle as Justice Democrats’ new
Executive Director.

Hodari brings his fierce and decades-long commitment to justice, deep
executive leadership experience, and organizing background to take our
work and mission to build power for working people into our next chapter
of growth.

The JD team and I first met Hodari while speaking to community leaders in
Georgia for our 2026 candidate recruitment process. He was recommended by
other local leaders as a justice-minded force for good who could provide
insights into struggles Georgians on the ground were facing, along with
the organizing work communities like his were leading locally.

It quickly became clear that he could just as likely be a formidable
congressional candidate alongside our other recruits, like Darializa Avila
Chevalier and Donavan McKinney, but he resisted our overtures for
candidacy.

When we began searching for our new Executive Director, we thought his
leadership of historically Black congregations across the country,
organizing in the South, and developing community-based initiatives to
build independent power for the working class was exactly the perspective
we needed.

Under Hodari’s leadership, JD aspires to build on this cycle’s successes
and expand our movement’s growth in the South and among communities
historically taken for granted by the Democratic establishment — the same
communities who fostered the struggles for economic justice and freedom
our work builds upon today.

We’ve also been on the forefront of every big financial story from the rise of Bitcoin and MRNA vaccines to robotics and artificial intelligence – just to name a few.

But today, I’m breaking the [ biggest story of my career ](https://links.dpt.deepregimetrends.com/u/click?_t=4a25883d9bf54436b571b8aa9717dcca&_m=5f1b442c65fa4fd093c542b5728605ce&_e=FYyM-Oe5_CVbIi7D4gT5rtktVX1WCAmYxatkUNX2k4mEWaziiqw2pd78iQ-NLF_ZId1wnMH4PfruCBeWWpmh3aAteO5RDX70AvT_8tS0Ud1hyB6hkYUGmKATIvRbO2V4T6tP9QN3ntc6AZMGXcU9aN7Lz7RpTz6mXmwq56tTArKRCzD8ldNzjVxb_VcnlRL5zlLWEONT8P7HZy7ro2kQyzWh6Fs0qiXjJDxzgMjVR86QZ3_Byay0n4hvyY8HWSOhyKKLSljEt8GBYOeQv7jTFGHrgoCZGPoO3I4D1bmw20zKWb2BIWPQcKUrAi9jYbKXbcvg022KpmsTqWfryRGoxrz_Y4phPPVo5YpHFpzj-dUdImX0WaMy5xX7G7rDHzqo5GWxJ241V8ybVrNeGCYCsT6WpDenLKMwMLEJwkZrE8I1mtIftq6pvDN26BHdHK9BmlKNE1LrObk6kFbt-KJMVL_e8fV4Ua3K2KtYw0aNX6fCWsCVQgLB7ny8sRMjeocUUHSPSBbEVJOk-W-5Rp8AnpRPfigVlo58zVP01YZ-G2E%3D) ...

And as you’ll discover today, the aftershock of this event could “reset” not just your personal wealth, but the entire U.S. economic system:

How you work, how you vote, how you protect and build your wealth... it’s all being turned upside down by what one famous Stanford economist says is:
_“The biggest change ever... bigger than electricity... bigger than the steam engine.”_
[ Yet almost nobody is prepared for it. ](https://links.dpt.deepregimetrends.com/u/click?_t=4a25883d9bf54436b571b8aa9717dcca&_m=5f1b442c65fa4fd093c542b5728605ce&_e=FYyM-Oe5_CVbIi7D4gT5rtktVX1WCAmYxatkUNX2k4mEWaziiqw2pd78iQ-NLF_ZId1wnMH4PfruCBeWWpmh3aAteO5RDX70AvT_8tS0Ud1hyB6hkYUGmKATIvRbO2V4T6tP9QN3ntc6AZMGXcU9aN7Lz7RpTz6mXmwq56tTArJ35I1b-8yLsLFpzD7GUGrLsYiH8e7Q3XhEYZRfxWgcavmVsMmNtyPGq3ZwSEgZDS5UZv3b6msNcDjxZkoUpG4vEOBLcxpSR_I50qmILJOlxvWYHbFzFHtlSMwRyhK9kYL6bgR7MlQAz3wr5ki04rQZB_Ltw9aHPTJAO3gnFWmMLnVfd51Gt50LmSCUxgXzWcAPmscztdIMHUq2Ge0VqUJ83-v6kL0tYJyiJ6d9qLW3PDH3x9L5bCDvn7qnT-vkf_AwMmMj5uDIHnFobxrKW0YDhgVzeiXJEjV4C6GB1EjrD5cW93JLtAIlKKk3JweMikjTnUh2-pEIsQJ4fY43-JoEb1glYlGV8D5P6uv_ajRJY7jYE1oh-XVWPEGok7PM2ok%3D) So, if you’ve been watching the chaos of the past year unfold, struggling to understand what it all means... you’re about to get many - if not all - of the answers you’ve been searching for.

And, most importantly, what it all means for you, your money, and your investment portfolio in the months ahead

Because as you’ll discover, everything from the government taking stakes in companies like Intel, Lithium Americas, and MP Materials.

To Trump’s strike on Venezuela... his deal with Greenland... his seemingly never-ending slew of executive orders... and increasingly centralized grip over the economy...

Case File No DRT-ED-1776 · Special File · The Turning Point
America Turned 250 This Year. It Also Hit a Turning Point Almost Nobody Is Talking About.
Washington owns stakes in 39 companies. Sixteen Nobel economists warn AI could be bigger than the Industrial Revolution. Hiring has stalled and voters are turning to radical alternatives. Separate stories, one shift, and it’s changing who wins.
Threat level 4/5 — Elevated
| | | | | | | | |
---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---
|
---
This year America turned 250. It also crossed into a period that looks less like the stable economy most of us grew up in and more like a turning point. The government is buying stakes in companies. AI is starting to take jobs. Voters are turning toward radical alternatives. Each of these stories gets covered on its own. Put them side by side and a single shift comes into view.
The evidence board
| | Three Shifts Happening at Once
---|---
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit A — the state as shareholder.** Washington now holds about $27.7 billion in stakes across 39 companies, including Intel, MP Materials and Lithium Americas. Policy is increasingly made through deals, stakes and executive orders.
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit B — the machine.** In July, more than 200 economists, researchers and executives, including 16 Nobel laureates, signed a letter warning that AI could bring an “unprecedented transformation of our economy, larger than the Industrial Revolution,” with risks of “large-scale job displacement.”
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit C — the paycheck.** The economy added just 29,000 jobs in September, and July was revised to a loss. Unemployment rose to 4.2%, and wage growth slowed to 3.0%, the slowest since 2021.
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit D — the ballot.** New York City elected a democratic socialist mayor, Zohran Mamdani, in November 2025. Anger about costs and jobs is reshaping politics on both sides.
Decoder
| | Why Economists Are Sounding the Alarm
---|---
| | “Larger than the Industrial Revolution.”— Open letter signed by 16 Nobel-winning economists and others, July 2026
---|---
What it says
AI could change the economy more than anything before.
What it means
**Our theory:** the Industrial Revolution created vast wealth, and it also upended who held power, how people worked and which businesses survived. If AI moves faster, the winners and losers will be sorted faster too. And a government that already owns stakes in companies will have more say than ever in who comes out on top.
The pattern
| | Turning Points Reward the Prepared
---|---
| | 1776
---
A new political order
Built new institutions and new fortunes, and ended old ones.
| | 1870s–1900s
---
The industrial age
Railroads, steel and oil made a new class of winners almost overnight.

Contender A
| | Oil
---|---
| EVIDENCE
---
Still the backbone of transport, and Utah’s Uinta Basin is a growing oil region. But oil is rarely burned for power in the U.S. anymore. It moves cars and trucks, not data centers.
Contender B
| | Natural Gas
---|---
| EVIDENCE
---
Today’s go-to fuel for new power plants. The catch: wait times for the large gas turbines that power plants need now stretch for years, and gas prices swing with every global supply shock.
Contender C
| | Uranium
---|---
| EVIDENCE
---
Big Tech is betting heavily on nuclear: Meta signed for up to 6.6 GW by 2035, and Microsoft is restarting Three Mile Island. But the first restart isn’t due until 2027, and most new reactors won’t run until the 2030s.
Contender D
| | Geothermal
---|---
| EVIDENCE
---
The first utility-scale next-generation geothermal plant came online in southern Utah in September. Rigs there have drilled one well to more than 19,000 feet of total depth in 21 days, reaching rock at 460°F.

---
| [ ](http://clicksp.shawnharrisforcongress.com/f/a/MT1ghLd_yF_7Z59OU6Biew~~/AAPPABA~/Pqym_WQeQVSYmHBPdiDzbMloli1pgl_p9YXEpJkV819swp_sEG0T5eZKF3RLju7-R1vgi210oRhn90m-mxiqcTLt40sZTlYmiByqXkxXLRjND1jTwKPvldhNGP-sEgn-dvowXDXqLd0C4qtWq_3CcdpkJ4LLIGKXGGghfh4ozNVlrUBzCvDL8edW4L1ET6qWgbzRjTfRqGlJ7k9yWmsRr0SijxNFuEZQRjTOW304OnQnR3XpvMRTF6jn4HLlHd6oZbu2Noid8ByvtBcq3ihP7su7bSdnB_wvZQPep358wOUxtjhVwSrbXrHMbsJ9h7Ei)

If you tuned in, you saw two completely different visions for Georgia: a campaign powered by working families who clock in every single day, and _Rick Jackson, who proved just how hopelessly out of touch he really is._ When asked a direct question about Georgia's economy and rising costs, Rick actually claimed, "My plumber drives a Mercedes." | | Friend, **Minnesota counties are on the hook for millions in costs that Washington used to cover.****_
_****Hard work should be rewarded**. In northern and central Minnesota, people want to work and build a stable life, but good-paying jobs aren’t always available when people need them. That’s why we need a safety net that is there when Minnesotans experience hard times. The One Big Beautiful Bill Act changed SNAP eligibility**** and work requirements while also shifting more of the program’s cost onto states and counties**.** Additionally, the Act removed SNAP work-rule exemptions that protected veterans and young adults who aged out of foster care. **Pete Stauber voted for that legislation.**
---
---
**Beginning October 1, Minnesota counties are now taking**** on more of the administrative costs of SNAP.** [The Minnesota Department of Children, Youth and Families estimates that change alone will mean **$32 million less** in federal funding for counties](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/140985088/652154548/1577714892?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjMvMS8xMjQ3MDYiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiZWI3MTMzNWYtNWRjMy1mMTExLWJmNWItMDAwZDNhNGZiZTgzIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=tdzYHyy4zq7HhvQ46ifaRZqnAbKQjleK-Eq_JJS3teQ=&emci=4ec392ef-57c3-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbe83&emdi=eb71335f-5dc3-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbe83&ceid=1071883). And the bill goes beyond food assistance. It made major changes to Medicaid**** that Minnesota DHS estimates could eventually leave as many as [**140,000 Minnesotans without health coverage.**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/140985090/652154551/-420048894?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjMvMS8xMjQ3MDYiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiZWI3MTMzNWYtNWRjMy1mMTExLWJmNWItMDAwZDNhNGZiZTgzIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=tdzYHyy4zq7HhvQ46ifaRZqnAbKQjleK-Eq_JJS3teQ=&emci=4ec392ef-57c3-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbe83&emdi=eb71335f-5dc3-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbe83&ceid=1071883) **Trina Swanson believes that we must recast the safety net around the realities that Minnesotans actually face**. We can value hard work while recognizing that sometimes people need support during difficult times. Everyone deserves the chance to be fed, housed, healthy, and secure while they get back on their feet. **As your Congresswoman, Trina will ensure support is available when Minnesotans need it most. ** **If you agree that Minnesota families shouldn’t pay the price for Washington’s choices, donate to Trina’s campaign to bring security back to Minnesotans.**

clean_body: Benefits reduced and Minnesota counties pay for it.| | | | | Friend, Minnesota counties are on the hook for millions in costs that Washington used to cover. Hard work should be rewarded. In northern and central Minnesota, people want to work and build a stable life, but good-paying jobs aren’t always available when people need them. That’s why we need a safety net that is there when Minnesotans experience hard times. The One Big Beautiful Bill Act changed SNAP eligibility** and work requirements while also shifting more of the program’s cost onto states and counties. Additionally, the Act removed SNAP work-rule exemptions that protected veterans and young adults who aged out of foster care. Pete Stauber voted for that legislation. Beginning October 1, Minnesota counties are now taking** on more of the administrative costs of SNAP. . And the bill goes beyond food assistance. It made major changes to Medicaid** that Minnesota DHS estimates could eventually leave as many as Trina Swanson believes that we must recast the safety net around the realities that Minnesotans actually face. We can value hard work while recognizing that sometimes people need support during difficult times. Everyone deserves the chance to be fed, housed, healthy, and secure while they get back on their feet. As your Congresswoman, Trina will ensure support is available when Minnesotans need it most. # [](https://act.fordfornevada.com/go/12?t=1&akid=1051%2E127862%2ES_hU7c)
In a few hours, I'm walking onto the debate stage to make my case for why our campaign is the one to move Nevada forward.
I've been preparing for this for weeks. But honestly, I've been preparing for it my whole life.
I grew up in a family where some nights, dinner was a stale candy bar my dad brought home from Safeway. I raised my first son as a single dad at 21, and government programs like WIC and food stamps helped us stay afloat.
So when I talk about rent, groceries, and health care tonight, I'm not reading off a briefing. **I know what it feels like.**
That's the message I'm taking to that stage: Nevada families are doing everything right, and they deserve a governor who's fighting for them.
But a debate only lasts a couple of hours. What matters is what comes after: **whether we have the resources to carry this message to every corner of the state before early voting starts.**

A large crowd of supporters gathered Tuesday outside the Sherburne County Government Center for a _**Protect the Polls**_ Community Action Event and press conference, publicly releasing an August 19, 2026, letter request that the U.S. Department of Justice deploy Civil Rights Division election monitors to Benton, Sherburne, and Stearns Counties for Minnesota's 2026 general election.
As stated in the DOJ letter, _**" We bring to your attention the following specific concerns regarding election administration in this jurisdiction that warrant federal oversight. During the 2024 election season, the St. Cloud area (Stearns, Sherburne, and Benton Counties) experienced a reported pattern of voter influence and intimidation that were followed by investigations by both the Stearns County Sheriff's Office and the Sherburne County Sheriff's Office."**_

---|---|---
The _**Protect the Polls**_ event reviewed documented problems from the 2024 election in the greater St. Cloud area, the county's refusal to assign a Sergeant-at-Arms during early voting, and the need for the August 19th request for Department of Justice monitors. Speakers included Brenda Hansen and Linda Schultz of the Sherburne County Community Action Team, a local chapter of Restore Minnesota; Rev. Dale Witherington, Chief Steward of Restore Minnesota; and Zach Freimark, Executive Director of America First Policy Institute-Minnesota.
After the outdoor program, the parties testified at the public comment period of the Sherburne County Commissioners where they asked the Board to welcome federal monitoring and to support the cooperation needed for monitors to observe early in-person voting, which begins Friday, October 16, and on Election, November 3.
Hansen restated findings from the 2024 early voting period at the Sherburne County Auditor/Treasurer's Office. Surveillance video captured an individual casting two separate ballots on the same day, and a search warrant and the Sheriff's investigation confirmed that double vote. Stearns County documented related problems in the same election. Election workers, in sworn interviews, described coordinated groups--often five to ten or more voters at a time--brought in by the same individuals posing as translators and assistants. Workers reported voters who appeared confused about the oath, questions about proof-of-residency documents, and ballots allegedly handled or completed by others.
"I have viewed the video of these women voters at the Sherburne County Courthouse. Words do not fully convey the shock of watching it," Hansen said. "More than a century of work went into the Nineteenth Amendment. That right belongs to the woman casting the ballot. It does not belong to the person who drives her there, stands over her, handles her paperwork, or completes the ballot for her. Vulnerable voters need protection. Election workers need support. That is the issue."
Schultz reminded the Commissioners of the efforts that had been made to secure the polling place prior to the request to the Department of Justice. The group first appeared before the Board in open forum on May 19, 2026, citing Minnesota Statute 204C.06, Subdivision 5, which allows election judges to appoint a Sergeant-at-Arms to keep order. On June 4, members of the Sherburne County Community Action Team met with Auditor Rupp, with County Administrator Bruce Messelt facilitating, and were told the request would not be granted. They returned to the Board on June 16 and again on August 4. Each time, they were told the decision rested with the Auditor, and the request was denied.
"This Board has heard this request before, and the local answer has always been no," Schultz said. "May 19, June 4, June 16, August 4--the dates are on the record. We cited a statute the county already has, a Sheriff's investigation the county already possesses, and a video the county has already seen. When every local door closes, asking for federal monitors is not an escalation. It is the next lawful step."
Dale Witherington then publicly reviewed the August 19 letter that he and Gary Tonsager sent to Jesus A. Osete, Principal Deputy Assistant Attorney General for the Civil Rights Division. As stated in that letter, _**" The presence of Civil Rights Division monitors would serve both to protect the voting rights of all eligible citizens and to ensure that election administration in this jurisdiction meets the standards required by federal law. The deployment of monitors would also promote public confidence in the integrity of the election process and help deter potential violations before they occur."**_
[](https://substack.com/redirect/3105d0fc-d23c-4035-b570-ba84c11d3c0c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
As summarized by Witherington, "Every eligible voter should be able to vote freely, privately, and according to his or her own conscience. Women, elderly individuals, and others who need assistance should be able to receive that help without surrendering their independence. Today I am publicly renewing our August 19 request, and I am asking this Board to welcome federal monitoring."
Freimark outlined the historical placement of DOJ election monitors in prior election As stated by Freimark, "The request for Department of Justice election monitors is not out of the ordinary. In 2024, DOJ deployed staff monitors to 86 jurisdictions across 27 states, including the State of Minnesota. Their primary role is to observe and document activities in the polling places. They are there to be a support mechanism for location election officials."
As concluded by Benda, "This matter is timely and pressing as early in-person voting begins October 16. The three-county request is already before the Civil Rights Division, and we hope to receive notice of where DOJ monitors will be placed very soon. The _**Protect the Polls**_ action group is**** requesting that Sherburne County officials Welcome Civil Rights Division staff monitors in Sherburne County polling places and at early-voting sites from October 16th through November 3rd. We are also requesting that Benton and Stearns Counties also welcome Department of Justice monitors into their polling locations".

| It happened because thousands of people stepped up with a dollar here, $5 there, and whatever they could afford to invest in this campaign.

| | Good Afternoon Team Demuth!
**Zoom Meeting**
I want to remind everyone that we will have our regularly scheduled grassroots volunteer meeting tonight at 8:30 PM. We will talk about volunteer efforts and how you can help the campaign! This meeting will be a little bit shorter than normal.
I have placed the link below. Once you click the link, you will be taken into a waiting room. I will let you into the meeting from there.
https://us06web.zoom.us/j/87316568944
**Right Insight**
If you are interested in joining Right Insight and our efforts in knocking on doors and calling phones, please contact Caleb Jungling. This is a fantastic way to help out our campaign. **Even five minutes of phone calling, or door knocking just your neighbors goes an incredibly long way!**
All of you that have previously been volunteers already have accounts. Simply download the app and sign in using the email address you received this message at. You will be sent a six-digit code to verify your identity, then you’re all logged in and ready to roll!For door knocking, we are utilizing a feature called Near Me. This will allow volunteers to go out and door knock houses that are nearby them. That list will change as you move around, so you can use it anywhere.Calls will be broken down by Congressional District. When we add you to Right Insight, we will assign you to calls specific for your area so you are talking to people who you may know, or share more common issues. Most of you will likely see all of them until we are able to organize you into Congressional district teams, so please just call into the CD you are from. For example, if you are from CD 1, call CD1.**If you do login and are told you do not have an account, please fill out the form below and we will get you added!**[ Sign up for a Right Insight Account.](https://us.list-manage.com/pkAyMKHPB98?e=422536b04e&c2id=3f96188058f7a1407b5cde0c924e7fd7)Both calls and door knocking projects are live and ready for volunteers. We are very excited to get everyone started! If you have technical questions or are unsure of how to get started, please call Caleb at 612-300-4202 or email him at Caleb@mngop.com**Events** We will be updating our volunteers on upcoming events. For example, we have an upcoming Phone Bank Potluck at our Burnsville office this Saturday. From 2:00 PM to 6:00 PM this Saturday, volunteers will bring a dish to share and call for Team Demuth and other Republican candidates! For more information on this event, please call Mary Ander (612) 599-0240 or email at andermary96@gmail.com

| | Friend, **Minnesota counties are on the hook for millions in costs that Washington used to cover.****_
_****Hard work should be rewarded**. In northern and central Minnesota, people want to work and build a stable life, but good-paying jobs aren’t always available when people need them. That’s why we need a safety net that is there when Minnesotans experience hard times. The One Big Beautiful Bill Act changed SNAP eligibility**** and work requirements while also shifting more of the program’s cost onto states and counties**.** Additionally, the Act removed SNAP work-rule exemptions that protected veterans and young adults who aged out of foster care. **Pete Stauber voted for that legislation.**
---
---
**Beginning October 1, Minnesota counties are now taking**** on more of the administrative costs of SNAP.** [The Minnesota Department of Children, Youth and Families estimates that change alone will mean **$32 million less** in federal funding for counties](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/140985724/652156753/1577714892?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjMvMS8xMjQ3MDYiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiNjMwYjMxNzktNWZjMy1mMTExLWJmNWItMDAwZDNhNGZiZTgzIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=_Kl1p_132QDQVbEuR--lysnfTKMof6tELuSfwcFHlyc=&emci=07f75e22-58c3-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbe83&emdi=630b3179-5fc3-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbe83&ceid=1071883). And the bill goes beyond food assistance. It made major changes to Medicaid**** that Minnesota DHS estimates could eventually leave as many as [**140,000 Minnesotans without health coverage.**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/140985726/652156756/-420048894?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjMvMS8xMjQ3MDYiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiNjMwYjMxNzktNWZjMy1mMTExLWJmNWItMDAwZDNhNGZiZTgzIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=_Kl1p_132QDQVbEuR--lysnfTKMof6tELuSfwcFHlyc=&emci=07f75e22-58c3-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbe83&emdi=630b3179-5fc3-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbe83&ceid=1071883) **Trina Swanson believes that we must recast the safety net around the realities that Minnesotans actually face**. We can value hard work while recognizing that sometimes people need support during difficult times. Everyone deserves the chance to be fed, housed, healthy, and secure while they get back on their feet. **As your Congresswoman, Trina will ensure support is available when Minnesotans need it most. ** **If you agree that Minnesota families shouldn’t pay the price for Washington’s choices, donate to Trina’s campaign to bring security back to Minnesotans.**

clean_body: Benefits reduced and Minnesota counties pay for it.| | | | | Friend, Minnesota counties are on the hook for millions in costs that Washington used to cover. Hard work should be rewarded. In northern and central Minnesota, people want to work and build a stable life, but good-paying jobs aren’t always available when people need them. That’s why we need a safety net that is there when Minnesotans experience hard times. The One Big Beautiful Bill Act changed SNAP eligibility** and work requirements while also shifting more of the program’s cost onto states and counties. Additionally, the Act removed SNAP work-rule exemptions that protected veterans and young adults who aged out of foster care. Pete Stauber voted for that legislation. Beginning October 1, Minnesota counties are now taking** on more of the administrative costs of SNAP. . And the bill goes beyond food assistance. It made major changes to Medicaid** that Minnesota DHS estimates could eventually leave as many as Trina Swanson believes that we must recast the safety net around the realities that Minnesotans actually face. We can value hard work while recognizing that sometimes people need support during difficult times. Everyone deserves the chance to be fed, housed, healthy, and secure while they get back on their feet. As your Congresswoman, Trina will ensure support is available when Minnesotans need it most. I wanted to tell you a bit about what’s happening in the U.S. Senate race in Kansas right now:

Conventional wisdom has always held that this seat is out of reach – Kansas was a state you crossed off the list before you even looked closely. But not this year. People organizing on the ground there have known something the political class is only now catching up to: this race is real, and Adam Hamilton is the reason.

[Friend, Adam can win, and I hope you'll help him do it by donating to his campaign today.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/140985824/652156870/-540544497?amounts=10,25,50,100,250&refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk528&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjMvMS8xMjYxMjYiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiNjYwYjMxNzktNWZjMy1mMTExLWJmNWItMDAwZDNhNGZiZTgzIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=9dR2ZPdAHXEQJ7J-3h-TR-zSL5sVsNhGLVmQRZJC0Ho=)

One of the things I've found in public service is that the best leaders are often those who were serving and leading in another way, long before they ever thought about running for office.

Adam is a fifth-generation Kansan and a pastor who has spent 36 years building a church around a simple belief: faith isn't something reserved for Sunday morning, it's something you carry out into the world. He's spent years bringing Republicans, Democrats, and Independents together around practical solutions, from a mobile dental clinic for kids who needed care, to food distribution for families going without.

That work is part of what led him to step forward. And it's just the kind of perspective we need more of in the United States Senate.

Sen. Roger Marshall has taken a different path. While families struggle to afford the basics, he voted to cut SNAP benefits for kids and hand billionaires a massive tax break. A New York Times investigation even found his medical practice sued patients over bills as low as $101.
Adam isn't a career politician. He's a pastor and a public servant who understands that politics isn't about left versus right – it's about right versus wrong.

Now, he has an extraordinary opportunity in a race that Republicans had assumed was safely theirs – and what happens next depends on whether his campaign has the resources to compete against outside spending and make sure Kansans hear what he has to offer.

I've seen a lot of races. One thing that experience teaches you is to pay attention when the political ground begins to move. Experts have shifted their view of this race, no longer rating it "Likely Republican," and a recent poll shows Adam with a two-point lead. But JD Vance has already traveled to Kansas to campaign for Sen. Marshall, and a super PAC is spending big to slow that momentum.

[**There is a real opportunity in Kansas. But opportunity only counts if we act on it. clean_body: This is a leader who deserves our support. | | | = Friend, I wanted to tell you a bit about what’s happening in the U.S. Senate race in Kansas right now: Conventional wisdom has always held that this seat is out of reach – Kansas was a state you crossed off the list before you even looked closely. But not this year. People organizing on the ground there have known something the political class is only now catching up to: this race is real, and Adam Hamilton is the reason. = | | = One of the things I've found in public service is that the best leaders are often those who were serving and leading in another way, long before they ever thought about running for office. Adam is a fifth-generation Kansan and a pastor who has spent 36 years building a church around a simple belief: faith isn't something reserved for Sunday morning, it's something you carry out into the world. He's spent years bringing Republicans, Democrats, and Independents together around practical solutions, from a mobile dental clinic for kids who needed care, to food distribution for families going without. That work is part of what led him to step forward. And it's just the kind of perspective we need more of in the United States Senate. Sen. Roger Marshall has taken a different path. While families struggle to afford the basics, he voted to cut SNAP benefits for kids and hand billionaires a massive tax break. A New York Times investigation even found his medical practice sued patients over bills as low as $101. Adam isn't a career politician. He's a pastor and a public servant who understands that politics isn't about left versus right – it's about right versus wrong. Now, he has an extraordinary opportunity in a race that Republicans had assumed was safely theirs – and what happens next depends on whether his campaign has the resources to compete against outside spending and make sure Kansans hear what he has to offer. I've seen a lot of races. One thing that experience teaches you is to pay attention when the political ground begins to move. Experts have shifted their view of this race, no longer rating it "Likely Republican," and a recent poll shows Adam with a two-point lead. But JD Vance has already traveled to Kansas to campaign for Sen. Marshall, and a super PAC is spending big to slow that momentum. = | | = Thank you, Pete | Adam Hamilton is a husband, father, pastor and fifth-generation Kansan. Now, he’s running for U.S. Senate as an independent-minded Democrat. Just like you, he’s tired of the chaos and corruption in Washington that is harming our farmers, raising costs at the checkout line and making critical health care services unattainable. He hears your concerns and is ready to get to work for you. Fellow Conservative: What's with liberals and our children? Every election cycle, Democrats tell us they're moderates. They talk about faith, decency, and "bringing people together." Then you look at the record, and you find the same thing again and again: when it comes to protecting kids, they look the other way. You've likely heard about **James Talarico** , the liberal candidate for U.S. Senate in Texas. He's a former seminarian who quotes Scripture on the campaign trail, but despite his attempts to wrap himself in Christianity, _**he voted against a bill to protect our children from sex-change surgeries, puberty blockers, and cross-sex hormones**_. So much for believing that we're all made in the image of God. Talarico even refused to oppose a bill banning sexual performances in front of minors, saying he didn't want any legislation to target the performers. He's more concerned about protecting drag queens than children in Texas. Now consider **Adam Hamilton** , the liberal candidate for U.S. Senate in Kansas. He's the founding pastor of one of the largest churches in America, and he wants Kansans to see him as a shepherd. But in November 2005, teenage boys at his church's sleep-away retreat reported that a man came into their cabin at night and touched them in their sleeping bags. A Kansas appeals court later found that camp leaders "were dismissive of their claims." The church ran its own internal review instead of calling the police. **_The next fall, the church sent the man back to the camp as a counselor._** The man was later convicted of sexual battery. Boys from Hamilton's church camp had to relive what happened to them on the witness stand. Hamilton now says he "absolutely" should have handled it differently.

This one is bizarre, disturbing, and honestly raises some serious questions about who's actually influencing Donald Trump.
Trump's niece Mary Trump is speaking out about his unusually close relationship with longtime aide Natalie Harp. And the more we learn about Harp's access to the president, the more concerned I get. Because this isn't just about gossip or weird personal relationships. It's about power, influence, and whether the president is getting anything resembling the truth.

* [**00:01:06**] Mary Trump weighs in on her uncle's relationship with Natalie Harp, and why Trump's increasingly isolated inner circle matters.
* [**00:03:30**] Trump's fixation on female staffers raises bigger questions as Americans struggle to pay their bills.
* [**00:05:30**] How much power does Natalie Harp really have? We dig into her extraordinary loyalty, influence, and new polling showing Americans want answers.

* [**00:09:39**] Senator Jon Ossoff calls out Trump's inner circle, and we break down why accountability and congressional oversight matter more than ever.

Look, I don't care about Washington gossip. I care about who's shaping the decisions that affect millions of Americans. body:
Eight years in, there is still so much work to do. | | Twenty-six days. That is all that stands between us and Election Day, friend. Right now, people are hurting. Costs are up. Friends,
Just a few days ago, something momentous happened that I wanted to share with you: **Former Kansas Republican Gov. Mike Hayden endorsed me for Kansas ' U.S. Senate seat over my opponent, Sen. Roger Marshall.**
Gov. Hayden's endorsement means so much to me because he believes in putting people over politics and delivering for working families, just as I do. Knowing he recognizes that I'm committed to fighting for real solutions for Kansans -- and that I will make listening to them a priority if I'm elected -- is an absolute honor.
_" I ran for office for the first time when I was only 28 years old because I felt the person representing my community in the legislature was failing to fight for the needs of our state," he said. "Today, I am endorsing Adam Hamilton for the U.S. Senate for the same reasons."_
His announcement comes just weeks after Republican former Gov. Bill Graves endorsed me, saying that Sen. Marshall had "turned his back" on Kansas.
I agree: Voting to slash the healthcare assistance that so many people in our state rely on is turning your back on your constituents. Supporting tariffs that drive up prices and make it harder for families to put food on the table and buy household essentials is, too. And not fighting for Kansas farmers, ranchers and small businesses -- well, so is that.
**Gov. Hayden understands that standing up for Kansans against the cruel and disastrous policies coming out of Washington might not be easy, but that doesn 't make giving in okay. Kansans deserve a leader who will put them ahead of Washington. If I'm elected, that's exactly what I'll do.**
Friends, Gov. Hayden's and Gov. Graves' endorsements are proof that the foundation of this campaign -- listening to folks, thinking critically about how to make their lives better and _fighting to do so even when it 's hard _-- is resonating with people across political parties.
And they aren't the only ones who think so:
💥 Kansas Gov. Laura Kelly gave me her endorsement
💥 Former Kansas Govs. Kathleen Sebelius, Mark Parkinson and John Carlin have all officially endorsed me
💥 Arch "Pond" Naramore, a lifelong Republican who ran against Sen. Marshall in the primary, has as well
Each of these people are supporting me not because of political party, but because they believe that leaders should fight for the people they represent -- and they know Roger Marshall isn't getting the job done.
But I'll be honest: As honored as I am to have their public support, there's one endorsement I want more than any other in the final stretch of this race:
_**Yours.**_
I'm running for U.S. Senate to make _your_ life better. To be a voice for _you_ in Washington. To be the true champion that _you_ deserve.
It would mean the world to me if you would add your name to endorse my campaign -- and affirm your belief that it's time for a leader who will open their heart to the people they're elected to represent, build bridges and stand up for their constituents amidst the chaos and corruption in Washington.
**[So I'm asking: Please, will you take a moment to officially endorse my campaign today?](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/8e46cd25-8456-4d38-8de7-83ae8d5d9347?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[ENDORSE ADAM HAMILTON](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/8e46cd25-8456-4d38-8de7-83ae8d5d9347?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Thank you for standing with me,
Adam

Elections have consequences. So do the Trump administration’s exhaustive efforts to undermine them.
Voters will be confident in their choices, but less certain whose voice will count in the face of myriad intrusions by the executive branch. A coalition of Democratic attorneys general are working to make sure voters across the political spectrum have their say.
Led by the attorneys general of Washington, California, Massachusetts and Nevada, 24 states sued to block President Donald Trump’s US Postal Service plot to interfere with voting by mail. Last month, the supreme court upheld our lower court victories and blocked the administration’s unconstitutional power grab, at least for this election.
The law says states decide who receives a mail ballot. The USPS has never had the final say and, according to the American Postal Workers Union, until this year had never in its 250-year history tried to put such arbitrary restrictions on what mail it will deliver.
The case we brought was an important victory in every state, and particularly Washington, where more than 99% of voters cast their ballot by mail. States such as Colorado, Hawaii and Oregon have similarly high mail voting rates. But mail voting is not confined to blue states; it is widely used in red states as well, particularly those like Nebraska and the Dakotas, with large rural populations. It’s also the president’s preferred way to cast his own ballot.
The case of the postal service is just part of the multi-pronged federal attack states are pushing back against. The administration has abandoned the federal government’s traditional role of supporting election security and defending voting rights, work I participated in first-hand as a US attorney.
Recall, in 2020, Trump’s own administration – and particularly the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency – worked to protect the vote and defend the election. Then, efforts to misuse the Department of Justice were thwarted, and Trump relied on insurrectionists to do his bidding. In return for serving honorably, many public servants were sent packing upon Trump’s return to office, and the convicted insurrectionists were pardoned.
Now we have a US solicitor general who described the postal service’s attempt to deprive the rights of millions of eligible voters as only a “modest” use of federal authority.
The Trump administration is not known for its discretion or consistency. While the administration was in court purportedly concerned about election integrity, the president publicly demanded his supporters “cheat like hell” in midterm voting. I don’t think Republican voters want that any more than Democrats do.
We don’t doubt the administration will continue its lawless blitz against voters. Democratic state attorneys general are prepared, and have undertaken the largest multi-state effort to protect the vote in modern American history.
Recent rulings keep state elections on track and show the law is on our side. If Trump attempts to intimidate or discourage eligible voters, or to obstruct the counting of votes or certification of the election, Democratic state attorneys general will take swift action. States have decades of experience countering these threats when lodged by private actors, and they are just as illegal when attempted by the federal government.
Voters can do their part by exercising the right to elect their representatives. The president’s scheming benefits from public doubt and uncertainty. Democracy depends on the participation of its citizens, and every eligible voter should have the opportunity to render a verdict on their elected representatives.
That verdict is unlikely to favor President Trump, who ran on lowering costs, preserving peace, and economic stability, but instead delivered higher prices, hollowed out critical public services, engaged in unprecedented self-dealing, and began a globally destabilizing war with no end in sight.
Presidents don’t decide elections. State attorneys general and the millions of eligible voters we represent will exercise our constitutional powers to help keep it that way.

| Peter,

But a rebellion is brewing in the Bayou.
A catastrophic vulnerability has been found in MAGA's death star, and we are about to blow it wide open. Trump's approval rating in the state is underwater. Voters are fed up with the foreign wars, an economy on the brink of collapse, and National Guard and ICE storm troopers patrolling our own streets.

body:
| |

Peter, three people with strong habeas cases are sitting in ICE detention right now, and every hour we wait is another chance for them to disappear... Here's the situation: All three are facing deportation. None of them has a lawyer. If ICE moves them to another facility or puts them on a deportation flight before an attorney can file a habeas claim on their behalf, their families may not even know where they've gone. That's why United for Democracy is joining forces with the Workers Circle this week. **Together, we need to raise $15,000 immediately to get all three attorneys who will file habeas cases.** [**Will you fight back against the deportation regime by making a $10, $25, or even $50 donation to the Freedom Advocates program?**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqsxp_UfjJJh6k2tGWsUPGeq_9XS4uVu_8Y0--Q7Kh9rPo3Oic7rlLJEsKIvSNydauaVub0f5r4wrD_Y0vg3RxXxJ1QMTNMMKbLdBPhex1AjavrdNmI01rpXZeFX_Xd9DvMsxDsICNYTLQqJCAdhdTnbmt8LMBIA8PyOjhSBmCBYUnIfvl-aKUqZk3mEb92Ov4QiEHgqv_MqIYsuarwwvrDXApskiGSRweAfyHQ4aHOuj9dCzb0J4Xp5HoB7LTy6ONT4u62LzrDSQrl0EWOWHMEEWm3-HLTsgg-MUhrB2lEdB4STDYSvq51AxVP8zYpyAO2NEpaAwPAUw3qkUhfUUI4q6evshvfCPxammhzpEtsm_X1mLZvJo3MRxQ3y0im53eg/4up/uM43H4DQRtGUJC2OPblGrw/h0/h001.C91FqEzGVqaiABM6rOfBKIP8Hd3tgX7wLnD7AL7lLcs) _Last month, with no announcement, ICE quietly stopped listing people with final deportation orders in its online detainee locator._ That's the database families and lawyers rely on to find someone in custody. More than 16,000 people in ICE detention are now missing from it. Lawyers search for their clients and come up empty. Families call facility after facility. Meanwhile, ICE moves people from one detention center to another, and deports people, often with no warning at all.**Immigration lawyers say that for someone with a final order, even a few hours can make the difference between being deported and getting a judge to step in.** This is serious enough that last week, human rights groups asked the United Nations panel that investigates enforced disappearances to intervene. DHS insists it isn't disappearing anyone. But when the government hides where it's holding people and rushes to deport them before anyone can find them, what else would you call it? ICE is counting on one thing, Peter: that no one will come looking in time. A lawyer changes that. It's much harder to disappear someone who has legal representation. An attorney knows the person's name and where they're being held, and has the standing to go before a federal judge. **A habeas petition forces the government to justify why it's holding someone.** While the case is heard, an attorney can ask the court for an emergency stay to stop a deportation. Freedom Advocates grew out of the relationships the Workers Circle built at the 47 consecutive weeks of freedom vigils outside Alligator Alcatraz that shut down that detention camp permanently. clean_body: | | Peter, three people with strong habeas cases are sitting in ICE detention right now, and every hour we wait is another chance for them to disappear... Here's the situation: All three are facing deportation. None of them has a lawyer. If ICE moves them to another facility or puts them on a deportation flight before an attorney can file a habeas claim on their behalf, their families may not even know where they've gone. That's why United for Democracy is joining forces with the Workers Circle this week. Together, we need to raise $15,000 immediately to get all three attorneys who will file habeas cases. Last month, with no announcement, ICE quietly stopped listing people with final deportation orders in its online detainee locator. That's the database families and lawyers rely on to find someone in custody. More than 16,000 people in ICE detention are now missing from it. Lawyers search for their clients and come up empty. Families call facility after facility. Meanwhile, ICE moves people from one detention center to another, and deports people, often with no warning at all.Immigration lawyers say that for someone with a final order, even a few hours can make the difference between being deported and getting a judge to step in. This is serious enough that last week, human rights groups asked the United Nations panel that investigates enforced disappearances to intervene. DHS insists it isn't disappearing anyone. But when the government hides where it's holding people and rushes to deport them before anyone can find them, what else would you call it? ICE is counting on one thing, Peter: that no one will come looking in time. A lawyer changes that. It's much harder to disappear someone who has legal representation. An attorney knows the person's name and where they're being held, and has the standing to go before a federal judge. A habeas petition forces the government to justify why it's holding someone. While the case is heard, an attorney can ask the court for an emergency stay to stop a deportation. Freedom Advocates grew out of the relationships the Workers Circle built at the 47 consecutive weeks of freedom vigils outside Alligator Alcatraz that shut down that detention camp permanently. Now, with immigration attorneys working at greatly reduced rates, we're reaching people in ICE detention centers across the country who have final orders, no lawyer, and no money. None of us can stop ICE's machine alone. But our two organizations and thousands of people giving together can put three attorneys in front of three people this week. That's three people ICE can no longer quietly erase. ** If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your secure donation will go through immediately, with 100% going directly to The Workers Circle | | | | | | | | | | ** In solidarity, Noelle Damico The Workers Circle Paid for by United for Democracy. | | Sent via . Fellow Conservative: What's with liberals and our children? Every election cycle, Democrats tell us they're moderates. They talk about faith, decency, and "bringing people together." Then you look at the record, and you find the same thing again and again: when it comes to protecting kids, they look the other way. You've likely heard about **James Talarico** , the liberal candidate for U.S. Senate in Texas. He's a former seminarian who quotes Scripture on the campaign trail, but despite his attempts to wrap himself in Christianity, _**he voted against a bill to protect our children from sex-change surgeries, puberty blockers, and cross-sex hormones**_. So much for believing that we're all made in the image of God. Talarico even refused to oppose a bill banning sexual performances in front of minors, saying he didn't want any legislation to target the performers. He's more concerned about protecting drag queens than children in Texas. Now consider **Adam Hamilton** , the liberal candidate for U.S. Senate in Kansas. He's the founding pastor of one of the largest churches in America, and he wants Kansans to see him as a shepherd. But in November 2005, teenage boys at his church's sleep-away retreat reported that a man came into their cabin at night and touched them in their sleeping bags. A Kansas appeals court later found that camp leaders "were dismissive of their claims." The church ran its own internal review instead of calling the police. **_The next fall, the church sent the man back to the camp as a counselor._** The man was later convicted of sexual battery. Boys from Hamilton's church camp had to relive what happened to them on the witness stand. Hamilton now says he "absolutely" should have handled it differently.

Last month, Donald Trump issued an executive order renaming Lake Ontario "Lake America." Let's pause here for a moment to let the absurdity sink in.
In the middle of an escalating trade war with one of our closest allies, the President of the United States decided the best use of his power was renaming a lake.
Ontario's premier had already dismissed this idea as rhetoric when Trump first floated it, but now Trump is trying to make it official policy. And it's just the latest example of a hostile action that has nothing to offer our economy or American families - it's just about Trump picking an unnecessary fight. Here in Nevada, we're feeling the consequences of that fight firsthand.
Canada is Nevada's second-largest export market, with Nevada exporting $1.6 billion of goods to Canada every year, and is the top source of international tourism to Nevada. Since Trump began his wholly unnecessary trade war with Canada, Nevada has seen a decline in Canadian tourists. Now, with Canada's retaliatory tariffs kicking in, Nevada exporters and small businesses are bracing for another hit they don't deserve.
None of this would've happened had it not been for Trump's ill-conceived trade war and disrespectful, inflammatory rhetoric, such as calling Canada the "51st state."
This is why I introduced a resolution denouncing Donald Trump's hostile actions towards Canada. My resolution calls for the removal of Trump's new 50 percent tariffs on Canada and demands that the President stop taking inflammatory actions that needlessly harm the U.S. relationship with Canada. I want every senator on the record: Trump's reckless actions are having real, negative consequences on our economy.
I've said it before, and I'll keep saying it: Trump needs to end this trade war and start repairing our relationship with Canada and so many other countries, so we can get Nevada's economy back on track. The hardworking people of Nevada deserve a President who treats our allies respectfully - _like allies_ - not one who picks fights without considering on-the-ground impact.
The best way we can stop Trump and start this repair is by flipping the Senate blue this November. It's time to take away Trump's rubber stamp on his agenda and put a huge check on his administration. But the only way we'll have a shot at that is if everyone does their part. And that starts here, friend: **[Can I count on you to pitch $5 or more now to make sure Democrats have what it takes to fight back against Trump's mega-donors and take back the Senate?](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/18b12a36-9aa6-4ebb-967f-5d3b4df8fb23?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
Thanks for reading and for standing with me as I keep fighting for Nevada families.
Jacky
* * *

##### `Now, I'm proud to fight tirelessly in the Senate to deliver progress for hardworking families like mine in Nevada and across our country. But with Donald Trump in the White House and Republicans in control of both houses of Congress, I need your grassroots support to keep up the fights that matter most.`

**Boysko Bulletin:****Speak Out at Friday’s SCC NOVA Public Hearing for the Proposed NextEra - Dominion Merger **
---
Dear Peter, Many of you have written to me with concerns about the proposed NextEra - Dominion merger in northern Virginia. There was also frustration because in person public comment was initially limited to Richmond. As I requested in a letter to the SCC, there is now a hearing scheduled for this Friday in NOVA. Please take this opportunity to share your questions and concerns regarding the merger. You do not need to sign up in advance. **Date and time:** Friday, October 9 from 6 pm until 8 pm **Location:** Fairfax County Government Center’s Board Auditorium, 12000 Government Center Parkway, Fairfax, Virginia 22035 The Virginia State Corporation Commission (SCC) has the authority to approve or block the merger if it determines the deal does not benefit or if it harms Virginia ratepayers. The SCC is in the process of conducting a robust examination of the proposal. Dominion Energy and NextEra Energy filed their [merger application](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/140988992/652167010/-1792758890?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDI2MjQiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiOTdkYWNlYTctNmFjMy1mMTExLWJmNWItMDAwZDNhNGZiZTgzIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=4EdRV76zkv4mokjF0Af26wPFdkBHVYTGfgO7pk2X0kY=&emci=05baa668-67c3-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbe83&emdi=97dacea7-6ac3-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbe83&ceid=22486556) with the SCC on July 15, 2026. Thousands of questions are expected to be asked to fully vet the public’s interest during the process. Dominion will be required to answer all of them. The SCC has assigned this proposed merger Case Number PUR-2026-00112 and the public comment period is taking place from July 21, 2026 to November 9, 2026. **I encourage you to use your voice to express your concerns.** Additional opportunities to use your power to submit a comment include speaking via telephone on November 5, 9 and 10. You must[ register to submit a telephone comment ](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/140988993/652167011/1541000673?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDI2MjQiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiOTdkYWNlYTctNmFjMy1mMTExLWJmNWItMDAwZDNhNGZiZTgzIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=4EdRV76zkv4mokjF0Af26wPFdkBHVYTGfgO7pk2X0kY=&emci=05baa668-67c3-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbe83&emdi=97dacea7-6ac3-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbe83&ceid=22486556)by November 2. The registration form requires that you select a date - then you must be available to receive the call to provide your comment. The in person hearing at the SCC building in Richmond will be held on November 5. clean_body: | | | | Boysko Bulletin:Speak Out at Friday’s SCC NOVA Public Hearing for the Proposed NextEra - Dominion Merger Dear Peter, Many of you have written to me with concerns about the proposed NextEra - Dominion merger in northern Virginia. There was also frustration because in person public comment was initially limited to Richmond. As I requested in a letter to the SCC, there is now a hearing scheduled for this Friday in NOVA. Please take this opportunity to share your questions and concerns regarding the merger. You do not need to sign up in advance. Date and time: Friday, October 9 from 6 pm until 8 pm Location: Fairfax County Government Center’s Board Auditorium, 12000 Government Center Parkway, Fairfax, Virginia 22035 The Virginia State Corporation Commission (SCC) has the authority to approve or block the merger if it determines the deal does not benefit or if it harms Virginia ratepayers. The SCC is in the process of conducting a robust examination of the proposal. Dominion Energy and NextEra Energy filed their with the SCC on July 15, 2026. Thousands of questions are expected to be asked to fully vet the public’s interest during the process. Dominion will be required to answer all of them. The SCC has assigned this proposed merger Case Number PUR-2026-00112 and the public comment period is taking place from July 21, 2026 to November 9, 2026. I encourage you to use your voice to express your concerns. Additional opportunities to use your power to submit a comment include speaking via telephone on November 5, 9 and 10. You must November 2. The registration form requires that you select a date - then you must be available to receive the call to provide your comment. The in person hearing at the SCC building in Richmond will be held on November 5. You can also through November 9. An evidentiary hearing is scheduled to begin November 17 at the SCC building in Richmond. More information can be found on the . Kindest regards, Jennifer B. * * *
James Talarico might be able to flip a Texas Senate seat Republicans have held for 65 years by warping Christianity.
The Senate race between Republican candidate Ken Paxton and the Democrat, Talarico, has become one of the most high profile in the nation. The race may be on track to become the most expensive non-presidential campaign of all time, as it has already cost $442 million a month before election day. The PACs pouring money into the election have resorted to buying national ad slots as opposed to multiple local slots to save money. As a result, Texas Senate campaign ads have been popping up on broadcasts nationwide, particularly **[during NFL and college football games.](https://substack.com/redirect/225f203e-f085-4c64-9d76-8d2a5c97c275?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

@AdImpact_Pol
Three races this cycle, #TXSen , #OHSen , and #CAGov already rank among the 10 most expensive non-presidential races on record. Do you think #TXSen 2026 ($442M) will surpass #OHSen 2024 ($543M)?
| 9:16 PM * Oct 5, 2026 * 6.36K Views3 Replies * 9 Reposts * 43 Likes
---](https://substack.com/redirect/7edad77d-f12a-4974-9030-77b7f5dbe30b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
About 67% of Texans identify as Christian. Talarico has proved to be a fire contender in the race due to his pastoral persona, which has given him a stealthy way to appeal to the overwhelming Christian voting bloc. **[Evangelicals For A Better Future](https://substack.com/redirect/a932bcd3-9ebe-42ba-becc-c4596f02e38f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** , an evangelical Christian super PAC, not only endorsed Talarico, but spent over $1 million supporting his campaign. Talarico has embedded himself into several church communities, including his home church, St. Andrew's Presbyterian near Austin.
However, Talarico's views are far more progressive than they are traditionally Christian. He has been defending transgenderism **[since 2021](https://substack.com/redirect/e3f09573-510e-4dbd-9e8c-bf9bbfb10fba?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** , when he advocated for allowing biological males to use girls restrooms and locker rooms. clean_body: A hot mic caught the GOP’s panic. | | Peter, Looks like the Texas GOP panic runs even deeper than we thought. A hot mic caught Ken Paxton at a private donor event in Washington, answering whether or not Trump was dragging them down. "It dropped our numbers. Everybody's numbers dropped. Right now, yeah, not good." That was his review of Trump's midterm vanity rally, the Dallas convention built to rescue Texas Republicans. It 's a shocking statement because Ken Paxton is telling the truth for once. He even admitted that he's completely lost control of his own campaign and that Washington has taken it over. CNN found that Democrats have stretched the generic ballot lead by at least two points since Trump's Texas spectacle, and a Fox News poll now shows James Talarico leading the Senate race outright. The event built to save Texas Republicans is burying them. And look at what the chaos the GOP are running from has done to your life. Gas pushing $4.50 because Trump's war closed the shipping lanes. Grocery bills climbing while his raids gut the beef industry. Our armed forces were humiliated and put in danger because Trump handed the Pentagon to a TV host who purges four-star officers and hides our war dead. Through every bit of it, Keith Self tweeted that Trump is the best president in American history and pushed legislation to codify his executive orders into permanent law. Anyone like Keith Self still championing one-man rule by a president this erratic and unmoored from reality should not be trusted with any decision bigger than lunch, let alone the responsibilities of a congressman. The national political forecast looks good for Democrats right now, but we are taking none of it for granted. A wave that crests in a Fox News poll in October still has to land on November 3, and waves do not knock doors. People do. Our team has outworked Keith Self for over a year, through triple-digit heat and every stunt he pulled. These final 26 days will be our hardest push yet. Everything is breaking our way at once. body:
We’re not backing down. And we’re not leaving our neighbors behind.
#
Peter,
Today, Donald Trump went on an unhinged social media tirade against our Somali neighbors, trashed Minnesota, and told people to “fight back” against members of their own communities.
**What the hell is wrong with this guy?**
You’d think the president of the United States would have more important things to do than spend his afternoon trying to turn Americans against each other.
Look, I know what he’s trying to do. But his deranged posts can’t distract from the fact that he’s losing a war and driving up costs. He’s lashing out at blue states because he can’t land a punch on America’s actual enemies.
Trump took a few shots at me, too. Fine. I’ve heard worse. But I won’t sit quietly while he stirs up hate against Minnesotans to distract from his own failures.
**To our Somali neighbors: You are valued. You belong here. And we’re going to stand with you.**
I’m proud of Minnesota. I’m proud of our people. And I’m sick of this guy tearing down our state when he ought to be doing his job.
This November, we’re going to hold him and his MAGA allies accountable at the ballot box. That means taking back the House and electing leaders with the backbone to stand up to him. People who will defend their neighbors and get to work for working families.

It means we're receiving support beyond this district now, at a national level, because this race has become exactly what we always believed it could be: genuinely competitive, in a seat nobody expected to be in play.

I’m Blake Gendebien, a dairy farmer from right here in the North Country, and people all over the country are betting on us to win a seat that’s been solidly Republican for over a decade.

Peter, did you see
this?

[ https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-em-20261008.Z9YEKp&refcode=em20261008-6813&amount=3&t=1002&akid=6813%2E420207%2EpdP1Eo ]POLITICO logo

[ https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-em-20261008.Z9YEKp&refcode=em20261008-6813&amount=3&t=1003&akid=6813%2E420207%2EpdP1Eo ]News headline: "Sam Altman to Decoded 'The world should accept some bad
things happening' for the benefits of AI"

Over the past few years, we’ve seen massive data centers dropped in
neighborhoods across the country, driving up water and energy costs for
people who live there.

We’ve seen AI models break free of testing and controls and act recklessly
on their own accord.

We’ve seen tragic and preventable loss of life due to horrible advice that
users have received from AI.

And yet, Big Tech and wealthy CEOs are putting profits above people yet
again.

Sam Altman, CEO of OpenAI, recently told Politico “we believe that the
world should accept some bad things happening for the benefits of this
technology.” This point of view holds no regard or remorse for anyone who
has been negatively impacted by the rapid advancement of AI.

As you may know, I recently introduced a new framework to rein in AI
companies. We must pass new regulations to keep them in line, hold these
greedy Big Tech companies accountable, and prevent them from further
encroaching on people's livelihoods.

Rather than continuing to let AI companies self-regulate, this framework
will ensure there are no negative effects as a result of advancing AI
technologies. When humanity is on the line, there is no time to take
chances.

two. In a deep blue state, a slow fundraising day isn’t the end of the
world — and it almost certainly won’t decide the outcome of an election.

But here in Pennsylvania?
